FIRST THEOREM FAMILY FORMALIZED —181/186/188
Impartial post-formalization review remains pending, as requested after all
intended families are formalized. The recoded-XOR and two-stage-helper families are also complete. Three
intended families remain unfinished; paid-padding support is in progress.

1. graph_expected_separator_bound / strategy_expected_separator_bound:
   E length(M) >= P - E L - 2D - 2H(Z),
   P=n^2 b, D=P-log2|F|, L=nb|S|+b sum_C |C|^2.
Inputs are uniform on any nonempty finite correct family F. A deterministic
helper selects a public strategy; each charged bit is an arbitrary nonlinear
function of at most two original rows. Query supports and stopping are public
functions of the helper/history. Each receiver decodes its column from its
own raw row, helper and complete transcript. Termination is required only on
F. S may depend on (helper,completed transcript); C are the actual components
of that transcript's interaction graph after deleting S. Compatibility,
rectangularity, entropy and volume/Kraft budgets are proved, not assumed.

2. graph_worst_case_separator_bound / strategy_worst_case_separator_bound:
   B >= P-L*-2(D+g),
if all runs on F have length<=B and loss<=L*, and at most2^g helper values
are actually attained on F. No termination assumption outside F is needed.

3. Separate sharpness of both coefficients2, for d=2 and every b>0:
   - Symmetric off-diagonal entries: |F|=2^(3b), D=b, constant helper,
     no transcript, P=4b and L=2b.
   - Full cube: |F|=2^(4b), D=0, helper X01 XOR X10 has exactly2^b
     attained values and entropy b bits, no transcript, L=2b.
Actual codes, decoding, cardinalities, entropies and c>=2 implications are
checked in SeparatorSharpness. The helper entropy equality uses the already
independently proved expected bound plus the direct alphabet upper bound;
this is acyclic and does not enter the proof of that bound.

4. average_treewidth_lower_bound (AdaptiveTreewidth.lean):
For n,b>0, if expected cost <=(1-epsilon)P, set eta=(D+H(Z))/P. Then
   E treewidth(G_(Z,M)) >= (n/4) max(epsilon-2eta,0)^2 - 1.
This STRENGTHENS the written188 consequence
   E treewidth >= (n/9) max(epsilon-1/n-2eta,0)^2 - 1.
Thus fixed positive expected savings with D+H(Z)=o(P) force average treewidth
Omega(n), for every b>=1. Treewidth is the minimum width of an ordinary finite
tree decomposition: vertex/edge coverage and connected occurrence subtrees.
No fragmentation condition is built into its definition. Empty graphs use
natural-valued treewidth0; the coding corollary explicitly assumes n>0.

WHY THE CONSTANT IMPROVED
WeightedTree.lean proves: for any finite tree with nonnegative integral node
weights and any threshold L>=0, there is a set U with
   (L+1)|U| <= totalWeight,
and every component left after deleting U has weight<=L. Leaf induction
removes an overweight leaf or transfers a light leaf's weight to its unique
neighbor. WeightedLeaf checks label masses and separator counts in both cases.
Assign each graph vertex to one containing decomposition bag. Running
intersection ensures each surviving graph component maps to one surviving
tree component. With bags of size<=h this gives
   (L+1)|S| <= hn, max_C |C| <= L.
The old written estimate was |S|<=2hn/L. A global integer threshold and direct
quadratic optimization give the new1/4 constant without Jensen or rounding
loss. These are standard graph/optimization ingredients; no priority claim.

LEAF INEQUALITY AND SUPPORTING PROOFS
RowCode.separator_leaf_bound proves
   2 log |A| <= log |R| + (b sum_C |C|^2) log2.
A is any nonempty correlated correct subfamily on one helper/transcript/
separator assignment. R is the full virtual transcript fiber with separator
rows fixed, without helper-consistency or correctness requirements elsewhere.
Individual column recovery, rather than a joint decoder, is used.
Other checked support includes shared matrix encoding/transpose, finite
entropy/Gibbs/Shearer and two-cover inequalities, exact adaptive transcript
factorization, prefix/Kraft bounds, actual leaf budgets and finite-family
truncation preserving all charged runs.

SECOND THEOREM FAMILY FORMALIZED —181B
Scope: fixed row graph; exactly nb transformed bits per row under an arbitrary
bijection (possibly nonlinear); each fixed packet is a singleton transformed
coordinate or XOR of two in equal/adjacent rows. All raw inputs must decode
from own raw row plus full broadcast. No helper, adaptive supports, redundant
features or high-entropy-family generalization is silently included.

Let P=n^2 b and Q_ell count raw bit coordinates with row/column connected by
a walk of length<ell. Disconnected pairs are never near (Mathlib's natural
valued distance alone would incorrectly classify them). Then
   B >= P-(P+ell Q_ell)/(ell+1).
Unanchored variable components can flip independently. Their flips preserve
far raw coordinates at EVERY basepoint, so arbitrary compositions also do.
The resulting free orbit injects into the near coordinates. No nonlinear raw
fiber is asserted to be a linear subspace.

For n>=2 and maximum degree<=Delta:
   B >= P-6 log(max(2,Delta)) P/log n.
This proves the written one-sided P-O_Delta(P/log n) with an explicit constant.
For paths, cycles, or any row graph injecting by a graph homomorphism into a
cycle (allowing arbitrary relabeling), n>0:
   P <= B+bn(3 floor(sqrt(n))+1),
   B >= P-4bn sqrt(n).
These prove the written O(b n^(3/2)) error with explicit constants.

THIRD THEOREM FAMILY FORMALIZED —216
TwoStageRows defines exactly the architecture
  D_final o G o Pi o L o F o C.
C is rowwise with an optional input permutation, F has arbitrary nonlinear
own-row bijective updates in a public triangular order, L is rowwise bijective,
Pi is a row permutation, G is arbitrary causal triangular in another order,
and D_final is rowwise with an output permutation. C,G,D_final may all lose
information. All maps and both orders may depend on the one global helper.
There are no extra banks, dense middle maps or source-dependent private orders.

TriangularRows.block_injective proves conditional block injectivity from
those explicit own-row updates. Global bijectivity follows from finite
injectivity; it is not an additional unproved property of a candidate.
The inverse block property and final suffix support are then derived.

For P=n^2 b, any correct family F and any integer0<=r<=n:
  |F| * 2^(br(n-r)) <= |h(F)| * 2^P.
In particular (quarter_count_toll):
  |F| * 2^(b floor(n^2/4)) <= |h(F)| * 2^P.
This finite form allows empty F and an arbitrary ambient helper type.
For nonempty F, D=P-log2|F| and |h(F)|<=2^g imply
  D+g >= b floor(n^2/4).
quarter_helper_bound_of_density also proves the manuscript formulation with
any real upper deficit D satisfying |F|>=2^(P-D). No rounding loss.

The proof records complementary intermediate rows and the raw R-by-J
rectangle. Correctness fixes the rest of each queried original row. Block
injectivity then recovers the intermediate state and hence the whole input.
This gives a finite injection, not an entropy-independence assumption.
The fixed-support sandwich lemma is enough for the exact requested theorem;
the optional general adaptive-query wrapper extension216.2/216.5 is NOT
silently claimed as formalized. No asymptotic strengthening of216.4 is claimed.

Relevance: this rules out the exact two-stage repair with o(P) helper bits
and o(P) correct-family deficit. It does not normalize arbitrary tape
algorithms to this architecture or improve the unrestricted transpose bound.

PAID-PADDING SUPPORT CHECKED —201/202, FULL FAMILY UNFINISHED
PaddingChords imports the first paper's current/previous-distinct resident
pair, pairRes and IsChord. NestedExcursion specifies an actual local walk:
4Kr-step rise starting at a from zr, a nested middle above the peak, and
4Kr-step fall starting at c, with c>=a+7Kr. For each0<=j<=4K-2:
  u=a+(j+2)r, w=c+(4K-j-1)r+1,
  x=floor((u-1)/r), y=floor(w/r), beta=z+j.
The proof derives residency at u-1,w, absence throughout[u,w), and x+1<y.
Thus (x,y,beta) is an actual imported pair-residency chord. Distinct beta
values give4K-1 distinct counted chords when endpoint labels differ.
Both full endpoint slots lie inside[a,a+6Kr) and[c,c+6Kr), respectively,
hence inside their seven-phase gadgets. No time-grid alignment is assumed.
The local conditions allow arbitrary earlier/later motion; they do not
by themselves construct the entire uniform excursion machine.

GadgetLabels reuses original label_change_between. For disjoint contiguous
slot windows, bad/nonconstant windows inject into actual labelChanges.
If each window has>=L slots and each slot-label class has<=m slots, every
good window-label class has size satisfying L*size<=m. Labels can oscillate
at every slot and depend on size. fullSlots uses the actual time-zero grid:
a physical interval of length Lr has at least L-1 complete global r-slots.

GLOBAL202 CONDITIONAL THEOREM CHECKED
ExpanderCutCount derives eta*v/2-q*|bad| good crossing edges from vertex
expansion, the maximum degree and repaired label fibers of size<=v/2.
RepairedGadgetLabels gives each bad gadget a fresh label and uses full-slot
counts to bound every good class. No pre-assumed cut count is used.
ExcursionLayout specifies disjoint7Kr gadget windows, their actual local
nested ramps, edge pages and separated spatial slabs. It does not postulate
chords: native chord properties and endpoint labels are derived from those
walk conditions. A page/block-address injection prevents global duplication.
Hence C >= (4K-1)*F, with C the actual sum of native crossChords and F the
number of good crossing edges, for arbitrary finite slot labelings.

With M=labelChanges and A=4K-1, F>=eta*v/2-q*M and C>=A*F imply
  3k*M+C >= 2v
under A*eta>=4 and 3k*eta>=4q. The weighted proof adds
eta*C>=4F and 3k*eta*M>=4q*M. This improves BOTH sufficient thresholds
from8 in the written two-case proof to4, with no division by q or A.
If n<=2v, v>=2 and n*entryBits(n)<=r*cellBits, it yields exactly
  CutIneq n cellBits r T 0 0 h,
including all finite labelings and both numerical slacks zero.
The layout/expansion hypotheses remain explicit. This is not the full
unconditional uniform paid-machine theorem, nor a sufficiency test for
transposition. No computational correctness or lower bound is inferred.

EXPLICIT WALKS AND CONDITIONAL FULL MSTAR CHECKED
ExcursionPulse uses min((t-a) dotminus,L), cast to integer after natural
subtraction, and subtracts the corresponding closing ramp. Summing these
pulses on each page defines the entire head walk. NestedPulseSchedule proves
at most one pulse changes per step, hence unit steps; outer pulses contribute
depth*L, the selected pulse supplies the exact ramp, and inner pulses remain
nonnegative during the middle. Zero start and eventual reset are derived.

NestedMatchingPages requires graph endpoints, their forward vertex order
and strictly nested same-page pairs. At start(i)=offset+7Kr*i, a4Kr ramp
starts after Kr waiting steps. Base(e)=4K*depth(e); strict depth ranks give
disjoint spatial slabs. It constructs every ExcursionLayout field, parks
page heads at0 through offset, and resets them at H=offset+7Kr*v.
H is the forward page-motion horizon, not total native setup/cleanup cost.

ExcursionTransfer injects pages into more tapes and retains the local
witnesses whenever those page walks agree through H. Later motion/horizon
and other tapes are arbitrary. cutIneq_after gives the literal zero-slack
CutIneq under the fixed expansion/degree/threshold conditions. This is
trajectory preservation, not yet a native machine composition/cost theorem.

CanonicalExcursion proves n/2<=v=4floor(n/4)<=n for n>=4 and imports original
blockSize ceiling bounds. Stationary extra tapes are explicit; fixed K/extra
choices exist for eta>0. H<=offset+7K*P, hence H<=(a+7K)P if offset<=aP.
Every geometric obligation is derived from the given finite expanding graph.

ExpandingPageFamily is an EXPLICIT HYPOTHESIS, not an existence theorem or
uniform generator. For such a family with sizes tending to infinity,
macrostar applies original theoremMStar_walk: convergent subsequences exist,
and EVERY subsequential limit is1-Lipschitz, obeys full star for the allowed
finite excisions and labels, satisfies excess/range bounds, and cannot have
all heads globally monotone. Original definitions and limit proof reused.

MONOTONE OVERLAP GRAPH AND PAGE COMPILER CHECKED
ResidueMatchingInput records a finite edge set with a map tag, no strict
inversions within each tag, and row/column endpoint spans less than M.
The explicit color(tag,i mod M,j mod M) lies in Fin(c*M^2). Equal residues
inside a span<M force equal endpoints, so each color is a matching; distinct
same-color edges have strictly increasing endpoints. This uses span bounds,
not a claim that degree bounds alone justify the chosen residue coloring.

OrderedBipartite constructs a simple graph from those actual finite edges
on the order A_0,...,A_(n-1),B_(n-1),...,B_0. Its edge equivalence proves
no lost/added edges. Reversal converts monotone matchings to nested pages.
MatchingPageDegree proves incidence edges inject into page labels and hence
maximum degree<=number of pages for every NestedMatchingPages value.

BoundedMonotoneMap specifies a domain, strict monotonicity and common integer
forward/inverse Lipschitz bound B. An overlap is a real witness in the domain
and the INTERIORS of both grid cells. Monotonicity gives no inversions;
scaled Lipschitz inequalities give row/column spans<B+1. These lemmas permit
arbitrary domains; equivalence to a positive-length interval overlap or to
rational endpoint tests is not silently assumed.

For a fixed family of c such maps, overlapEdges is a finite simple edge set.
Every duplicate is kept once and assigned the least witnessing map tag.
overlapPages constructs c(B+1)^2 nested matching pages, with a corresponding
degree bound independent of n. This feeds the checked page-walk construction.
The real-existential overlap predicate is not yet a native decision algorithm.
No expansion, unconditional expander existence or runtime follows just from
these bounded-monotone hypotheses.

CONTINUOUS EXPANSION TO CANONICAL PADDING CHECKED
BipartiteExpansionCount and BipartiteVertexExpansion prove: on two classes
of size2h, if every subset of either class of size<=h has at least
(1+epsilon) times as many neighbors, then every vertex set of size<=2h
has at least (epsilon/2) times as many OUTSIDE neighbors in the actual
ordered simple graph. Left/right class images are disjoint; their cardinal
partition and adjacency equivalence are proved, not assumed.

GridCellMeasure gives exactly |A|/n Lebesgue mass for the union of the
selected open cells. Cells are measurable/disjoint and lie in[0,1]. The
finite grid-boundary set has zero measure; every other point in[0,1] lies
in a cell. This explicitly removes the endpoint ambiguity.

OverlapExpansion covers forward images by right-neighbor cells plus that
finite boundary, and restricted preimages by left-neighbor cells plus the
boundary. Outer-measure monotonicity suffices for these upper bounds; no
unproved image-measurability assumption is introduced. Continuous expansion
on measurable sets of mass<=1/2 gives the literal discrete neighbor bound.

SymmetricOverlap constructs the restricted inverse of each bounded monotone
map and proves it has the SAME forward/inverse bound B. Its overlap relation
is exactly the transposed relation. Adjoining all inverses makes both-side
expansion follow from ONE forward continuous expansion hypothesis. The
symmetrized fixed c-map family has (2c)(B+1)^2 nested pages and degree bound,
independent of n. The inverse is currently defined by classical choice;
this is not an exact-arithmetic implementation claim.

ContinuouslyExpandingMaps remains an EXPLICIT INPUT, not a proved existence
theorem. Given such an input, canonicalPages constructs the expanding graph
at v=4floor(n/4) for every n>=4, with eta=epsilon/2. pageFamily supplies the
existing ExpandingPageFamily interface without sparse-size/dummy-vertex
assumptions. exists_canonical_cut_walks chooses fixed K/extra tapes and gives
the exact original zero-slack CutIneq at every size. The existing paths,
linear horizon and imported macrostar theorem apply to that same family.
No uniform generator or native machine is inferred from these real-valued
noncomputable definitions. Unconditional existence and all paid execution
obligations remain required for the full201/202 family.

EXACT RATIONAL OVERLAP AND BOUNDED ENUMERATION CHECKED
RationalMobius uses f(x)=(a*x+b)/(c*x+d) with rational coefficients and
rational lo<hi, positive determinant delta=a*d-b*c, and positive denominator
at both closed endpoints. The computational domain is the OPEN interval
(lo,hi). Positivity throughout the closure, continuity, strict increase and
the exact difference identity are derived.

Let L=min(c*lo+d,c*hi+d), U=max(c*lo+d,c*hi+d). The executable integer
  B=ceil(max(delta/L^2,U^2/delta))
bounds both |f(x)-f(y)|/|x-y| and its reciprocal on the closed interval.
RationalMobius.bounded therefore supplies the earlier BoundedMonotoneMap
interface with a proved, size-independent constant. This includes affine
maps with positive slope; no arbitrary singular/disconnected domain claim.

IntervalOverlap and RationalOverlapTest use
  l=max(lo,i/n), u=min(hi,(i+1)/n).
The executable test is exactly
  l<u and max(f(l),j/n)<min(f(u),(j+1)/n),
with EVERY comparison and evaluation performed in the rationals. It is
proved equivalent to the original real-witness overlap and to strictly
positive Lebesgue length of f((lo,hi) intersect cell_i) intersect cell_j.
Endpoint-only contacts yield no edge. All domain/nondegeneracy hypotheses
are explicit; this is not an equivalence for arbitrary BoundedMonotoneMap
values whose domains may be irregular.

RationalNeighbors evaluates s=floor_nat(n*f(l)), forms only the B+1 integer
candidates s,...,s+B, discards those outside Fin n, then applies that test.
Every genuine target neighbor belongs to this range, and mem_neighbors
proves exactness for every n,i,j. The floor_nat convention also handles
negative image endpoints. Candidate cardinality<=B+1 is proved.

RationalInverse constructs (d*y-b)/(-c*y+a) on (f(lo),f(hi)), with rational
endpoints/coefficients. It proves all structural requirements, actual inverse
composition and exact reversal of overlap. The same neighbor algorithm on
this explicit inverse gives all incoming neighbors, bounded by B_inv+1.
It replaces classical choice for this concrete rational map class.

RationalFamilyGraph takes the maximum B over a fixed finite c-map family,
proves its outgoing rows have<=c(B+1) neighbors, and builds a row-by-row
edge stream of length<=n*c(B+1). Each bounded row is sorted; distinct source
rows cannot duplicate an edge. The stream is proved Nodup and its finite
set equals the old real overlapEdges exactly. It does not scan the n-by-n
Cartesian square or perform global duplicate removal. The auxiliary finite
set union is only a convenient specification; no cost bound is inferred
from its implementation.

RationalSymmetricGraph adjoins the explicit rational inverses and proves
its computed edge set/stream represent exactly the symmetrized graph used
in the expansion transfer. Thus the epsilon/2 vertex expansion conclusion
applies to the computed graph GIVEN the original continuous expansion input.
No expanding coefficient family is asserted to exist by these lemmas.

Compiled evaluation succeeded for identity on(0,1),2x on(0,1/2), and
x/(1+x) on(0,1), at n=8. Their outgoing/incoming lists agree with exact
interval intersections and are mutual transposes. Source/output preserved
in verification/rational-evaluation.json. These are execution smoke checks;
the kernel statements establish all-size correctness. Neither finite counts
nor successful execution prove bit complexity or a native tape-time bound.

EXECUTABLE PAGE RECORDS AND LOCAL NATIVE MOTION CHECKED
RationalPageColor tests the fixed map family, chooses the least witnessing
map tag and computes the explicit residue color(tag,i mod(B+1),j mod(B+1)).
Those choices equal the old overlapTag/overlapColoring exactly, including
absence of a color when no edge exists. No graph-wide search is introduced.

PageOpcode and BipartitePageEvents derive source/target events from the
actual edge equivalence. Matching uniqueness proves at most one event on
each page/vertex and excludes simultaneous opening and closing. The forward
A order and reversed B order are the same as the earlier page construction.
RationalPageOpcode uses only bounded outgoing/incoming lists and rational
color tests to compute open/close/idle; rationalPageOpcode_eq proves exact
agreement with those graph events at every vertex and page.

PageOpcodeWalk regroups the edge-pulse sum by its endpoints; no expanding
or nonempty graph assumption is needed. OpcodeRamp proves for any record
array, R>=0, and elapsed0<=s<=7R within vertex i's block:
  h(start_i+s)-h(start_i) = direction(op_i)*min(s dotminus R,4R).
Earlier records are constant and later ones have not begun. Here start_i is
offset+7Ri and the cast to integer occurs after natural subtraction.
At s=7R the displacement is4R times the opcode direction.

RecordMotion uses the original Transpose.Dir and Dir.shift, not a new
movement convention. It defines sequential execution that stays for R
steps, moves for4R steps, then stays for2R. recordRun_eq and
opcodeRampWalk_recordRun prove equality at EVERY within-record step, from
any starting position. This is a semantic specification: R, the opcode and
elapsed phase are externally supplied, and the clock/fetch implementation
still must be represented and charged in one fixed finite-state TM.

RationalOpcodeWalk materializes a List.Vector of2n records, each a
List.Vector of k=c(B+1)^2 three-symbol opcodes. The flattened tape has
exactly2nk symbols. rationalOpcodeWalk_eq identifies the resulting path with
the previous nested-page walk for R=Kr; reset follows at offset+7Kr(2n).
The temporary function-valued stream was removed in favor of these actual
lists. No cost claim follows merely from this linear stored length.

Executable checks of the combined identity/doubling/fractional map family
at n=0,...,8 agree on opening/closing/distinct-edge counts. At n=0,...,6,
R=2 and offset3, every page/vertex/internal step agrees between sequential
Dir.shift execution and the pulse walk, with final position0. The n=4
identity table explicitly exhibits reversed closing order. Exact source
and output: verification/opcode-evaluation.json. All-size correctness comes
from the kernel theorems; these checks do not prove native time or expansion.

RATIONAL SIZES AND INTEGER-ONLY GENERATION CHECKED
RationalHeight defines H(q)=max(|q.num|,q.den), for the canonical positive
denominator. Rat.num_den_mk proves reduction cannot enlarge numerator or
denominator bounds. H(q+r)<=2H(q)H(r), H(qr),H(q/r)<=H(q)H(r), and
H(1/q)=H(q), including q=0. A polynomial bound H(q)<=C(n+1)^d gives each
numerator-magnitude/denominator bit size<=size(C)+d*size(n+1)+1. Signed
encoding needs its one additional sign bit. This is a size theorem only.

RationalOpcodeSize sets C=1+sum of the six fixed coefficient/endpoint heights.
The source endpoints have height<=C(n+1); evaluated endpoints have the general
bound4C^6(n+1)^2. The neighbor-start argument and range endpoint have explicit
cubic bounds, hence logarithmic bit sizes. These broad bounds remain valid
for empty clipped source cells and totalized zero denominators.

IntegerMobius clears the four coefficient denominators once, with a positive
scale L and integer coefficients A,B,C,D. For q!=0, evaluation at p/q equals
  (A*p+B*q)/(C*p+D*q),
including zero output denominator under the existing totalized convention.
The integer forms have linear magnitude in max(|p|,|q|). Image denominator
positivity is proved when q>0 and p/q lies in the original closed domain.

IntegerEndpoints chooses the clipped left/right fractions with integer
cross-comparisons against the fixed rational endpoints. Both input
denominators are positive; pair values equal sourceLeft/sourceRight exactly.
Their integer images equal evalQ at those endpoints. No reduction to a
canonical rational is needed to compute these pairs.

IntegerOverlap uses exactly three integer inequalities: source nonempty,
left image below the target cell's upper endpoint, and target lower endpoint
below the right image. Source nonemptiness places BOTH endpoints in the
valid domain, gives positive image denominators, and supplies strict image
order. Hence integerOverlapTest_spec proves equivalence to the old real
witness overlap for every grid/source/target. Empty cells cannot be accepted,
even if their otherwise unused image denominator is zero or negative.

Let M=1+|A|+|B|+|C|+|D| and E=M*arithmeticConstant. IntegerOperandSize proves each unreduced
endpoint and image component has magnitude<=E(n+1). This also strengthens
the canonical evaluated-endpoint height to<=E(n+1). The six products used
in the three overlap inequalities have magnitude<=E^2(n+1)^2, and each has
binary magnitude size<=size(E^2)+2*size(n+1)+1. Constants depend only on F.

IntegerNeighbors rejects empty clipped source cells first. On an open cell,
  start=toNat((n*imageNumerator)/imageDenominator)
uses signed integer division with positive denominator and is proved equal
to the previous rational natural floor. It checks at most B+1 consecutive
candidates using the integer overlap test. integerNeighbors_eq proves exact
agreement with the earlier rational neighbor set at EVERY cell; its range
may differ before filtering on empty cells. Integer division here is an
executable reference operation, not a unit-cost native instruction.

Seven maps at n=0,...,24: all34300 source/target tests agree, all2100 endpoint
pairs/images agree, and all2100 outgoing neighbor sets agree with the earlier

That pole case explicitly produces raw zero/negative image denominators at

A direct read of the archive VariableDivisionFamily/VariableDivisionExecution
shows unary conversion and a128*(value numerator+value denominator+1) bound.
This cannot justify polynomial-in-BIT-LENGTH arithmetic. The separate
MicroBinaryDivisionFamily keeps a fixed divisor d in its finite control;
that does not supply a uniform divider when d depends on n. No such runtime
claim was imported. A native binary implementation, or bounded binary search
using binary arithmetic, is required. The required absolute-coordinate model bridge is now checked below;
this does not repair the unsuitable arithmetic runtime bounds.

NATIVE MODEL AND FINITE MICROCODE COMPILER CHECKED —R1696
AbsoluteTape represents an absolute work cell at z by relativeTape.nth(z-p).
Its write/move lemmas retain p explicitly and prove every native cell update.
RelativeMachine uses the SAME original finite delta table and proves exact
step/stepN representation, ComputesWithin equivalence, frozen-run equality
and original absolute head trajectories. No simulation slowdown appears.

NativeMicrocode imports only our own earlier CopyMachine/OperationalTrace/
Microcode base. The three local support sources are portable snapshots with
source and destination hashes in archive-source-provenance.json; one unused
section parameter was removed from rename_run. The first paper remains a
DIRECT import and its original directory is untouched.

The compiler assigns blank/start/stop/data0/data1 to Fin5, encodes the fixed
ports and labels, and implements read, act and jump by one original TM delta
transition apiece. Read/jump rewrite the scanned symbol and stay; act writes
its optional symbol and moves each work head by at most one. Halt and reject
both halt, with distinct encoded final control states. The finite program
itself never reads/moves the input head or emits output.

Located configurations retain absolute positions alongside actual tapes.
step_denote and native_trajectory prove exact native execution/positions.
run_core agrees with the prior relative-tape semantics. actual_result_transfers
moves an existing relative result to the original native state and every
cell relative to the ACTUAL final head, retaining input position/output.
It does NOT conclude that final heads reset from relative-tape equality.
Active traces give original partial stepN; computations that have halted
cannot be counted as extra executed instructions. Stopping by n microsteps
implies the native ComputesWithin bound. A fixed finite enumeration maps
any chosen initial label to zero, with no input-size-dependent control.

These are implementation/refinement theorems, not an arithmetic algorithm or
proof that the padding generator runs in linear time. Initial loading,
physical clock/fetch, binary arithmetic, resets, cleanup and payload remain.
A further archive check found SubtractFamily.all_inputs bounds
256*(value aw+value bw+1): that routine is also unsuitable for bit-polynomial
arithmetic. Neither its cost nor the unary division cost is imported.

BINARY COMPARISON AND ADDITIVE GENERATOR PLAN CHECKED —R1697
NativeZipper lifts the older zipper semantics while carrying actual absolute
head positions. run_denote, trace_of_run and stopped_subroutine transfer
located execution and active traces to original native stepN. Prepared input
tapes are explicit; no input-loader cost is supplied by this lemma.

IMPORTANT BUDGET SIMPLIFICATION
A fast arbitrary divider is unnecessary for201/202. LinearGenerationBudget
imports original le_two_pow_entryBits and proves
  size(n+1)<=entryBits(n)+2,
  n(n+1)(A+B*size(n+1))<=2(A+3B)*inputLength(n), n>=1.
Thus O(n) records can each use O(n) arithmetic operations of bit-linear cost.
Repeated addition can form products of O(n)-magnitude operands within that
budget. Old unary subtraction/division on O(n^2) values still do NOT fit:
their value-linear bounds can cost O(n^2) per record instead of O(n log n).

CappedAdditiveDivision defines a reference state(q,trial), initially(0,d).
If trial<=a, update(q+1,trial+d); otherwise retain it. For signed a and d>0,
after n steps the exact state is(q,(q+1)d), q=min(n,toNat(a/d)). It uses no
variable division at runtime. repeatedAdd x n=n*x supplies multiplication
by n using the same kind of bounded addition loop. Physical loop fuel,
binary addition and signed encoding still have to be implemented and paid.

AdditiveNeighbors replaces the old floor by this capped quotient. A start
at or above n admits no candidate below n; clipping to n therefore preserves
the entire bounded candidate set. Empty clipped source cells are guarded
first. All outgoing neighbor sets equal the earlier exact rational/integer
ones, including negative images and quotients larger than the grid size.
At every intermediate t<=n, the positive trial has magnitude-bit size at most
  E.size+2*(n+1).size+1, E=integerOperandConstant fixed for the map.
The candidate count remains<=B+1. These are exact algorithm/operand/budget
proofs; this reference loop is not yet the required native generator.

NATIVE SHARED CARRY ARITHMETIC AND CALLER EMBEDDING CHECKED
BinaryCarryData uses the existing little-endian value definition. One Boolean
carry recurrence with optional complement of the second operand proves, for
all equal m-bit words (empty and padded allowed), result length m and
  value(result)+2^m*carryOut = value(xs)+value(transformed ys)+carryIn.
Addition uses uncomplemented ys and initial carry0. Subtraction complements ys
and uses initial carry1, giving result+2^m*carryOut+value(ys)=value(xs)+2^m.
The subtraction carry is true exactly when value(ys)<=value(xs); nonnegative
subtraction and no-overflow addition therefore have their literal Nat values.

PHYSICAL COUNTER, PAID LOOPS AND REUSABLE BUFFER CHECKED
ZipperLocation resolves the absolute-position gap without redoing old execution
proofs. Located says pos=origin+length(left). SafeLeft requires a nonempty
represented left list whenever the next instruction moves left. Action/step/

condition is essential: moving left into implicit blanks would otherwise
break that length formula. NativeCounter and NativeBuffer prove their actual
boundary invariants. Blank-buffer initialization uses a direct two-step

controller. Every m-bit word has an exact zipper run of2*stepCost transitions;

NativeBuffer reuses the archived erasure, then executes two marker-preparation

R1758 — TRANSLATION GAIN AND CELL UNIFORMITY
In progress. R1758 proves the first analytic reduction of continuous expansion for the actual augmented rational family. An explicit expansion-or-uniformity dichotomy follows. No half-measure restriction is required for this intermediate reduction. R1759 — CENTRAL TRIMMING AND ACTUAL SQUARED-INTEGRAL PROJECTION ERROR
In progress. R1759 discharges cell trimming and its actual squared-integral projection error. EXACT STATEMENTS

The first/last-m specialization has r=2m and central support [m/K,1-m/K]. Cell-centered functions have zero integral on each cell.

R1760 — EXACT VARIANCE AND NORMALIZED L2 SPECTRAL INPUT
In progress. R1760 completes the normalized analytic input for the trimmed cell-centered function. CellCenteredVariance proves membership in every finite or infinite Lp exponent, exact squared integral M_prime-K*sum_i(m_i_prime^2), a lower bound from a cell-mass cap, and positive variance when 0<M<=1/2, 0<=delta<1 and theta*(1+delta)<1. It also proves the function vanishes outside the retained cells. If delta<=1/100 and theta<=1/200, its variance is at least (49/100)*M, and the squared-integral error from global centering is at most one hundredth of this variance. CellCenteredSpectralInput constructs the actual real L2 equivalence class, identifies its norm square with the variance integral, normalizes it, proves its representative has zero integral on every grid cell, and proves almost-everywhere support in the retained cells and hence the central interval for central trimming. The final spectral-input theorem identifies the normalized function explicitly with this trimmed indicator. These are formal analytic prerequisites; no spectral-gap or rational-generator-existence result is assumed or claimed.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let K>0, A be measurable in [0,1], M=volume(A)<=1/2, and let T be A restricted to selected cells B. Write M_prime=volume(T), m_i_prime=volume(T intersect cell_i), and theta=card(complement B)/K. Under |K*volume(A intersect cell_i)-M|<=delta*M, the actual function F=1_T-sum_i(K*m_i_prime)*1_cell_i satisfies integral(F^2)=M_prime-K*sum_i(m_i_prime^2), and this is at least (1-(1+delta)*M)*M_prime. It is positive when M>0, 0<=delta<1 and theta*(1+delta)<1. Under the stronger bounds 0<=delta<=1/100 and theta<=1/200, integral(F^2)>=(49/100)*M and integral((H-F)^2)<=(1/100)*integral(F^2), where H=1_T-M_prime*1_[0,1]. The actual L2 class u of F has norm squared equal to integral(F^2). Its normalized class has norm one under positive variance, zero cell integrals, and vanishes almost everywhere outside the retained cells. Central trimming therefore gives support in [m/K,1-m/K].

PROOF AND REUSE

The prior explicit projection-error estimate, including its theta term for deleted cells, supplies the one-percent relative bound. Mathlib L2 inner products and normalization identify the actual equivalence class and transfer support and zero cell integrals through almost-everywhere equality. The construction is not an arbitrary existential test function.

R1761 — NEAR-IDENTITY MOBIUS CALCULUS AND ACTUAL CHANGE OF VARIABLES
In progress. R1761 completes quantitative near-identity Mobius control and reuses Mathlib for actual change of variables. MobiusCalculus proves the derivative formula, its positivity and continuity, measurable images, the real image-measure integral formula, and the exact squared-integral identity for the square-root-Jacobian weighted pullback on measurable subsets of the existing rational interval. It proves both inverse compositions on the unit interval, the reciprocal derivative identity, and the unit-restricted preimage/inverse-image equality under its explicit domain hypothesis. NearIdentityMobius bounds coefficients entrywise by eta, transfers the condition to the adjugate inverse, and derives it from squared coefficient distance at most eta^2. For eta<=1/8 and x in [0,1], the denominator lies between 1-2eta and 1+2eta, displacement is at most 8eta, and derivative and square-root-derivative errors are at most 32eta. These imply actual image-measure distortion between factors 1-32eta and 1+32eta. A central interval [r,1-r] with r>=8eta lies in the clipped domain and maps into [0,1], for the map and its inverse. The corresponding preimage identity is proved. These local identities do not by themselves establish a unitary L2 representation, almost-invariance, the spectral gap, or generator existence.

EXACT STATEMENTS
For the existing positive-determinant rational Mobius data, let phi(x)=(a*x+b)/(c*x+d), q(x)=c*x+d, Delta=a*d-b*c and D(x)=Delta/q(x)^2. On the certified closed interval, HasDerivAt phi D(x) is proved, as are measurable images and integral_image(g)=integral_domain(D*(g composed with phi)). In particular, volume.real(phi(A))=integral_A D, and integral_A((sqrt(D)*(f composed with phi))^2)=integral_phi(A)(f^2). These are actual Lebesgue/Bochner integrals, not formal scalar substitutes. For unit-interval data, both adjugate inverse compositions are proved at every point of [0,1], together with D_inverse(phi(x))*D(x)=1.

If |a-1|, |b|, |c| and |d-1| are each at most eta<=1/8, then 1-2eta<=q(x)<=1+2eta, |Delta-1|<=3eta, |phi(x)-x|<=8eta, |D(x)-1|<=32eta and |sqrt(D(x))-1|<=32eta on [0,1]. Thus (1-32eta)*volume(A)<=volume(phi(A))<=(1+32eta)*volume(A) for measurable A in [0,1]. If r>=8eta, [r,1-r] is contained in the clipped domain and maps into [0,1]. R1762 — SMALL EXPANSION TO ACTUAL WEIGHTED INDICATOR ERROR
In progress. R1762 converts small augmented-family expansion into actual unweighted and Jacobian-weighted indicator error. SmallExpansionSymmDiff proves a finite-measure common-cover inequality, inclusion of each generator/inverse image in the actual augmented cover, and the symmetric-difference bound B=2*sigma*M+2*(M-M_prime)+32*eta*M_prime for the centrally trimmed set T. It substitutes the existing trimming loss to give an explicit bound in sigma, delta, eta and m/K. IndicatorPullbackError proves the pointwise indicator/symmetric-difference identity, integrability of the square, and the exact unit-interval integral as the measure of the inverse-map image symmetric difference. Both generator and inverse corollaries are proved. WeightedIndicatorError proves measurability and a pointwise square-root-Jacobian error estimate, derives integrability of the actual weighted error before comparing integrals, and bounds its unit-interval energy by 2*(1+32*eta)*B+2*(32*eta)^2*M_prime. The central-trim corollary replaces B by C*M, where C=2*sigma+4*m/K*(1+delta)+32*eta, and M_prime by M. This proves almost-invariance of the uncentered trimmed indicator locally on [0,1]; global centering and the normalized spectral input remain separate obligations.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let M=volume(A), T be a measurable subset of A in [r,1-r], M_prime=volume(T), and eta<=1/8 bound each coefficient error of a selected generator. Assume r>=8eta and the actual augmented image cover has volume at most (1+sigma)*M. R1765 — GLOBAL REAL MOBIUS REPRESENTATION AND L2 GAP INTERFACE
In progress. R1765 formalizes the real fractional-linear action of actual SL(2,R) matrices. It proves inverse/product identities away from the pole, finite exceptional sets, measurability, positive Jacobian off the pole, and global change of variables and integrability equivalence. The weighted pullback W_g(f)(x)=|c*x+d|^(-1)*f((a*x+b)/(c*x+d)) preserves squared integrals and respects almost-everywhere equality. It descends to a linear isometric equivalence of the actual L2 quotient. T_g=W_(g inverse) is packaged as a group homomorphism into linear isometric equivalences, with norm, inverse, composition and inner-product laws proved. Determinant-one rational maps and their square-root-Jacobian action agree exactly with this global construction. Their finite symmetric average is a continuous linear contraction and is symmetric for the real inner product. The actual L2 restricted-gap premise implies the function-form premise from R1764, and hence the proved continuous expansion bound. Neither gap existence nor strong continuity in the matrix parameter is asserted.

EXACT STATEMENTS
For g in the actual Mathlib SL(2,R), write phi_g(x)=(a*x+b)/(c*x+d), D_g={x:c*x+d!=0}, and J_g(x)=1/(c*x+d)^2. The complement of D_g is finite (empty or a singleton), phi_g maps D_g bijectively onto D_(g inverse), and phi_(g inverse)(phi_g(x))=x on D_g. The Jacobian theorem gives integral_R(J_g*(f composed with phi_g))=integral_R(f), together with the corresponding integrability equivalence. The possible pole is removed only as a proved null set.

Define W_g f=|c*x+d|^(-1)*(f composed with phi_g). Its squared integral equals that of f, and squared integrability is equivalent. If f=h almost everywhere, then W_g f=W_g h almost everywhere; this is proved using the zero squared integral of their difference, before defining any quotient action. W_(g*h)f=W_h(W_g f) almost everywhere. On actual L2 classes, the induced pullback is linear, norm preserving and inverse to the pullback by g inverse. Defining T_g=W_(g inverse) gives T_(g*h)=T_g T_h, T_1=id, and preservation of the real inner product. unitaryRepresentation is an actual group homomorphism into real linear isometric equivalences; no continuity in the group parameter is part of this statement.

For a nonempty finite tuple G of such matrices, A_G=(1/(2*card G))*sum_g(T_g+T_(g inverse)) is a continuous linear operator satisfying norm(A_G f)<=norm(f), and inner(A_G f,h)=inner(f,A_G h). For determinant-one RationalUnitMobius data F, the embedding into SL2 commutes with inverse and agrees pointwise with the existing rational evaluation, Jacobian and weighted pullback, including their totalized values at a pole. For L2 representatives supported in [0,1] almost everywhere, the inner product of the average with f equals the earlier symmetricCorrelation F f.

RestrictedL2Gap(G,K) quantifies over the actual L2 quotient: norm(f)=1, support in [0,1] almost everywhere, and zero integrals on every closed grid cell imply inner(A_G f,f)<1/2. This is a named premise, not a proved existence claim. It implies RestrictedCorrelationGap(F,K), with the representative normalization, support and cell integrals checked. For c>0, K>=10000, determinant-one rational F and entrywise near-identity error eta<=1/1000000, this premise therefore yields the R1764 expansion factor 1+1/(100*K^2) for the actual augmented restricted family.

R1766 — CLASSICAL FOURIER CANCELLATION AND CORRELATION STABILITY
In progress. R1766 proves cancellation against tests with bounded cell oscillation, the explicit classical Fourier estimate |Ff(xi)| <= (2*pi*|xi|/K)*||f||_1, and the unit-support inequality ||f||_1^2 <= integral ||f||^2. For normalized real L2 representatives supported in [0,1] with zero closed-grid-cell means, the classical low-frequency squared integral on [-R,R] is at most 8*pi^2*R^3/K^2. A threshold uniform over these functions makes this at most 1/256. Separately, every real Hilbert-space linear contraction satisfies |<Tf,f>-<Tg,g>| <= ||f-g||*(||f||+||g||). If ||f||=1, ||f-g||<=1/16 and <Tf,f>>=1/2, then <Tg,g>>=95/256. This applies to the actual Mobius average. The identification of the classical integral with Mathlib's L2 Fourier transform and the actual high-frequency decomposition are still unproved here.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let K>0, let f:R->C be integrable and supported in [0,1] almost everywhere, and assume its integral on each open grid cell (i/K,(i+1)/K) is zero. If f*phi is integrable and ||phi(x)-a_i||<=B on each cell, then |integral f*phi|<=B*integral ||f||. For a test satisfying ||phi(x)-phi(y)||<=L|x-y| with L>=0, the bound is (L/K)*||f||_1. The finite set of cell endpoints has proved zero measure; the sum over cells equals the global integral.

With Mathlib's classical Fourier convention Ff(xi)=integral f(x)*exp(-2*pi*i*x*xi), the estimate is |Ff(xi)|<=(2*pi*|xi|/K)*||f||_1. For R>=0, integral_[-R,R]|Ff|^2 <= (8*pi^2*R^3/K^2)*||f||_1^2. Every unit-supported L2 function is L1 and satisfies ||f||_1^2<=integral ||f||^2, proved by integrating the nonnegative variance of ||f|| on the unit interval. Thus the squared norm factor is at most one for normalized inputs.

For the actual RealMobius.RealL2 quotient representative f, ||f||=1, almost-everywhere unit support and zero means on each CLOSED grid cell imply integral_[-R,R]|F(ofReal f)|^2<=8*pi^2*R^3/K^2. In particular it is <=1/256 if 2048*pi^2*R^3<=K^2. For each fixed R>=0 a positive natural threshold K0 exists such that this conclusion holds for all K>=K0 and all such f. This is a classical Fourier integral statement, not yet a statement about the L2 Fourier projection.

For any real Hilbert space and continuous linear contraction T, |<Tf,f>-<Tg,g>|<=||f-g||*(||f||+||g||). If ||f||=1 and ||f-g||<=delta, the bound is delta*(2+delta). If delta=1/16 and <Tf,f>>=1/2, then <Tg,g>>=95/256, strictly above 1/4. No symmetry hypothesis is needed for this stability estimate. The actual nonempty finite Mobius average satisfies the contraction premise and receives a direct corollary. No high-frequency g is constructed by this theorem.

R1767 — L2 FOURIER BRIDGE AND ACTUAL HIGH-FREQUENCY WITNESS
In progress. R1767 proves that the classical Fourier integral and Mathlib's L2 Fourier transform agree almost everywhere for every L1-intersection-L2 input, using equality against smooth compactly supported tests and the tempered-distribution compatibility theorem. Actual low/high-frequency L2 components are constructed, with exact Fourier representative formulas, norm contraction, and an exact low-component energy identity. Real and imaginary part maps reuse the existing real Mobius action: its complexification preserves contraction and symmetry, agrees with the real action on embedded real inputs, and each group action has the expected complex weighted-pullback formula almost everywhere. For a normalized unit-supported real L2 input with zero K-cell means, 2048*pi^2*R^3<=K^2 makes the low component norm <=1/16. If original average correlation is >=1/2, the complementary component g has norm <=1, no Fourier mass on [-R,R], distance <=1/16 from the original complexified input, and real-inner-product correlation >=95/256>1/4. This is an explicit sharp-cutoff high-frequency reduction; smooth Littlewood-Paley band isolation and the spectral-gap contradiction remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS
For f in actual complex L2(R) which is also L1, the representative of Mathlib's L2 Fourier transform agrees almost everywhere with the classical integral Ff(xi)=integral f(x) exp(-2*pi*i*x*xi). The proof compares both sides against smooth compactly supported real tests, using a Schwartz embedding, Fourier/Fubini, the L2-to-tempered-distribution compatibility theorem, and uniqueness of locally integrable functions from their test integrals. The corresponding toLp theorem handles raw L1-intersection-L2 functions without assuming representative identities.

For any measurable frequency set S, define low_S f=F_inverse(1_S Ff) and high_S f=f-low_S f in the actual complex L2 quotient. Their Fourier representatives are respectively 1_S Ff and 1_(S complement) Ff almost everywhere. Both components have norm at most ||f||, low+high=f, and ||f-high||=||low||. The exact identity ||low||^2=integral_S |Ff|^2 holds for the L2 Fourier representative, and also for the classical transform when f is L1.

The continuous real-linear maps ofRealL2, realPartL2 and imagPartL2 act on L2 quotient representatives almost everywhere as their names specify. The embedding ofRealL2 preserves norm and real inner product; the squared norm and real inner product of a complex L2 function split into the corresponding real/imaginary contributions. For any real L2 operator T, define T_C f=ofReal(T(Re f))+i*ofReal(T(Im f)). If T is a contraction, T_C is a contraction; if T is symmetric for the real inner product, so is T_C. It agrees with T on embedded real inputs and preserves their quadratic correlation. For an actual SL2 group action, T_C has precisely the complex weighted-pullback formula |c*x+d|^(-1)f(phi(x)), with inverse matrix convention and almost-everywhere transport proved.

Let G be a nonempty finite tuple of actual SL2(R) matrices, T its symmetric average, K>0, R>=0, and f a real L2 class with norm 1, support in [0,1] almost everywhere, and zero integrals on all CLOSED K-grid cells. If 2048*pi^2*R^3<=K^2 and <Tf,f>>=1/2, then the actual g=high_[-R,R](ofRealL2 f) has ||g||<=1, Fourier transform zero on [-R,R] almost everywhere, ||ofRealL2 f-g||<=1/16, and <T_C g,g>_real>=95/256>1/4. No near-identity, freeness or spectral-gap premise is required for this reduction. Its sharp cutoff is not identified with the source's smooth Littlewood-Paley decomposition.

R1768 — WEIGHTED DERIVATIVES, SPATIAL MOMENTS AND GLOBAL SMOOTHNESS
In progress. R1768 proves the exact differential expression D_g u(y)=(a-c*y)^2*u'(y)-c*(a-c*y)*u(y) for the weighted pullback W_g u(x)=|c*x+d|^(-1)*u((a*x+b)/(c*x+d)). Away from the possible pole, (W_g u)'=W_g(D_g u); the almost-everywhere identity gives exact derivative-energy transport. An explicit four-moment estimate is proved with coefficients 16*a^4, 16*c^4, 4*c^2*a^2 and 4*c^4. All even polynomial L2 moments of Schwartz inputs and their derivatives are integrable, and D_g preserves Schwartz space. Cubic decay proves derivative zero at the pole, closing the jump/singularity issue. Hence W_g u is globally C-infinity for every Schwartz input, its nth derivative is W_g(D_g^n u), and every derivative is in L2 with exact energy equality. The complex pullback is identified with the existing complexified actual group action using its inverse convention. Uniform scale-dependent moment bounds for actual smooth band pieces, band isolation and the restricted spectral gap remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let g=[[a,b],[c,d]] be any actual matrix in SL2(R), and let E be a real normed vector space. Define W_g u(x)=|c*x+d|^(-1) scalar-multiplied by u((a*x+b)/(c*x+d)), with the value zero at a denominator zero. If u is differentiable everywhere, define D_g u(y)=(a-c*y)^2*u'(y)-c*(a-c*y)*u(y). The classical derivative of W_g u is W_g(D_g u) away from the possible pole, hence almost everywhere. Change of variables gives integral ||(W_g u)'||^2 = integral ||D_g u||^2, and the corresponding square-integrability equivalence. These general identities do not alone assert a weak derivative across the pole.

For any u,du and every y, the polynomial expression (a-c*y)^2*du(y)-c*(a-c*y)*u(y) has squared norm at most 16*a^4*||du(y)||^2 +16*c^4*y^4*||du(y)||^2 +4*c^2*a^2*||u(y)||^2 +4*c^4*y^2*||u(y)||^2. The integrated bound is proved under the explicit integrability hypotheses. For a Schwartz function u, every even moment integral y^(2k)*||u(y)||^2 and y^(2k)*||u'(y)||^2 is finite; D_g u is itself a Schwartz function, so all hypotheses of the derivative-energy bound are discharged.

If |y|^3*||u(y)||<=B for all y and |a*x+b|>=eta>0, then ||W_g u(x)||<=B/eta^3*|c*x+d|^2. At any pole p, the determinant identity makes a*p+b nonzero and c*x+d=c*(x-p). The local quadratic estimate therefore proves HasDerivAt (W_g u) 0 p. Applying this to Schwartz functions makes the derivative identity global, with (W_g u)'=W_g(D_g u) at every point. Induction proves W_g u is globally C-infinity and (d/dx)^n W_g u=W_g(D_g^n u), where D_g is iterated on Schwartz space. For every n, the derivative has finite squared-norm integral and exact energy integral ||(d/dx)^n W_g u||^2=integral ||D_g^n u||^2. This does not claim W_g u itself is Schwartz.

For actual complex L2 classes, the existing complexified operator for g inverse has representative W_g f almost everywhere. Thus the new calculus concerns the same action used by the high-frequency witness, not a replacement action. No gap, generator, near-identity or uniform band-bound assumption is used in these calculus results.

R1769 — WEAK L2 FOURIER DERIVATIVES AND SEPARATED-FREQUENCY CORRELATION
In progress. R1769 proves integration by parts against Schwartz tests for functions and derivatives in L2 without an L1 assumption. A weak derivative represented by an L2 class gives the actual Fourier representative identity F(df)(xi)=2*pi*i*xi*F(f)(xi), exact derivative energy, and integrability of the weighted Fourier energy. The actual high-frequency component satisfies (2*pi*R)||P_high f||<=||df|| for R>=0 and the divided bound for R>0. These results are connected to the existing complexified Mobius action on Schwartz inputs, with null-set transport proved for arbitrary real normed target spaces. Iterated transported derivatives have the expected Fourier powers. The high-frequency energy is bounded by the four explicit spatial moments from R1768. Low-frequency orthogonality gives |<W_g u,h>_real|<=||D_g u||_2*||h||_2/(2*pi*R) whenever Fh vanishes on [-R,R]. Smooth band construction, square-summed moment estimates and band isolation remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let f,df be actual complex L2(R) classes. Suppose integral phi(x)*df(x) = -integral phi'(x)*f(x) for every complex Schwartz test phi. Then F(df)(xi)=2*pi*i*xi*F(f)(xi) almost everywhere for Mathlib's L2 Fourier transform. The weighted energy is integrable and integral (2*pi*xi)^2*|F(f)(xi)|^2 = ||df||_2^2. If raw functions u,du have HasDerivAt u (du(x)) at every x and both are in L2, the required weak pairing is proved automatically by integration by parts for integrable products. Neither u nor du is required to be L1.

For R>=0, let P_high be the actual complementary Fourier projection outside [-R,R]. The estimate (2*pi*R)*||P_high f||_2<=||df||_2 and its squared form hold. For R>0 this yields ||P_high f||_2<=||df||_2/(2*pi*R). For any measurable frequency set S and h whose Fourier representative is zero on S almost everywhere, the low component is orthogonal to h for the real L2 inner product, and <f,h>_real=<P_high,S f,h>_real. Consequently, if S=[-R,R] and R>0, |<f,h>_real|<=||df||_2*||h||_2/(2*pi*R).

For any actual g=[[a,b],[c,d]] in SL2(R), schwartzActionL2 g u is exactly the existing complexification of actionCLM(g inverse) applied to u.toLp. Its representative is W_g u, with representative changes handled by a proved null-set transport theorem. For Schwartz u, its weak L2 derivative is schwartzActionL2 g (D_g u), where D_g u(y)=(a-c*y)^2*u'(y)-c*(a-c*y)*u(y). Hence F(W_g D_g^n u)=(2*pi*i*xi)^n*F(W_g u) almost everywhere for every natural n. The n=1 Fourier energy is integral ||D_g u||^2, and (2*pi*R)^2*||P_high W_g u||_2^2 is at most that energy. It is therefore at most 16*a^4*integral||u'||^2 +16*c^4*integral y^4||u'||^2 +4*c^2*a^2*integral||u||^2 +4*c^4*integral y^2||u||^2. For h with no frequencies in [-R,R], |<W_g u,h>_real|<=||D_g u||_2*||h||_2/(2*pi*R). The derivative norm here is the L2 norm of the actual Schwartz differential expression, with action isometry proved. No uniform frequency-band estimate for this norm is asserted.

R1770 — ACTUAL SMOOTH BANDS AND FINITE-FAMILY DERIVATIVE ENERGIES
In progress. R1770 proves that all polynomial moments x^n*f of a unit-supported L2 input are L1 and L2 with L2 norm at most ||f||. Its classical Fourier transform is smooth, every nth derivative is in L2, and the derivative energy is at most (2*pi)^(2n)*||f||^2. For every compactly supported Schwartz cutoff chi, chi*Ff is embedded in Schwartz space and its inverse Fourier transform is an actual Schwartz band. The band's L2 Fourier representative is exactly chi times the original L2 Fourier representative; exact energy, norm bounds and frequency-zero statements are proved. A pointwise weighted square-sum bound on cutoff values controls total band energy. First and second derivatives of the actual band spectrum satisfy explicit finite-family energy bounds in terms of square-sum constants B0,B1,B2 for cutoff values and derivatives. The constants do not depend on the number of bands. Concrete dyadic cutoffs, spatial-moment conversion, transported derivative square sums and band isolation remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let f:R->C be in L2 and zero outside [0,1] almost everywhere. For every natural n, x^n*f(x) is in L1 and L2, with L2 norm at most ||f||_2. The classical Fourier transform Ff is C-infinity. Its nth derivative is the classical transform of (-2*pi*i*x)^n*f(x), agrees almost everywhere with the corresponding actual L2 Fourier transform, belongs to L2, and has energy at most (2*pi)^(2n)*||f||_2^2.

For any compactly supported Schwartz cutoff chi, define sigma=chi*Ff as an actual Schwartz map using the proved smoothness and compact support, then define u=F_inverse(sigma) in Schwartz space. The actual L2 Fourier transform of u.toLp has representative chi*F(f.toLp) almost everywhere. Thus ||u||_2^2=integral |chi(xi)|^2*|F(f.toLp)(xi)|^2. If |chi|<=M with M>=0, then ||u||_2<=M*||f||_2; wherever chi is zero, the L2 Fourier representative is zero almost everywhere.

For a finite index set I, real weights w_i and Schwartz multipliers psi_i, if sum_i w_i*|psi_i(xi)|^2<=B at every xi, then sum_i w_i*integral |psi_i*F|^2<=B*integral |F|^2 for any L2 function F. In particular, the same pointwise hypothesis for the cutoffs gives sum_i w_i*||u_i||_2^2<=B*||f||_2^2. No family-size factor occurs. For B>=0 and F=(d/dxi)^n Ff, the right side is at most B*(2*pi)^(2n)*||f||_2^2.

Let w_i>=0, let every chi_i be compactly supported Schwartz, and suppose B0,B1,B2>=0 bound the pointwise sums sum_i w_i*|chi_i|^2, sum_i w_i*|chi_i'|^2, and sum_i w_i*|chi_i''|^2. For sigma_i=chi_i*Ff and t=2*pi, the proved bounds are sum_i w_i*||sigma_i'||_2^2 <= (2*B0*t^2+2*B1)*||f||_2^2 and sum_i w_i*||sigma_i''||_2^2 <= (3*B0*t^4+12*B1*t^2+3*B2)*||f||_2^2. The full iterated Leibniz formula for sigma_i is also proved. These estimates are uniform in the finite family size, but the cutoff square-sum hypotheses are not yet instantiated by a concrete dyadic family. They control frequency-spectrum derivatives; conversion to the specific spatial moments in D_g is the next step.

R1771 — EXACT SPATIAL MOMENTS AND FINITE-FAMILY TRANSPORT ENERGY
In progress. R1771 proves the exact Plancherel identity for every polynomial spatial moment of any complex Schwartz function, with no spatial support hypothesis. For each actual smooth band u=F_inverse(chi*Ff), its derivative is exactly the smooth band with cutoff q(xi)=2*pi*i*xi*chi(xi); q is compactly supported Schwartz. The R1770 finite-family frequency derivative estimates now give the spatial moments needed for D_g u=(a-c*x)^2*u'-c*(a-c*x)*u. Five explicit pointwise weighted square-sum bounds on chi, chi', q, q', q'' control the sum of ||D_g u_i||_2^2, with a displayed constant independent of family size. A finite-family high-frequency tail estimate permits different thresholds for different bands. Concrete dyadic cutoffs, their coefficient bounds, L2 decomposition and band isolation remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS
For any complex Schwartz function u and every natural n, write t=2*pi. The exact identities are integral |(F u)^(n)|^2 = t^(2n)*integral x^(2n)*|u(x)|^2 and integral x^(2n)*|u(x)|^2 = t^(-2n)*integral |(F u)^(n)|^2. No unit-support hypothesis is imposed on u. The Schwartz Fourier transform of u' equals q(Fu), where q(v)(xi)=i*t*xi*v(xi). The actual L2 norm of u equals its ordinary integral norm.

For original f in L2 supported in [0,1] almost everywhere and a compactly supported Schwartz cutoff chi, u=F_inverse(chi*Ff) is the R1770 actual Schwartz band. The multiplier q_chi(xi)=i*t*xi*chi(xi) is compactly supported Schwartz, and u' is exactly the actual band F_inverse(q_chi*Ff). Consequently every spatial moment of u and u' is identified with the corresponding derivative energy of chi*Ff and q_chi*Ff.

Let I be finite, w_i>=0, chi_i compactly supported Schwartz, and let B0,B1,Q0,Q1,Q2>=0 bound, at every xi, the sums sum_i w_i*|chi_i|^2, sum_i w_i*|chi_i'|^2, sum_i w_i*|q_i|^2, sum_i w_i*|q_i'|^2, sum_i w_i*|q_i''|^2, respectively, with q_i=i*t*xi*chi_i. For u_i=F_inverse(chi_i*Ff), the proved finite moment bounds are:
  sum_i w_i*||u_i'||_2^2 <= Q0*||f||_2^2;
  sum_i w_i*||x*u_i||_2^2 <= t^(-2)*(2*B0*t^2+2*B1)*||f||_2^2;
  sum_i w_i*||x^2*u_i'||_2^2 <= t^(-4)*(3*Q0*t^4+12*Q1*t^2+3*Q2)*||f||_2^2.
Together with the R1770 energy bound sum_i w_i*||u_i||_2^2 <= B0*||f||_2^2, these give, for every g in SL2(R) with a=g00 and c=g10,
  sum_i w_i*||D_g u_i||_2^2 <= C*||f||_2^2,
  D_g u(x)=(a-c*x)^2*u'(x)-c*(a-c*x)*u(x),
  C=16*a^4*Q0 + 16*c^4*t^(-4)*(3*Q0*t^4+12*Q1*t^2+3*Q2)
    +4*c^2*a^2*B0 +4*c^4*t^(-2)*(2*B0*t^2+2*B1).
C is independent of the number of bands. These are conditional coefficient bounds, not a completed concrete dyadic estimate.

For any finite Schwartz family u_i, nonnegative weights w_i, and nonnegative individual thresholds R_i, sum_i w_i*(t*R_i)^2*||high_[−R_i,R_i](W_g u_i)||_2^2 <= sum_i w_i*||D_g u_i||_2^2. This is an actual L2 Fourier-tail bound and composes directly with the displayed coefficient estimate. No claim that W_g u_i is Schwartz, or that frequency truncation preserves unit spatial support, is used.

R1772 — CONCRETE DYADIC CUTOFFS AND UNIFORM TRANSPORT ENERGY
In progress. R1772 constructs an actual compactly supported smooth cutoff rho, equal to one on [-1,1], zero outside [-2,2], and bounded in norm by one. Its dyadic differences chi_j=rho(xi/2^(j+1))-rho(xi/2^j) are actual compactly supported Schwartz functions, vanish at and outside the prescribed annular boundaries, and satisfy an exact finite telescoping identity. Closed dyadic annuli have overlap at most three, including boundary points needed for derivative supports. The five R1771 coefficient hypotheses are fully discharged. L2 convergence of the telescoping band sums and band isolation remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Choose the fixed Mathlib smooth bump with inner radius 1 and outer radius 2, and embed its complex-valued version rho in Schwartz space. Then rho(x)=1 for |x|<=1, rho(x)=0 for |x|>=2, and |rho(x)|<=1. Define D_j u(x)=u(2^(-j)*x), rho_j=D_j rho, chi_0=rho_1-rho, and chi_j=D_j chi_0. All these are actual Schwartz maps; the cutoffs are compactly supported. The exact identities D_j(D_k u)=D_(j+k)u, (D_j u)^(n)(x)=2^(-jn)*u^(n)(2^(-j)*x), chi_j=rho_(j+1)-rho_j, and sum_(j<N) chi_j=rho_N-rho are proved. chi_j vanishes for |x|<=2^j and for |x|>=2^(j+2).

For every finite set I of natural indices and every real x, at most three indices j in I satisfy 2^j<=|x|<=2^(j+2). The topological support of every iterated derivative is contained in the original topological support. Thus the closed annular support bound applies to every derivative order, including boundary points.

Write t=2*pi, q_j(x)=i*t*x*chi_j(x), w_j=2^(-2j), B_n=3*seminorm_(0,n)(chi_0)^2, and Q_n=3*seminorm_(0,n)(q_0)^2. These are fixed finite nonnegative real constants. For every finite I, every real x, and every natural n,
  sum_(j in I) w_j*|chi_j^(n)(x)|^2 <= B_n,
  sum_(j in I) w_j*|q_j^(n)(x)|^2 <= Q_n.
The second estimate uses the exact cancellation w_j*|q_j^(n)(x)|^2=|(D_j q_0)^(n)(x)|^2. The underlying unweighted square-sum estimate for dilates of any Schwartz function supported in the closed annulus 1<=|x|<=4 is also proved.

For original complex f in L2 supported in [0,1] almost everywhere, let u_j=F_inverse(chi_j*Ff) be the actual Schwartz bands. For every finite I,
  sum_(j in I) ||u_j||_2^2 <= B_0*||f||_2^2.
For every g in SL2(R), with a=g00,c=g10 and differential transport D_g u=(a-c*x)^2*u'-c*(a-c*x)*u,
  sum_(j in I) 2^(-2j)*||D_g u_j||_2^2 <= C_g*||f||_2^2,
where the verified nonnegative constant is
  C_g=16*a^4*Q_0 +16*c^4*t^(-4)*(3*Q_0*t^4+12*Q_1*t^2+3*Q_2)
      +4*c^2*a^2*B_0 +4*c^4*t^(-2)*(2*B_0*t^2+2*B_1).
This theorem has no undischarged cutoff/coefficient bounds and is uniform in both f and the finite index set. It does not assume spatial support or relative moment bounds on the individual bands.

For any nonnegative thresholds R_j on I, the concrete actual L2 Fourier-tail consequence is
  sum_(j in I) 2^(-2j)*(t*R_j)^2*||high_[−R_j,R_j](W_g u_j)||_2^2 <= C_g*||f||_2^2.
Finite cutoff telescoping is proved; the L2 limit of the band sum and the band-isolation conclusion remain outstanding.

R1774 — UNIFORM SYMMETRIC-AVERAGE BOUNDS AND NONZERO-BAND ISOLATION
In progress. R1774 assembles the exact symmetric complex average from the forward and inverse Mobius actions. Let f:R->C be in L2, zero outside [0,1] almost everywhere, and let u_j=F_inverse(chi_j*Ff) be the actual Schwartz bands already constructed, with chi_j=rho_(j+1)-rho_j. Write B0=dyadicCutoffDerivativeBound 0. Define the fixed nonnegative C_*=universalDyadicTransportConstant by replacing a^4,c^4,c^2*a^2 in the established transport constant by their upper bounds 16,16,16 for |a|,|c|<=2, and define L=(2/(2*pi))*sqrt(C_*)*sqrt(B0).

For every nonempty finite generator family G:Fin c->SL2(R) satisfying |G_i(0,0)|, |G_i(1,0)|, |G_i(1,1)| <=2, the actual complex symmetric average is
  T u = (2c)^(-1) sum_i (W_(G_i) u + W_(G_i^-1) u).
The inverse entries are (G_i^-1)(0,0)=G_i(1,1) and (G_i^-1)(1,0)=-G_i(1,0), so the same constant controls both. For arbitrary D,M>=0 and arbitrary finite sets I_r,
  sum_(r<M) sum_(j in I_r) |<T u_j,u_(j+D+r)>| <= 2^(-D)*L*||f||^2.
The reversed inner products satisfy the same estimate by symmetry. Averaging cancels the factor c; the bound is independent of c.

For every finite set I and offset d, sum_(j in I)||u_j||*||u_(j+d)|| <= B0*||f||^2. Therefore, if ||T u_j||<=r*||u_j|| for all j and r>=0, each near-offset correlation sum is at most r*B0*||f||^2. The generic finite symmetric-matrix bound is
  sum_(j,k<N) a(j,k) <= 2*sum_(d<N)sum_(j<N) a(j,j+d)
for any nonnegative symmetric a on natural-number pairs. Applying it and overcounting offsets up to D+N proves, for v_N=sum_(j<N)u_j,
  <T v_N,v_N> <= 2*(D*r*B0 + 2^(-D)*L)*||f||^2.

Choose D with 24*L<2^D and r=[24*(D+1)*(B0+1)]^(-1)>0. Then 2*(D*r*B0+2^(-D)*L)<1/3. Consequently there is a UNIVERSAL r>0 such that, for every family above and every unit-norm supported input, if some finite v_N has <T v_N,v_N>>=1/3, then some actual band u_j is nonzero and satisfies ||T u_j||>r*||u_j||. No compact-support or relative-moment assertion is made about that band.

For a real unit-norm f supported in [0,1], with zero integral on each of K closed grid cells, K>0, K^2>=16384*pi^2, and <averageOperator(G)f,f>>=1/2, R1773 supplies the finite-sum hypothesis. The same universal r therefore gives a nonzero actual complex dyadic band with the strict norm ratio above. The current theorem has j>=0; no arbitrary prescribed lower bound j>=J has yet been proved.

R1775 — JOINT HIGH-BAND ISOLATION WITH RELATIVE REGULARITY CONTROL
In progress. R1775 extends actual dyadic reconstruction to every starting level J and proves the corresponding grid correlation estimate under K^2>=16384*pi^2*2^(3J). A reusable finite correlation lemma and arbitrary band masks extend the universal norm-ratio theorem to any retained family; the old level-zero proof now reuses this more general result. Finite sums of actual bands satisfy ||sum u_j||^2<=3*sum||u_j||^2 by their bounded Fourier overlap. A concrete nonnegative regularity cost M_j, combining ||u_j||^2, ||x*u_j||^2 and 2^(-2j)*(||u_j'||^2+||x^2*u_j'||^2), has a fixed summed bound C*||f||^2. Discarding bands with M_j>R*||u_j||^2 for the fixed R=3*1024^2*(C+1) costs at most 1/1024 in L2 for every finite subfamily of a unit input. The retained sums preserve sufficient correlation, so a band j>=J is selected with u_j!=0, ||T u_j||>r*||u_j|| and M_j<=R*||u_j||^2, simultaneously. Both r and R are independent of J, the input, the grid and the bounded generator family.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let f:R->C be an L2 input supported in [0,1] almost everywhere. Let u_j be the established actual Schwartz bands with chi_j=rho_(j+1)-rho_j and v_J=F_inverse(rho_J*Ff). For every J,N>=0,
  sum_(j<N) u_(J+j) = v_(J+N)-v_J.
The sum converges in actual L2 to h_J=f-v_J. Its actual Fourier representative is (1-rho_J)*Ff, its norm is at most ||f||, and its Fourier transform vanishes on [-2^J,2^J]. Its distance from f is bounded by the sharp low-frequency projection on [-2^(J+1),2^(J+1)]. For normalized real grid inputs with zero integral on each of K closed cells and K^2>=16384*pi^2*2^(3J), this distance is <=1/16. If the original average correlation is >=1/2, h_J has correlation >=95/256 and its finite tail sums eventually have correlation >=1/3.

For an arbitrary predicate p on the band indices, retain u_j when p(j) holds and replace it by zero otherwise. The previous small-ratio correlation bound remains valid when the ratio assumption is imposed only on retained bands. Consequently there is a fixed r>0 such that positive finite retained-sum correlation >=1/3 forces some retained nonzero u_j with ||T u_j||>r*||u_j||. The same r works for every predicate, input, starting level and nonempty generator family with |g00|,|g10|,|g11|<=2. Taking p(j)=(j>=J) gives the arbitrary-high-start norm-ratio theorem.

For every finite band set I, the actual Fourier annuli overlap at most three times and
  ||sum_(j in I)u_j||^2 <= 3*sum_(j in I)||u_j||^2.
Define w_j=2^(-2j) and the concrete regularity cost
  M_j=||u_j||^2 + integral x^2*|u_j(x)|^2 dx
      +w_j*(integral |u_j'(x)|^2 dx + integral x^4*|u_j'(x)|^2 dx).
M_j>=0. Write B_n and Q_n for the existing fixed cutoff derivative bounds and t=2*pi. The fixed nonnegative constant
  C=B_0+t^(-2)*(2*B_0*t^2+2*B_1)+Q_0
      +t^(-4)*(3*Q_0*t^4+12*Q_1*t^2+3*Q_2)
satisfies sum_(j in I) M_j<=C*||f||^2 for every finite I. This cost matches the terms needed by the established quadratic Mobius differential-transport bound; it does not assert bounds for every higher spatial moment.

Set R=3*1024^2*(C+1)>0. For a unit input, every finite sum of bands failing M_j<=R*||u_j||^2 has norm <=1/1024. The same bound controls the difference between any finite retained sum and the sum obtained by retaining only its good-cost bands. A generic contraction lemma combines this with convergence to a limit within 1/16 of the original unit input: some retained finite sum still has correlation >=1/3. Its proof takes an approximant within 1/1024 of the limit and bounds total distance by 1/14, then uses the verified normalized correlation-loss inequality.

Joint selection: there is a universal r>0 such that for every prescribed J, nonempty bounded generator family as above, and real unit grid input satisfying K>0, K^2>=16384*pi^2*2^(3J), the closed-cell zero-mean conditions, unit spatial support and original correlation >=1/2, there exists j>=J with
  u_j!=0,  ||T u_j||>r*||u_j||,  M_j<=R*||u_j||^2.
The two selection properties hold for the same actual Schwartz band. r and R are independent of J, K, f, the generator values and their number within the stated class. A quantitative near-identity group-action bound is not part of this theorem.

R1776 — NORMALIZED HIGH BAND AND QUANTITATIVE LOCAL MOBIUS ACTION
In progress. R1776 promotes the actual dyadic regularity cost to arbitrary Schwartz functions, proves its quadratic homogeneity, and normalizes the jointly selected nonzero band without losing its fixed cost bound, strict average norm ratio, prescribed lower frequency level or exact Fourier annulus. A general C1 translation energy inequality needs only continuous square-integrable derivative, not integrability of the original function. The actual complex L2 Mobius action preserves norms and obeys the verified reversed product order. Translation, inversion conjugation and one fixed translated inversion give upper, lower and tilted unipotent bounds. A three-factor matrix decomposition then proves ||W_g u-u|| <= 29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta whenever Q_j(u)<=R, eta<=1/2, |g00-1|<=eta, |g01|<=eta and |g10|<=eta. No condition on g11 beyond determinant one is needed. This completes the targeted local perturbation estimate without a separate dilation-flow argument.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Write W_g u(x)=|c*x+d|^(-1)*u((a*x+b)/(c*x+d)) for g=[[a,b],[c,d]] in SL(2,R), with the already established value at a pole. The actual complex L2 operator is complexPullbackL2(g)=complexifyL2(actionCLM(g^-1)). It satisfies W_(g*h)=W_h o W_g, W_1=identity and ||W_g f||=||f|| for every actual complex L2 class. In particular ||W_(g*h)f-f||<=||W_g f-f||+||W_h f-f||, and conjugation differences reduce by exact isometry.

For any Schwartz u and j>=0, define
  Q_j(u)=||u||_2^2 + integral x^2*|u(x)|^2 dx
       +2^(-2j)*(integral |u'(x)|^2 dx + integral x^4*|u'(x)|^2 dx).
Q_j>=0 and Q_j(a*u)=a^2*Q_j(u) for real a. Its components are bounded by Q_j; the sum of the two derivative energies is <=2^(2j)*Q_j. Also integral x^2*|u'|^2 <= integral |u'|^2 + integral x^4*|u'|^2, using x^2<=1+x^4. This sufficient inequality is weaker than the optional half-sum version in the prior plan.

If u is nonzero in L2 and Q_j(u)<=R*||u||_2^2, the actual Schwartz function F=u/||u||_2 has ||F||_2=1, Q_j(F)<=R, the same Fourier zero set, and r<||T F|| whenever r*||u||<||T u|| for a real continuous linear T. In particular integral x^2*|F|^2<=R, integral |F'|^2 + integral x^4*|F'|^2<=2^(2j)*R, and integral x^2*|F'|^2<=2^(2j)*R.

The selected-band theorem: there is a universal r>0 such that for every J>=0, nonempty finite generator family with |g00|,|g10|,|g11|<=2, and real L2 input f with norm one, support in [0,1] almost everywhere, zero integral on every one of K closed grid cells, K>0, K^2>=16384*pi^2*2^(3J), and original average correlation >=1/2, there exist j>=J and an actual Schwartz F with
  ||F||_2=1,  ||complexAverage(G) F||_2>r,  Q_j(F)<=R,
  Fourier(F)(xi)=0 whenever |xi|<=2^j or |xi|>=2^(j+2).
Here R is the fixed dyadicRegularityThreshold from R1775. The same r and R apply to all these inputs, starting levels, grids and bounded generator families.

For arbitrary C1 u:R->C with continuous derivative du and integral |du|^2 finite, every real t satisfies
  integral |u(x+t)-u(x)|^2 dx <= t^2*integral |du(x)|^2 dx.
The proof supplies integrability of the difference energy rather than exploiting the convention for a nonintegrable Bochner integral. It uses the fundamental theorem of calculus, Jensen on the unit interval and Fubini. u itself need not be L1, L2 or Schwartz. The theorem therefore applies to the globally smooth Mobius transform of a Schwartz function, including inversion, without assuming the transform remains Schwartz.

Let U(t)=[[1,t],[0,1]], L(t)=[[1,0],[t,1]], S=[[0,-1],[1,0]], and H(t)=U(1)*L(t)*U(1)^-1=[[1+t,-t],[t,1-t]]. For Q_j(u)<=R, the actual L2 energy differences obey
  ||W_U(t)u-u||^2 <= t^2*2^(2j)*R,
  ||W_L(t)u-u||^2 <=20*t^2*2^(2j)*R,
  ||W_H(t)u-u||^2 <=24*t^2*2^(2j)*R.
The corresponding norm constants used are 1,5,5. The lower and tilted bounds use translation of W_S u and W_(U(1)*S)u, respectively, together with the already verified global derivative transport and moment bounds.

If a!=0, every determinant-one matrix g=[[a,b],[c,d]] has the exact factorization
  g=L((c-(a-1))/a)*H(a-1)*U((b+(a-1))/a).
When |a-1|,|b|,|c|<=eta<=1/2, a>0, the two outer parameters have absolute value <=4*eta, and the middle parameter has absolute value <=eta. Combining isometry, the product difference bound and the three norm estimates yields
  ||W_g u-u||_2 <=29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta.
This holds for every Schwartz u with Q_j(u)<=R. It needs no normalization, frequency localization or spatial support assumption; no g11 restriction beyond determinant one is required. Specializing to the normalized selected band gives the previously targeted uniform local perturbation bound. Group-average smoothing and restricted spectral-gap existence are not conclusions of this theorem.
