R1777 — PAIRWISE ACTION, CONTINUITY AND PROBABILITY CONVOLUTION SMOOTHING
In progress. R1777 extends the local perturbation bound to pairs g,h with arbitrary reference-entry bound B: if |h_ik|<=B, |g_ik-h_ik|<=eta and 2*B*eta<=1/2, then ||W_g u-W_h u||<=58*B*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta for Q_j(u)<=R. The B=2 case gives constant 116. This proves continuity of every Schwartz orbit, and density plus isometry proves joint continuity on actual complex L2 times SL(2,R). Finite Borel measures give integrable actual representation orbits T_g=W_(g^-1). Their Bochner averages contract for probability measures and satisfy the exact convolution identity A_(mu*nu)=A_mu o A_nu. Consequently right-convolution smoothing changes A_mu u by at most ||A_nu u-u||, and by at most 29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta for a kernel nu supported almost everywhere in the stated near-identity entry neighborhood. The error is independent of mu's support size or word length. A corresponding half-norm lower bound is proved whenever the error is at most half a known original lower bound.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let G=SL(2,R), let W_g denote the previously verified actual complex L2 pullback, and let Q_j be the homogeneous Schwartz regularity cost from R1776.

Pairwise comparison. For any g,h in G, actual complex L2 f satisfies
  ||W_g f-W_h f||=||W_(g*h^-1)f-f||.
If every entry of h has absolute value <=B and every entry of g-h has absolute value <=eta, then the three relevant entry errors of g*h^-1 from identity are <=2*B*eta. Therefore, for every Schwartz u with Q_j(u)<=R and 2*B*eta<=1/2,
  ||W_g u-W_h u||<=58*B*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta.
When B=2 and eta<=1/8, the constant is 116. The relative-entry identities are proved using the determinant-one equation, not by treating g-h as a group element. The variable B covers larger products as well as bounded individual generators.

Continuity. Each W_g is an isometry on actual complex L2. The pairwise estimate proves g->W_g u is continuous for every Schwartz input u; it suffices to take j=0 and R=Q_0(u). Schwartz functions are dense in L2. Applying the existing Mathlib dense-fiber/uniform-Lipschitz continuity theorem proves that (f,g)->W_g f is jointly continuous on complex L2 times G. Thus g->W_g f and g->W_(g^-1)f are continuous for every actual L2 input. Second countability of G is proved through its closed embedding into the real 2-by-2 matrices.

Actual averages. Equip G with its Borel sigma algebra. For a measure mu, define
  A_mu f=integral_G W_(g^-1)f dmu(g).
For finite mu, the orbit is strongly measurable and integrable, with constant norm ||f||. Thus this is a genuine Bochner integral. The verified bounds are
  ||A_mu f||<=mu(G)*||f||,
  A_mu(f-h)=A_mu f-A_mu h.
For probability mu, A_mu contracts norms and differences. If ||W_(g^-1)f-f||<=C almost everywhere under probability mu, then ||A_mu f-f||<=C. Exact isometry also gives ||W_(g^-1)f-f||=||W_g f-f||.

For finite Borel measures mu,nu and every actual complex L2 f,
  A_(mu*nu)f=A_mu(A_nu f),
where * is Mathlib's actual multiplicative measure convolution, the pushforward of mu times nu under (g,h)->g*h. The integral_mconv theorem applies to the proved integrable orbit; the fixed continuous linear operator W_(g^-1) then commutes with the inner integral. The inverse convention makes this product order match the representation T_g=W_(g^-1).

Quantitative right smoothing. For arbitrary probability measures mu,nu,
  ||A_(mu*nu)f-A_mu f||<=||A_nu f-f||.
In particular, if u is Schwartz, Q_j(u)<=R, eta<=1/2, and nu-almost every g satisfies
  |g00-1|<=eta, |g01|<=eta, |g10|<=eta,
then
  ||A_(mu*nu)u-A_mu u||<=29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta.
There is no support-size or word-length restriction on mu. If in addition m<=||A_mu u|| and 29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta<=m/2, then
  m/2<=||A_(mu*nu)u||.
This theorem needs neither normalization nor spectral localization beyond its explicit regularity-cost hypothesis. It is a smoothing-stability theorem, not an existence theorem for a flat kernel or a spectral gap. Instantiation with the concrete symmetric generator walk, its power lower bound and a Haar-neighborhood kernel remains to be proved.

R1778 — CONCRETE GENERATOR WALKS, DYADIC POWERS AND HAAR SMOOTHING
In progress. R1778 defines the multiplicity-preserving symmetric generator probability measure rho and its actual convolution walk, proving A_(rho^(*n))f=T^n f for the existing finite symmetric average T on actual complex L2. For any symmetric linear map on a real inner-product space, unit f and 0<=r<=||Tf|| imply r^(2^m)<=||T^(2^m)f||. Completeness, boundedness and contraction are unnecessary in the linear-map version. SL(2,R) is locally compact by its closed matrix embedding. The explicit Frobenius ball B_eta={g:sum of four squared entry errors<eta^2} is open, contains identity for eta>0, and lies in a compact matrix-entry box. Its Haar mass is positive and finite. The normalized restricted Haar measure P_eta is therefore an actual probability kernel, with the explicit indicator density and almost-everywhere entry bounds. EXACT STATEMENTS
Let A_mu f=integral W_(g^-1)f dmu(g), in the already verified actual complex L2 representation of SL(2,R). For c>0 and G:Fin c->SL(2,R), define
  rho=(2c)^(-1) sum_i (delta_(G_i)+delta_(G_i^-1)).
Repeated generators retain their multiplicities. This is a probability measure and A_rho f=complexAverage G f=T f. The equality itself also holds for the empty generator family. Define the actual walk by mu_0=delta_1 and mu_(n+1)=rho*mu_n. Every mu_n is a probability measure and A_(mu_n)f=T^[n]f.

For any real inner-product space, symmetric linear map S, unit f, r>=0 with r<=||Sf||, and m>=0,
  r^(2^m)<=||S^(2^m)f||.
The proof iterates ||Sf||^2=<S^2f,f><=||S^2f|| and symmetry of powers. This does not require completeness, continuity, boundedness or contraction of S. A continuous-linear-map/function-iterate corollary applies to T. Consequently r^(2^m)<=||A_(mu_(2^m))f||.

Equip SL(2,R) with its Borel sigma algebra and Mathlib's actual Haar measure H. Local compactness is proved via the closed embedding into real 2-by-2 matrices. For eta>0 let
  B_eta={g:(g00-1)^2+g01^2+g10^2+(g11-1)^2<eta^2},
  P_eta=H(B_eta)^(-1) H restricted to B_eta.
The open ball contains identity and lies in a compact entry box. Thus 0<H(B_eta)<infinity, P_eta is a probability measure, and
  P_eta=H.withDensity(1_(B_eta)/H(B_eta)).
Almost every g under P_eta satisfies |g00-1|<=eta, |g01|<=eta and |g10|<=eta. This is the ordinary Frobenius radius; eta^2 is the threshold on the squared-entry sum.

For unit Schwartz u, Q_j(u)<=R, r>=0, ||Tu||>=r, 0<eta<=1/2 and any m satisfying

the concrete smoothed convolution walk satisfies

This follows from the proved dyadic lower bound and R1777's exact right-smoothing contraction estimate; it does not require a word-length or support-size restriction on mu. R1779 — SMOOTHED HAAR DENSITY AND ADJUSTABLE DYADIC SCALES
In progress. R1779 proves the general right-convolution density formula mu*(H.withDensity p)=H.withDensity(k), k(g)=integral p(h^-1*g) dmu(h), for arbitrary s-finite mu and a left-invariant s-finite base H with measurable nonnegative p. The first measure may be atomic. For the actual Haar kernel, the smoothed density is measurable, finite everywhere for positive radius, integrates to one under probability mu, and is bounded by 1/H(B_eta). The weighted actual complex-L2 orbit is Bochner integrable and its Haar integral equals groupActionAverage. Scalar lemmas choose dyadic length ell=2^m between j/(4N) and j/(2N), above C*log(1/eta)/log(1/epsilon), while making the smoothing error at eta=4^(-j) at most r^ell/2. N may be arbitrarily large above a requested Nmin. Composing with the existing normalized regular band selection produces a unit Schwartz witness with exact annular Fourier support, fixed regularity cost and an actual smoothed-density norm at least r^ell/2, with no remaining smoothing-error inequality as a hypothesis.

EXACT STATEMENTS
General density identity. Let H be an s-finite left-invariant measure on a measurable group, let mu be any s-finite measure, and let p be measurable with values in the extended nonnegative reals. Define
  k(g)=integral_h p(h^-1*g) dmu(h).
Then k is measurable and
  mu*(H.withDensity p)=H.withDensity k.
This follows from actual measure convolution, left invariance and Tonelli. It does not require mu to have a density. If mu is a probability measure and p<=D pointwise, then k<=D pointwise.

Specialize H to the actual Haar measure on SL(2,R), p to the normalized indicator of the ordinary Frobenius ball B_eta from R1778, and mu to any probability measure. For eta>0 the resulting density k_mu,eta is measurable, finite at every group element, bounded by 1/H(B_eta), and has Haar integral one. For every actual complex L2 vector f,
  g -> k_mu,eta(g) T_g f
is genuinely Bochner integrable, with T_g=W_(g^-1), and
  A_(mu*P_eta)f=integral_g k_mu,eta(g) T_g f dH(g).
This applies to all concrete generator-walk measures, including the atomic ones. The finite-scale lower bound from R1778 is transferred to this density integral.

Compatible scales. Given A>=0, r>0 and any requested integer Nmin, there are integers N>=max(1,Nmin) and J>=1 such that, for every L>0, C real satisfying 4*N*C*log(4)<=L, and every j>=J, one can choose m>=0, ell=2^m, with
  ell<=j/(2N),
  C*log(1/eta)/L<ell,
  A*2^j*eta<=r^ell/2,  eta=(1/4)^j<=1/2.
A separate dyadic-window lemma gives j/(4N)<ell<=j/(2N), and its witness is used in the combined theorem. The construction chooses (1/2)^N<=r and a fixed K with A*(1/2)^K<=1/2, then forces N*ell+K<=j. Natural powers, dyadic selection and the logarithmic identity are all proved. For any prescribed M, an explicit sufficiently small epsilon_0>0 makes log(1/epsilon)>0 and >=M for every 0<epsilon<=epsilon_0. In particular take L=log(1/epsilon) and M=4*N*C*log(4).

Selected-band composition. There is a universal r>0 such that, for every Nmin, suitable N>=max(1,Nmin) and J0 exist; for every C>0 there is epsilon_0 in (0,1). For every 0<epsilon<=epsilon_0 and every starting frequency J>=J0, retain the existing input hypotheses: nonempty generator family G with |g00|,|g10|,|g11|<=2; K>0; real L2 input f of norm one, supported almost everywhere in [0,1]; zero integral on each of the K closed grid cells; K^2>=16384*pi^2*2^(3J); and <Tf,f>>=1/2. Then there exist j>=J, a complex Schwartz function F and a dyadic length ell=2^m such that
  ||F||_2=1, ||TF||_2>r, Q_j(F)<=dyadicRegularityThreshold,
  Fourier(F)(xi)=0 for |xi|<=2^j or |xi|>=2^(j+2),
  ell<=j/(2N), C*log(1/eta)/log(1/epsilon)<ell, eta=4^(-j),
  ||integral_g k_(walk_ell),eta(g) T_g F dH(g)||_2>=r^ell/2.
There is no additional smoothing-error premise in this final theorem. The large adjustable N preserves freedom for comparison with the future upper-bound decay exponent. Epsilon is a threshold parameter here; this theorem alone does not certify epsilon-nearness of G. Flatness, a quantitative upper bound and the spectral-gap contradiction have not been proved.

R1780 — AFFINE WAVELET BOUND FOR ARBITRARY L2 TEST VECTORS
In progress. R1780 proves exact Fourier scaling/translation and translation-correlation Plancherel for actual Schwartz functions, proves integrability of the singular wavelet scale kernel, and bounds positive-scale affine energy by M^(-1)||u||_2^2||v||_2^2 whenever the Schwartz analyzing vector u has Fourier transform zero on |xi|<M, M>0. The test vector v is an arbitrary actual complex L2 vector. Schwartz density and Fatou establish the extended nonnegative integral bound; its finiteness proves genuine Bochner integrability and the real product and iterated integral bounds. The matrix g(s,t)=[[sqrt(s),t/sqrt(s)],[0,1/sqrt(s)]] has determinant one for s>0, and the existing action T_g=W_(g^-1) on u is exactly s^(-1/2)u((x-t)/s). No spatial support or regularity assumption on v is imposed.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Let u be a complex-valued Schwartz function on R, let v be any element of the actual complex L2(R) space, and let M>0. Assume Fourier(u)(xi)=0 whenever |xi|<M. For s>0 define
  pi(s,t)u(x)=s^(-1/2)*u((x-t)/s).
Then the coefficient c(s,t)=<v,pi(s,t)u> is measurable in (s,t), the nonnegative function |c(s,t)|^2/s^2 is genuinely integrable for ds dt on (0,infinity) x R, and
  integral_(s>0) integral_t |c(s,t)|^2 dt ds/s^2
    <= M^(-1)*||u||_2^2*||v||_2^2.
Both product and iterated real Bochner integral bounds and the extended nonnegative integral bound are formalized. The coefficient is defined to be zero for nonpositive scale solely to give a total measurable function. The theorem integrates only positive scales. No smoothness, Fourier cutoff or spatial support is required of v, and u need not have compact spatial support.

For two Schwartz functions, translation Plancherel gives
  integral_t |<v,u(.-t)>|^2 dt
    = integral_xi |Fourier(u)(xi)|^2*|Fourier(v)(xi)|^2 dxi.
Exact Fourier formulas for positive rescaling and translation are proved directly. After applying the unitary dilation, the scale density is controlled using
  integral_R |Fourier(u)(xi)|^2/|xi| dxi <= M^(-1)*||u||_2^2.
The full real-scale change-of-variable identity is used to bound the positive-scale integral, not to assert an incorrect positive-scale equality. The product kernel is integrable, so exchanges of real integrals are justified. Schwartz density and pointwise coefficient convergence establish the arbitrary-L2 version by Fatou, and finiteness then supplies actual Bochner integrability.

The determinant-one matrix
  g(s,t)=[[sqrt(s),t/sqrt(s)],[0,1/sqrt(s)]]
satisfies eval_(g^-1)(x)=(x-t)/s and denom_(g^-1)(x)=sqrt(s). Its existing complex L2 action T_g=W_(g^-1) is exactly the translated unitary dilation pi(s,t)u. Thus the proved affine coefficient is a literal restriction of the action used by groupActionAverage; no alternate action or convention is substituted. Translation/dilation norm preservation follows from this same action.

R1781 — ACTUAL COLUMN HAAR MEASURE, POLAR FORMULA AND BOX VOLUME
In progress. R1781 constructs global column/shear coordinates for SL2: for v nonzero and q=v0^2+v1^2, the second column is (-v1,v0)/q+b*v. Reconstruction is exact. Left multiplication acts by the determinant-one linear map on v and a measurable fiberwise translation on b, so the pushforward mu0 of Lebesgue dv db is left invariant. The zero-column fiber is null; the inverse coordinates are continuous, map mu0 back to Lebesgue measure, and prove finiteness on compact sets. Mu0 is a nonzero Haar measure and the already-used Haar measure H equals c_H*mu0 for a proved positive finite scalar. Polar change of variables gives density c_H*a da dtheta db on a>0, -pi<theta<pi, with the exact factorization into rotation and affineWaveletMatrix(a^2,a^2*b). Bounded entries imply a^2<=2B^2 and |b|<=B^2; the entry box is compact and H(box_B)<=8*c_H*B^4 for B>=0.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Global coordinates. Write a determinant-one matrix by its columns v,w, and let q=v0^2+v1^2. The first column is nonzero, q>0, and there is a unique b=(v dot w)/q such that
  w=(-v1,v0)/q+b*v.
The actual matrix columnMatrix(v,b), its coordinates and both reconstruction identities are formalized. A total chart sends the null fiber v=0 to identity. Its inverse on the group is continuous; the chart itself is measurable.

Actual Haar measure. Let mu0 be the pushforward under this total chart of ordinary Lebesgue measure on (Fin 2 -> R) x R. Under multiplication by any h in SL2, coordinates transform as
  (v,b) -> (h*v, c(h,v)+b),
with a measurable shift c independent of b. The first factor preserves Lebesgue measure because det(h)=1, and every second-factor translation preserves Lebesgue measure. The library skew-product theorem proves invariance of the full product measure. The chart intertwines this map with left multiplication outside the null zero-column fiber. Thus mu0 is left invariant. Mapping mu0 back by the coordinates recovers Lebesgue measure exactly. Compact sets have finite mass by their compact coordinate images; mu0 is nonzero and hence a Haar measure. For the same previously used Haar measure H,
  H=c_H*mu0,  c_H=haarScalarFactor(H,mu0)>0.
The scalar is an actual nonnegative real, so it is finite. No coordinate-density premise is imported.

Polar formula. For v=(a*cos(theta),a*sin(theta)), q=a^2. For a>0 the coordinate matrix is exactly
  rotationMatrix(theta)*affineWaveletMatrix(a^2,a^2*b)
  = rotationMatrix(theta)*diag(a,1/a)*upperUnipotent(b).
For every measurable nonnegative extended-real function F on the actual group,
  integral F(g) dH(g)
    = c_H * integral_((a,theta) in (0,infinity)x(-pi,pi))
        a * integral_b F(columnChart(polarColumn(a,theta),b)) db da dtheta.
This is the product-integral notation of the checked theorem; no integrability premise is needed for this nonnegative formula. The omitted ray is null through the library polar theorem. The same chart and representation are used as in R1780.

Bounded boxes. For every determinant-one matrix,
  |columnShear(g)| <= (g01^2+g11^2)/2.
The proof uses the exact Gram/determinant identity q*||w||^2-(v dot w)^2=1. Consequently if all entries have absolute value at most B, then q<=2B^2 and |b|<=B^2. The entry box is compact and its coordinate image lies in [-B,B]^2 x [-B^2,B^2]. For B>=0 this yields
  mu0(box_B)<=8*B^4,
  H(box_B)<=8*c_H*B^4.
The same c_H occurs in the Haar identity and polar formula.

These complete the Haar-coordinate and polynomial-volume obligations selected after R1780. They do not yet prove the bounded-box coefficient energy bound or the smoothed-average upper bound. Retaining an arbitrary L2 test vector in that next estimate should allow a direct Cauchy–Schwarz argument; this proposed consequence remains explicitly unproved. No novelty is claimed for the standard geometric support results.

R1782 — BOUNDED-ENTRY HAAR COEFFICIENT ENERGY FOR ARBITRARY L2 TEST VECTORS
In progress. R1782 proves the actual bounded-entry Haar coefficient estimate. For every real B, M>0, Schwartz u with Fourier(u)=0 on |xi|<M, and arbitrary complex L2 v, integral_box_B |<v,T_g u>|^2 dH(g) <= 2*pi*c_H*B^2*M^(-1)*||u||_2^2*||v||_2^2. Here T_g=W_(g^-1), box_B consists of actual SL2 matrices with every entry bounded in absolute value by B, and c_H=haarScalarFactor(H,columnChartMeasure) is the same proved positive finite Haar scalar from R1781. The nonnegative integral bound proves genuine integrability before the real integral is used. The proof establishes commutation with complex I and complex inner-product preservation, the exact changes s=a^2 and t=a^2*b giving affine density 2 da db/a, transfer of rotations to v, and the pointwise Haar-weight comparison a<=B^2*(2/a) on the entry box. Tonelli and the angular interval length 2*pi finish the estimate. The high-frequency Schwartz input retains its spatial tails.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Complex inner products. For the actual complexified action W_g, multiplication by I commutes with W_g. Complex polarization then proves
  <W_g v,W_g w> = <v,w>.
In particular <v,W_(g^-1)w>=<W_g v,w> and
  <v,T_(g*h)u>=<W_g v,T_h u>,  T_g=W_(g^-1).
This is proved from the existing action, not asserted from real linearity alone.

Affine substitutions. For arbitrary extended-nonnegative functions, the one-dimensional Jacobian theorem proves the changes s=a^2 and t=a^2*b, a>0. Their exact combined identity is
  integral_(a>0) (2/a) integral_b f(a^2,a^2*b) db da
    = integral_(s>0) (1/s^2) integral_t f(s,t) dt ds.
No finiteness or measurability premise is needed for this substitution identity. For each rotation theta, the actual group coefficient in the polar chart is the affine wavelet coefficient against W_rotation(theta) v. Norm preservation allows the proved R1780 bound to apply with the original ||v||.

General polar-to-box estimate. Let f:SL2(R)->[0,infinity] be measurable. Suppose, for every theta,
  integral_(a>0) (2/a) integral_b f(columnChart(polarColumn(a,theta),b)) db da <= K.
For every real B,
  integral_box_B f(g) dH(g) <= c_H*(2*pi*B^2)*K.
This includes infinite K. The same H and c_H from R1781 are used. On the box, a^2<=2B^2, hence a<=B^2*(2/a). Apply this to the indicator of the box, then Tonelli and the angular interval (-pi,pi) of length 2*pi. Measurability of the actual polar-chart integrand is proved.

Actual coefficient energy. Let u be a complex Schwartz function on R with Fourier(u)(xi)=0 whenever |xi|<M, with M>0. Let v be any vector in the actual complex L2 space. Set T_g=W_(g^-1) and box_B={g in SL2(R): for all i,j, |g_ij|<=B}. Then for every real B,
  integral_box_B |<v,T_g u>|^2 dH(g)
    <= 2*pi*c_H*B^2*M^(-1)*||u||_2^2*||v||_2^2.
The coefficient-squared function is continuous. Its nonnegative integral is bounded by a finite number, which proves its Bochner integrability over the box. The real integral theorem is then derived, so it cannot hold vacuously from a default integral value. The arbitrary-v formulation is stronger than restricting the estimate to the self-coefficient, and will be used for a density-weighted average. That average bound remains unproved at this checkpoint. No new original theorem family is completed; these are analytical support results for paid padding, with no novelty claim.

R1783 — ACTUAL DENSITY AVERAGES, WALK SUPPORT AND RESTRICTED GAP FROM FLATNESS
In progress. A uniform scalar theorem shows that D^2<=2^j makes this impossible for large j and 2*N*ell<=j with sufficiently large N. Combining the actual lower witness with this barrier yields a restricted quadratic-form gap below 1/2, conditional on the explicitly quantified flatness of the actual smoothed generator walks. No generator family is proved to satisfy that hypothesis yet.

    <=2*pi*c_H*B^2*D*M^(-1)*||u||^2.

R1784 — ACTUAL SMALL-BALL VOLUME AND NORMALIZED HAAR KERNEL

R1785 — EXPLICIT RATIONAL FREE SEED AND QUANTITATIVE SIGNED WORDS
In progress. R1785 constructs q=3(n+1), a=(q+1)/q, A=diag(a,a^-1), M=[[1,1],[1,2]], B=M*A*M^-1. The map from the free group on two generators sending them to A,B is injective over both Q and R. A direct 3-adic ping-pong proof on nonzero rational vectors replaces the source strong-Tits invocation for this seed-pair step. Each entry error from identity is <=4/q and the squared ordinary Frobenius distance is <=(8/q)^2; inversion preserves that distance. Thus for every eta>0 some fixed n gives a free pair and their inverses inside the actual ball B_eta. With Q=q(q+1), every signed word of length ell has Q^ell as a common denominator and every entry has absolute value <=(1+8/q)^ell. Equal-length words representing different free-group elements differ in some real matrix entry by at least Q^(-ell). Word evaluation agrees exactly with Mathlib FreeGroup.lift/mk, including its sign convention. The larger near-identity family and actual-walk flatness are still unproved.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Explicit rational free pair. For every rational a with |a|_3>1, let A=diag(a,a^-1), M=[[1,1],[1,2]], and B=M*A*M^-1. The hypothesis implies a!=0; the formal theorem takes that nonzero proof explicitly. The homomorphism FreeGroup(Bool)->SL2(Q) sending false to A and true to B is injective. The action is on actual nonzero vectors in Q^2. Positive/negative cones have |v1|_3<|v0|_3 and the reversed inequality. A maps the complement of the negative cone into the positive cone; A^-1 reverses these roles. Since |2|_3=1, M maps either cone into vectors with equal coordinate norms, making the original and conjugated cones disjoint. The inherited vector action and Mathlib ping-pong theorem finish freeness. No p-adic completion, projectivization, or strong-Tits premise is used.

Explicit near-identity specialization. For every natural n, q=3(n+1)>0 and a=(q+1)/q satisfy |a|_3>1. Set seed(n)=(A,B) as above. Its rational free-group lift is injective. The exact conjugate matrix is
  B=[[2a-a^-1, -a+a^-1], [2a-2a^-1, -a+2a^-1]].
For every seed entry ij,
  |seed(n,k)_ij-I_ij| <=4/q.
The entrywise rational-to-real map is an injective group homomorphism, so the real free-group lift is also injective. In the SAME actual Frobenius-ball convention used by the Haar kernel,
  mobiusIdentityDistanceSq(realSeed(n,k)) <=(8/q)^2.
For all determinant-one real2x2 matrices, that squared identity distance is unchanged by inversion. Therefore for every eta>0 there is n such that both generators AND their inverses lie in the actual open B_eta, and their real free-group lift is injective.

Exact word arithmetic and size. Let Q=q(q+1)>0. HasDenominator(D,g) means every D*g_ij is an integer. It is closed under multiplication with denominators multiplying, and inversion in SL2 with denominator unchanged. The seed pair and both inverses have common denominatorQ. For every signed word w of length ell, without any reducedness assumption,
  HasDenominator(Q^ell, product(w)),
  |product(w)_ij| <=(1+8/q)^ell for every i,j.
The growth proof uses row sums <=1+8/q for each signed letter; it avoids introducing a factor2 at every multiplication. It relies on the entry-error bound and the determinant-one inverse formula. The signed-word convention exactly matches FreeGroup.Lift.aux: true means a positive generator, false its inverse. Accordingly product(w)=FreeGroup.lift(seed(n))(FreeGroup.mk(w)), and product(u)=product(v) iff mk(u)=mk(v).

Quantitative distinction. If D>0 and g,h have common denominatorD and g!=h, then some entry satisfies |g_ij-h_ij|>=1/D. Consequently, if signed words u,v have the SAME length ell and mk(u)!=mk(v), then some rational entry, and the corresponding real entry, differ by at least Q^(-ell). Distinct raw lists are not claimed to have distinct products: the hypothesis distinguishes their free-group elements and therefore respects cancellation.

Scope. This proves the fixed rational near-identity free seed and its quantitative word bounds. It does not yet construct the growing free family of the source Lemma1.1, prove its packing/cardinality estimates, establish walk flattening, or finish unconditional paid padding. No novelty is claimed for the explicit ping-pong method or these supporting facts.

R1786 — EXPONENTIAL FREE WORD FAMILIES AND QUANTITATIVE RECENTERING
In progress. R1786 proves a general free-group prefix-survival lemma and a ping-pong theorem for squares of equal-length distinct words with reduced doubles and no inverse coincidences. All positive binary words of lengthL>0 instantiate it, giving exactly2^L freely generating squares of reduced length2L. Their images in the R1785 rational/real seed are free and distinct, have common denominatorQ^(2L), entries and inverse entries bounded by N=(1+8/q)^(2L), and entry separation at leastQ^(-2L). An explicit invertible Nielsen basis change shows that any injectively indexed subfamily w0^-1*w avoiding the base remains free. The translated matrices have denominatorQ^(4L). If their unshifted coordinate differences from the base are <=delta and inverse base entries are <=N, their ordinary Frobenius distance from identity is <=4*N*delta. Thus coordinate differences <=eta/(8*N) put the actual translated matrices inside B_eta. The large nearby cluster and the resulting scale/cardinality relations have not yet been constructed.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Cancellation and free squares. If u++v is reduced and invRev(v) is NOT a prefix of the reduced representative of x in a free group, then u is a prefix of the reduced representative of mk(u++v)*x. The proof removes the last letter of v: either it cancels and the induction applies, or the boundary is reduced and the whole prefix survives. The standard existing reduction/toWord APIs are reused. Define prefixDomain(w)={x : w is a prefix of toWord(x)}. Distinct equal-length words have disjoint prefix domains. If w++w is reduced, mk(w)^2 sends the complement of prefixDomain(invRev(w)) into prefixDomain(w), and its inverse has the reversed property.

For any nontrivial index type and words w_i whose doubles w_i++w_i are reduced, suppose all lengths agree, the map i->w_i is injective, and w_i!=invRev(w_j) for all i,j. Then the homomorphism sending the free generator i to mk(w_i)^2 is injective. No finiteness assumption on the index type is needed. The formal alphabet and index types share a universe, matching Mathlib ping-pong. The theorem also transfers through any injective homomorphism out of the ambient free group.

Exponential concrete family. For every L>0, index all positive binary words of lengthL by f:Fin L->Bool. Their squared words are reduced, have length2L and freely generate a group. There are exactly2^L distinct squares. Endpoint restrictions are unnecessary because all letters have positive sign, while inverse words have negative sign. The exact reduced representative is the doubled word.

Actual matrix family. For the fixed R1785 seed parameter n, let q=3(n+1), Q=q(q+1), s=1+8/q. The image W(n,L) of the positive squares in SL2(Q), and its injective real image, have exactly2^L members and their free-group lifts are injective. Every member has common denominatorQ^(2L), every entry of each member and of its inverse has absolute value<=N=s^(2L), and any two different members differ in some rational/real entry by at leastQ^(-2L). The word-evaluation identity is exact; there is no assumed matrix freeness or counting premise.

Translation preserves freeness. For an arbitrary free basis indexed by i and a chosen o, the change fixing x_o and sending each x_i (i!=o) to x_o^-1*x_i is an actual group automorphism. Its inverse fixes x_o and sends x_i to x_o*x_i. Both compositions are proved equal to identity. Consequently for any group family a with injective free-group lift, any injective j:K->indices avoiding o gives another injective free-group lift k->a_o^-1*a_(j(k)). K need not be finite or nontrivial. This is instantiated for both the rational and real square families.

Quantitative recentering. Translated square-family matrices have common denominatorQ^(4L). The rational-to-real embedding preserves this actual inverse-product. For arbitrary a,b inSL2(R), suppose every entry of a^-1 has absolute value<=N and every coordinate difference b_ij-a_ij has absolute value<=delta. Then
  |(a^-1*b)_ij-I_ij| <=2*N*delta,
  mobiusIdentityDistanceSq(a^-1*b) <=(4*N*delta)^2.
Nonnegativity of N,delta is derived from the premises. If4*N*delta<eta, the translated matrix belongs to the actual open Frobenius ballB_eta. In particular, for our square family and eta>0, coordinate differences <=eta/(8*s^(2L)) imply B_eta membership. The factor8 provides strict margin: the radius bound is eta/2.

Scope. These results complete the short-word free-family and translation portions of the selected generator construction. R1787 — RATIONAL NEAR-IDENTITY FREE FAMILIES WITH POLYNOMIAL ARITHMETIC
In progress. R1787 completes the unconditional generator construction. EXACT STATEMENTS
Finite coordinate packing. Let a finite indexed family have four real coordinates in[-N,N], and delta>0. Set K=floor_nat(2N/delta)+1. The coordinate bin is floor_nat((x+N)/delta). Every coordinate bin is<K, and equal bins imply absolute difference<delta. If K^4*m<=the number of indices, a subset of at least m indices has all pairwise coordinate differences<delta. For N>=1 and0<eta<=1, choosing delta=eta/(8N) gives K<=17N^2/eta. These facts follow from actual finite bins and the finite pigeonhole theorem; no packing principle is assumed.

Selecting the actual free family. Let q=3(n+1), Q0=q(q+1), s=1+8/q, L>0 and N=s^(2L). If the preceding bin count at delta=eta/(8N) satisfies K^4*(m+1)<=2^L, then there is g:Fin m->SL2(Q) whose rational and real free-group lifts are injective, whose entries are cleared by Q0^(4L), and whose real images lie in the actual open Frobenius eta-ball about identity. Select a large bin fiber, choose a base, remove it, select exactly m remaining members, enumerate them and apply the R1786 free-basis translation. Thus the removed base costs exactly one index and does not remain as an identity generator.

Fixed dyadic scales. Fix n=9999 once and for all, so q=30000 and Q0=900030000. Lean verifies s^64<=2 and the required numerical denominator/bin bounds. For r>=5, let L=16r, eta=2^(-r), N=s^(32r).   m>=epsilon^(-3), m>=2, Q>0,

R1788 — ACTUAL WALK NONCONCENTRATION AND INITIAL SQUARED L2 BOUND
In progress. R1788 establishes nonconcentration at the rational separation scale for the actual symmetric generator walk. For m freely generating matrices and any k>=1 with k^2<=2m, every n-step endpoint has probability <=(2/k)^n. The proof uses a radial free-group supersolution and an exact identification with the actual matrix-walk singleton measure. For rational generators with common denominator Q, every endpoint has denominator Q^n. If eta>0, eta<=1 and 8*eta<Q^(-2n), a right-smoothing ball meets at most one possible endpoint. Consequently the actual smoothed density is bounded by (2/k)^n/H(B_eta). For the R1787 family, m>=epsilon^(-3) gives the factor (2*epsilon)^n. When eta<=1/2, both the pointwise density and its squared L2 integral are bounded by 512*(2*epsilon)^n/(c_H*eta^3). Integrability of the real density squared is proved. This is an initial estimate, not the much stronger full walk-flatness bound.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Rational arithmetic and support. For any rational generator family with common denominator Q, evaluation of a signed word of length n has denominator Q^n; inverses preserve the denominator. Equal-length words representing different free-group elements evaluate to real matrices separated in some coordinate by at least Q^(-n), if the generator lift is injective. Unequal raw words are not assumed distinct after evaluation. The real matrices admitting a common denominator D form a countable measurable carrier. It contains identity, is inverse-closed and multiplies D- and E-carriers into the DE-carrier. The actual symmetric generator walk lies almost everywhere in the Q^n-carrier.

Free-walk atom estimate. For a finite alphabet of cardinality m, put weight_q(w)=q^(length of the reduced representative). Left multiplication by the inverse of a letter extends the reduced word except for at most one cancelling letter. The sum over the2m letters of the neighboring weights is at most (2m*q+q^(-1))*weight_q(w). For k>=1 with k^2<=2m, q=1/k is therefore a supersolution with normalized factor2/k. The exact symmetric free-walk recurrence p_n satisfies
  0<=p_n(w)<=(2/k)^n * k^(-reduced_length(w))<=(2/k)^n.
For any actual matrix family with injective free-group lift, the n-step generatorWalkMeasure singleton at the evaluated w equals ENNReal.ofReal(p_n(w)). Points outside the lift range have zero mass. Hence every endpoint of the actual matrix walk has probability at most(2/k)^n. This is an elementary sufficient bound, not the sharp Kesten spectral radius.

Separation-scale uniqueness. If a,b have common denominator D, and a^-1*x and b^-1*x both lie in the ordinary Frobenius eta-ball, with0<eta<=1, then every entry of a^-1*b-I has absolute value<=8*eta. But a^-1*b has denominator D^2 and is separated from identity by at least1/D^2 unless a=b. Therefore8*eta<1/D^2 forces a=b. Applied to D=Q^n, the right-smoothing ball at any x contains at most one possible n-step endpoint. No left/right interchange or smoothing symmetry is assumed.

Actual density. For any measure whose almost-everywhere support has this uniqueness property and whose atoms are bounded by A, its actual one-sided Haar-smoothed density is at most A/H(B_eta). This follows by identifying the integrand with a singleton indicator, or with zero when no support point contributes. Applied to the rational free walk,
  kappa_(n,eta)(x) <= (2/k)^n / H(B_eta)
under the explicit condition8*eta<Q^(-2n). For eta<=1/2, the proved cubic Haar-volume lower bound gives
  kappa_(n,eta)(x) <= 512*(2/k)^n/(c_H*eta^3).
For the R1787 generator family and0<epsilon<=1, m>=epsilon^(-3) permits k=1/epsilon, hence the factor(2*epsilon)^n.

Squared L2 estimate. A nonnegative probability density bounded by C has integral of its square at most C. This is proved for the actual smoothed density, including integrability of its real-valued square and the conversion from the extended-nonnegative integral. Thus, under the same hypotheses,
  integral kappa_(n,eta)(x)^2 dH(x) <=512*(2*epsilon)^n/(c_H*eta^3).
The bound is for the squared L2 norm. The Haar factor is exactly the same positive finite c_H used throughout the analytic chain.

Scope. These estimates establish the arithmetic/free-walk initialization at a precise separation scale. They do not prove the later density-flatness exponent, metric BSG, product growth, spectral expansion or unconditional paid padding. Converting the initial factor into a radius gain is the next target. No novelty is claimed for these standard support facts.

R1789 — INITIAL RADIUS GAIN FOR ALL LATER WALK LENGTHS
In progress. R1789 proves an explicit initial density and squared-L2 radius gain. There is a threshold J0 such that, for every r>=5, one fixed rational free family of exactly 2^(3r) generators in the Frobenius ball of radius2^(-r), with inverses in the same ball and common denominator Q_r<=2^(1920r), works for all j>=max(J0,7680r) and all walk lengths ell>=floor(j/(3840r)). J0 is independent of r. This is the initialization for flattening, not the final flatness bound.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Scales. For r>=5 and j>=7680r, put eta=4^(-j), rho=2^(-r), and n0=floor(j/(3840r)). Then n0>=1,3840r*n0<=j<=7680r*n0<=15360(r-1)n0. Initial density gain. For any free rational family of exactly2^(3r) generators with common denominator Q_r, the actual n0-step one-sided Haar-smoothed density is bounded at every point by(512/c_H)*eta^(-3+1/30720), where c_H is the same positive Haar column-chart factor used throughout the analytic chain.

Propagation. Left convolution of a density bounded by C with a probability measure remains bounded by C. The convolution identity and its orientation are proved for the actual density. Consequently the initial bound survives every additional generator-walk step, without changing eta or claiming inversion symmetry.

Prefactor absorption. For every fixed real C there exists J0 such that C*(4^(-j))^(-3+1/30720)<=(4^(-j))^(-3+1/61440) for all j>=J0. In particular C=512/c_H gives a threshold independent of r.

Combined family theorem. There exists J0 such that for every r>=5 there exists one g:Fin(2^(3r))->SL2(Q) with injective rational and real free-group lifts, exactly2^(3r) distinct rational and real images, denominator Q_r, and g_i and g_i^(-1) in the real Frobenius ball of radius2^(-r), satisfying the following for every j>=max(J0,7680r) and every ell>=floor(j/(3840r)):
  kappa_(ell,4^(-j))(x) <= (4^(-j))^(-3+1/61440) at every x;
  the real-valued density squared is Haar-integrable;
  integral kappa_(ell,4^(-j))^2 dH <= (4^(-j))^(-3+1/61440).
The same g works for all j and ell; the existing polynomial denominator bounds remain available for this Q_r. The integral is the squared L2 norm, not the L2 norm. These are initial bounds, not the final flatness exponent, spectral expansion or unconditional paid padding.

R1790 — SYMMETRIC AUTOCORRELATION AND EXACT ENERGY/ACTION BRIDGE
In progress. R1790 proves the symmetry and energy bridge for the actual smoothed walk. Haar measure on SL2(R) is right- and inversion-invariant, using mathlib perfectness and modular-character results. If mu=nu^n*P_eta, its autocorrelation mu.inv*mu is exactly P_eta*nu^(2n)*P_eta. Its canonical density rho(x)=integral kappa(y)*kappa(y*x)dH(y) is pointwise inversion-symmetric, has mass1, inherits any initial pointwise bound for kappa, and satisfies rho(x)<=rho(1)=integral kappa^2. Real squared-L2 integrability/bounds also transfer. For the actual representation average A_mu, inner(f,A_(mu.inv*mu)f)=norm(A_mu f)^2; hence a large action survives symmetrization. Full flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Haar measure. The modular character of SL2(R) is identically1, because mathlib proves the commutator subgroup is the entire group and a homomorphism into an abelian group kills commutators. Thus the existing Haar measure is right-invariant. Haar uniqueness and the inverse-closed Frobenius unit ball give inversion invariance with the same normalization. No separate replacement Haar measure is introduced.

Measure identities. For SFinite measures on a measurable group, inversion reverses convolution: (mu*nu).inv=nu.inv*mu.inv. In particular (mu.inv*mu).inv=mu.inv*mu. Inversion preserves probability. The actual symmetric generator measure and every walk power are inverse-invariant; walk lengths concatenate by convolution. The actual Haar-ball kernel is inverse-invariant. Therefore, for positive generator count and eta>0,
  (nu^n*P_eta).inv*(nu^n*P_eta)=P_eta*nu^(2n)*P_eta.
The order of the factors is exact; no kernel/walk commutativity is used.

Canonical density. For a measurable nonnegative extended density f over a right-invariant measure H, define rho=leftConvolutionDensity((H.withDensity f).inv,f). Then
  rho(x)=integral f(y)*f(y*x)dH(y),
  rho(x^-1)=rho(x),
  rho(1)=integral f(y)^2dH(y),
  rho(x)<=rho(1).
The last statement uses Holder with exponents2,2 and right-invariance. With left-invariance as well, H.withDensity rho=(H.withDensity f).inv*(H.withDensity f).

Actual smoothed probability. Apply this construction to kappa, the existing one-sided smoothed density of any probability measure mu at eta>0. Its autocorrelation density is measurable, has Haar integral1, and every interval level set is invariant under inversion. A pointwise bound kappa<=C implies rho<=C. A real nonnegative bound C gives integrability of rho.toReal^2 and integral rho.toReal^2<=C. The real value rho(1).toReal equals integral kappa.toReal^2. For the generator walk, this density is pointwise equal to the actual Haar density of P_eta*nu^(2n)*P_eta. Thus the R1789 initial bound transfers immediately, with unchanged exponent and constant, for the same family and radii.

Action identity. For any finite measure mu, the actual representation averages satisfy
  inner_R(A_mu f,h)=inner_R(f,A_(mu.inv) h),
  inner_R(f,A_(mu.inv*mu) f)=norm(A_mu f)^2.
The autocorrelation average is symmetric on the real Hilbert space underlying the complex L2 space. For norm(f)=1,
  norm(A_mu f)^2<=norm(A_(mu.inv*mu) f).
These statements use the already proved isometric action, Bochner-integrable orbits and actual convolution identity. They establish the positive-action bridge; no spectral or flattening hypothesis is hidden in it.

Scope. These are standard analytic support results, not new impossibility theorems and not a flattening theorem. They provide a rigorously symmetric object retaining both the initial density control and a large-action witness. The remaining direct contradiction and product-growth/flattening steps must still be proved.

They act by iteration of the actual bounded linear average. Put alpha=(mu*P_eta).inv*(mu*P_eta), rho_0=its canonical R1790 density, and rho_(k+1)=autocorrelationDensity(H,rho_k). Then for every k,

R1792 — NONFLATTENING TO CONTINUOUS LEVEL-PAIR ENERGY
In progress. R1792 proves that a bounded nonnegative subprobability density whose self-convolution has squared L2 mass at least tau>0 contains a pair of dyadic level sets with quantitatively large weighted Haar multiplicative energy. The low tail costs at most8a in squared energy, with factor2 on the high part, without a finite-volume support hypothesis. Choosing a=tau/16 yields at most1+log2(max(1,16C/tau)) levels and a fourth-power loss in their number. The theorem is instantiated for the actual symmetric smoothed-autocorrelation iterate rho_k when integral rho_(k+1)^2>=tau; measurability, inverse symmetry and weighted level masses are included. Relative-energy normalization, self-energy conversion, metric BSG, SL2 product growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Continuous definitions and hypotheses. Let H be a measurable group and sigma an s-finite left-, right- and inversion-invariant measure. For measurable nonnegative densities,
  (f*g)(x)=integral f(y)g(y^-1*x) dsigma(y),
  E(A,B)=integral (1_A*1_B)(x)^2 dsigma(x).
The density convolution is identified with the already defined convolution against sigma.withDensity f; its total mass is the product of masses. For inversion-symmetric f it equals the existing autocorrelation density.

Low-tail removal. If integral f<=1 and a>=0, put h=f*1_{f>=a}. Then
  integral(f*f)^2 <=8a+2 integral(h*h)^2.
The proof splits f into low and high parts. Each mixed term has total mass<=1 and pointwise bound<=a; each therefore has squared integral<=a. Two applications of the checked finite Cauchy–Schwarz bound give the displayed constants. No finite-support-volume hypothesis is used.

Dyadic extraction with an explicit cutoff. Let N>0, f(x)<a*2^N for every x, and A_i={a*2^i<=f<a*2^(i+1)}. Some i,j<N satisfy
  integral(f*f)^2 <=8a+2*N^4*((a*2^(i+1))*(a*2^(j+1)))^2*E(A_i,A_j).
The proof bounds the high part by its N-level upper envelope, expands its convolution into N^2 nonnegative terms, uses finite Cauchy–Schwarz, and selects a maximal-energy pair. If finite tau<=integral(f*f)^2 and16a<=tau, the tail is absorbed to give
  tau<=4*N^4*((a*2^(i+1))*(a*2^(j+1)))^2*E(A_i,A_j).
Every A_i is measurable; inversion symmetry of f gives inversion symmetry of A_i. The weighted mass bound (a*2^i)*sigma(A_i)<=integral f is proved.

Automatic logarithmic cutoff. For a real bound C with f<=ofReal(C), real tau>0 and ofReal(tau)<=integral(f*f)^2, take a=ofReal(tau/16). There exist N>0 and i,j<N with
  N<=1+log_2(max(1,16C/tau))
and the preceding large-energy inequality. The integer cutoff is constructed using consecutive powers of two; its logarithmic bound is proved, not assumed. This statement is valid for any measurable subprobability density in the stated group-measure setting.

Actual smoothed iterates. For any probability mu and eta>0, let rho_k be the canonical smoothedAutocorrelationIterate. The new identity rho_(k+1)=rho_k*rho_k follows from its already proved pointwise inversion symmetry. Given initial kappa_(mu,eta)<=ofReal(C), tau>0 and ofReal(tau)<=integral rho_(k+1)^2, the logarithmic extraction applies to f=rho_k. It returns i,j,N and, in the same theorem, measurability, pointwise inverse symmetry, weighted mass<=1 for both levels, and the large-energy inequality. The inherited density bound and exact mass1 are discharged from the actual construction.

R1793 — NONFLATTENING TO HIGH SELF-ENERGY WITH A CONTROLLED VOLUME WINDOW
In progress. R1793 upgrades the weighted level-pair extraction to relative Haar energy and then to one symmetric positive finite-volume level set with high self-energy. If f is a bounded symmetric probability density, U=integral f^2 and integral(f*f)^2>=theta*U for theta>0, there are N logarithmically bounded levels and one level A such that, for K=64N^4, theta/(K U)<=H(A)<=K/(theta U) and E(A,A)>=theta^2*H(A)^3/K^2. Positivity/finiteness of U and level volumes, noncommutative trace/Cauchy–Schwarz and every cancellation are checked. The result applies to the actual smoothed-autocorrelation iterates. Open/precompact regularization, continuous BSG, metric transfer, SL2 product growth/escape and strict flattening remain unproved; unconditional paid padding is incomplete.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Notation. For a measurable group with s-finite left-, right- and inversion-invariant measure H, define (f*g)(x)=integral f(y)g(y^-1 x)dH(y) and E(A,B)=integral(1_A*1_B)^2 dH. These are the actual R1792 continuous densities and energy, not finite quadruple counts.

Moment normalization. Every dyadic level A_i={a_i<=f<2a_i}, a_i=a*2^i, satisfies a_i H(A_i)<=integral f and a_i^2 H(A_i)<=integral f^2. Positive a and finite total mass give finite level volume. A measurable nonnegative density with nonzero total mass has nonzero squared mass. If aA<=1,bB<=1,a^2 A<=U,b^2 B<=U,0<U<infinity and theta U<=K a^2 b^2 E, then theta A^2 B<=K E and theta A B^2<=K E. The proof multiplies by the volume products and cancels the positive finite U.

Set-energy upper bounds and nondegeneracy. For measurable A,B,
  E(A,B)<=H(A)^2 H(B), and E(A,B)<=H(A)H(B)^2.
Positive energy forces both volumes positive. Finite volumes give finite energy. Together with the preceding relative lower bounds these imply theta H(A)<=K H(B) and theta H(B)<=K H(A).

Automatic relative level extraction. Let f be a measurable probability density, f<=ofReal(C), theta>0, and integral(f*f)^2>=theta integral f^2. Put U=integral f^2, tau=theta U, a=tau/16. There exist N>0 and i,j<N with
  N<=1+log_2(max(1,16C/tau)), K=64N^4,
  theta H(A_i)^2 H(A_j)<=K E(A_i,A_j),
  theta H(A_i)H(A_j)^2<=K E(A_i,A_j).
Both volumes are positive and finite and are comparable within factor K/theta. In addition, BOTH selected levels satisfy the stronger scale information
  theta<=K U H(A), and theta U H(A)<=K,
equivalently theta/(K U)<=H(A)<=K/(theta U). These volume bounds are derived from the original weighted inequality plus the first/second moments and the two energy upper bounds. They are not extra assumptions.

Noncommutative trace and self-energy. Associativity of the actual density convolution, inversion reversal for symmetric factors, and commutation at identity are proved by Haar change of variables and Tonelli. For symmetric measurable f,g,
  integral(f*g)^2 = integral(f*f)(g*g),
  [integral(f*g)^2]^2 <= integral(f*f)^2 integral(g*g)^2.
Thus symmetric measurable sets satisfy E(A,B)^2<=E(A,A)E(B,B). Combining both relative mixed-energy bounds with E(A,A)<=H(A)^3 and E(B,B)<=H(B)^3 yields
  theta^2 H(A)^3<=K^2 E(A,A),
  theta^2 H(B)^3<=K^2 E(B,B).
The required nonzero finite volume cancellations are explicit.

Single symmetric level. If the density f above is inversion-symmetric, one selected level A is measurable, inversion-symmetric and of positive finite volume v, with the displayed N bound, volume window, and E(A,A)>=theta^2 v^3/(4096N^8). This is the full continuous high-self-energy conclusion at this stage.

Actual iterate application. For any probability mu,eta>0 and k, initial right-smoothed density kappa_(mu,eta)<=ofReal(C), and theta>0 satisfying integral rho_(k+1)^2>=theta integral rho_k^2, the single-set result applies to f=rho_k. Measurability, symmetry, exact mass1 and the bound C come from the canonical construction. The new theorem returns its actual dyadic level, the N bound, positive finite Haar volume, both volume-window inequalities and the self-energy lower bound.

Scope. The original theorem families are still3/6 formalized. This result supports the flattening proof; it does not yet construct an approximate group, prove strict flattening or complete paid padding. Open/precompact regularization is a real missing hypothesis for the next continuous BSG step.

R1794 — OPEN PRECOMPACT HIGH-ENERGY SETS WITH CONTROLLED LOCATION AND VOLUME ERROR
In progress. R1794 closes the topological input gap between the measurable high-energy level and a symmetric nonempty open precompact set. Null-set support restriction preserves volume and energy. EXACT STATEMENTS
Write H for Haar measure, (f*g)(x)=integral f(y)g(y^-1 x)dH(y), and E(A,B)=integral(1_A*1_B)^2. Box(R) means determinant-one real2x2 matrices with all entry absolute values at most R.

Null-set invariance: on a measurable group with right- and inversion-invariant measure, a.e.-equal convolution factors give equal convolutions at EVERY point. Thus a.e.-equal sets have equal energy. Energy is monotone under inclusion of both sets. A positive-threshold dyadic level of a function vanishing a.e. outside S agrees a.e. with its intersection with S.

General regularization: in a Hausdorff topological group with outer-regular measure, suppose A is symmetric, 0<measure(A)<infinity, and A is inside open W inside compact K. For every epsilon>0 there is symmetric nonempty open O with A subset O subset W, compact closure inside K, and measure(A)<=measure(O)<=measure(A)+epsilon. Neither W nor K must be symmetric. Intersect an outer-regular open approximation with W and its inverse. The factor-two corollary uses epsilon=measure(A).

SL2 specialization: if A is symmetric of positive finite Haar volume v and A intersect Box(R) agrees a.e. with A, then for every epsilon>0 there is symmetric nonempty open O containing A intersect Box(R), with compact closure inside Box(R+1), v<=H(O)<=v+epsilon, and E(O,O)>=E(A,A). Strict entry boxes supply the open neighborhood; existing closed entry boxes supply compactness. Null outliers are removed before literal support claims.

Actual iterate: let mu be a probability measure, eta>0, k natural, and mu*P_eta supported a.e. in Box(B). Assume kappa<=C, theta>0, and integral rho_(k+1)^2>=theta integral rho_k^2. R1795 — CONTINUOUS POPULAR PRODUCTS AND THE ACTUAL DENSE PAIR RELATION
In progress. R1795 proves that an open set O of finite positive Haar volume w, bounded in Box(Q), with E(O,O)>=w^3/L for positive finite L, has the explicit popular-product region C={1_O*1_O>w/(2L)}. It is nonempty open precompact, its closure lies in Box(2Q^2), H(C)<=2Lw, and the actual pairs in O x O with product in C have measure at least w^2/(2L). Lower semicontinuity follows directly from Fatou; product mass equals pair measure by a proved convolution-of-restrictions identity. The actual smoothed nonflattening iterates give this relation with L=8(64N^4)^2/theta^2 and prove L>=1 and finite, preserving the dyadic level, volume window and arbitrary small enlargement error. Weak BSG selection, small-product/approximate-group extraction, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Write H for Haar measure, F=1_A*1_B with the previously defined continuous convolution, and E(A,B)=integral F^2.

Topology and support. In a first-countable parameter space, an integral of nonnegative functions which are lower semicontinuous in the parameter and measurable in the integration variable is lower semicontinuous, by Fatou. Consequently 1_A*1_B is lower semicontinuous for measurable A and open B in the stated topological measurable group. The strict popularProductSet(H,A,B,t)={F>t} is open. The density is zero outside A*B, so every such strict superlevel lies in A*B. These results do not require symmetry or a discrete model.

Exact pair identity. For measurable A,B,C and s-finite left-invariant H, (H restricted to A)*(H restricted to B)=H.withDensity(1_A*1_B), hence
  integral_C (1_A*1_B) = (H x H){(a,b):a in A,b in B,ab in C}.

Scalar bounds. Integral F=H(A)H(B), F<=H(A), and t H({F>t})<=H(A)H(B). Splitting at t gives
  E(A,B)<=t H(A)H(B)+H(A) integral_{F>t} F.
For measurable A with 0<w=H(A)<infinity, 0<L<infinity, and w^3<=L E(A,A), put t=w/(2L), C={1_A*1_A>t}. Then
  H(C)<=2Lw, and w^2<=2L integral_C (1_A*1_A).
All finite nonzero cancellations are explicit; L>=1 is not needed as an input to this scalar theorem.

Geometry. For SL2(R), if O is open, contained in Box(Q), has positive finite volume w and the preceding self-energy bound, C is nonempty open with positive finite volume, compact closure inside Box(2Q^2), and
  H(C)<=2Lw,
  (H x H){(a,b) in O x O:ab in C}>=w^2/(2L).

Actual nonflattening iterates. Under the R1794 hypotheses on mu,eta,k,theta,initial density bound and base smoothed support Box(B), the same dyadic level and open set O produce the preceding C. The theorem keeps N<=1+log2(max(1,16M/(theta U))), R=(4B^2)^(2^k), Q=R+1, K0=64N^4, all previous O volume bounds and arbitrary relative enlargement error delta. It sets L=8K0^2/theta^2=32768N^8/theta^2, proves 1<=L<infinity, and supplies the full geometry and pair-measure conclusion. This is genuine weak-BSG input, not a theorem assuming such a relation.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Weighted selection. For a measure nu of positive finite total mass, measurable f>=0, any nonnegative g, positive finite epsilon,z, and an a.e.-full allowed set T, if integral f>=4z nu(Y) and integral g<=2epsilon z nu(Y), there exists y in T with f(y)>z and g(y)<epsilon f(y). Otherwise epsilon f<=epsilon z+g a.e.; integrating and cancelling a positive finite common factor gives 4<=3. No subtraction or measurability assumption on g is needed.

Incidence selection. For finite measures mu,nu of positive mass, measurable E subset X x Y, positive finite K,epsilon, and mu(X)nu(Y)<=K (mu x nu)(E), put c(x,x')=integral 1_E(x,y)1_E(x',y) dnu(y) and t=epsilon nu(Y)/(2K^2). There is an allowed y whose fiber mass s satisfies mu(X)^2<4K^2 s^2 and whose fiber-pair measure with c<=t is <epsilon s^2. The proof derives the second-moment lower bound by Cauchy–Schwarz, and the integrated low-codegree count by Tonelli. All normalizations and cancellations are checked. Product relations are obtained by restricting the actual Haar measures to A and B, with exact fiber and bad-pair measure identities.

Quotient comparison. For left-invariant H,
  (1_C*1_(C^-1))(d)=integral 1_C(dx)1_C(x)dH(x).
The B-restricted common-neighbor count of a,a' is at most this value at d=aa'^-1. Thus low membership in the popular quotient region implies low codegree. Markov and inversion invariance give t H(D)<=H(C)^2.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Strict degree trimming. For a measure mu of finite total mass s and measurable f>=0, suppose f(x)+g(x)=s for every x, 0<r<=s and 2 integral g<=r*s. Then the strict good set T={x:s-r<f(x)} has mu(T)>=s/2 and g(x)<r throughout T. If f is lower semicontinuous, T is open. The proof uses the complementary degree and finite additive/multiplicative cancellation; g need not be measurable for the stated lemma. Row-degree integrals equal the actual pair measure, including for measures restricted to input sets.

Noncommutative representation identity. For left- and inversion-invariant Haar measure,
  (1_D*1_C)(ab)=integral 1_D(a*x^-1)1_C(x*b)dH(x).
The S-restricted C-neighbor degree of b is bounded above by this density plus the S-restricted bad quotient degree of a. This keeps the order (a*x^-1)(x*b)=ab exact.

Rich-row selection. If open O,C have 0<w=H(O)<infinity and product-pair mass at least w^2/(2L), 0<L<infinity, the open A_hi={a in O:integral_O 1_C(ab)>w/(4L)} has positive measure, w<=4L H(A_hi), and retained pair mass at least H(A_hi)*w/(4L).

Suppose every a in S has O-neighbor degree >H(O)/(4L), and 64L times the exceptional quotient-pair measure in S x S is at most H(S)^2. Then there exist open A subset S and B subset O such that H(S)<=2H(A), H(O)<=8L H(B), and H(S)H(AB)<=16L H(D)H(C). A is a strict superlevel of the good quotient degree; B is a strict column-degree superlevel. Every ab in AB has convolution density >H(S)/(16L), so Markov controls the entire product, not only almost every pair.

Full self-energy BSG. Let H be Haar measure on SL2(R), O open with O subset Box(Q), w=H(O)>0, 1<=L<infinity and w^3<=L E(O,O). Then there exist open A,B subset O with positive finite Haar volume,
  w<=64 L^2 H(A),
  w<=8 L H(B),
  H(AB)<=8388608 L^9 w.
The closures of A and B are compact in Box(Q). The closure of AB is compact in Box(2Q^2). Here Box(Q) bounds the absolute value of every matrix entry by Q. The proof composes R1795 popular products, rich-row selection, R1796 weak BSG with K=4L and epsilon=1/(64L), and the whole-product trim. Intermediate bounds are w<=32L^2 H(S) and H(D)<=8192L^5 w. Every cancellation is on a proved finite positive factor.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Ruzsa and energy bounds. For the stated measurable sets and invariant Haar measure,
 H(AA^-1)H(B)<=H(AB)^2,
 (H(A)H(B))^2<=E(A,B)H(AB).
The first bound counts common B-neighbors of each quotient a*a'^-1 through AB; the second is Cauchy-Schwarz on the actual product support. They apply to actual measures, including extended nonnegative values; later cancellations explicitly require finite positive factors.

Inverse-energy trace. For arbitrary measurable A, without assuming A=A^-1,
 E(A,A^-1)=E(A^-1,A).
The proof reuses convolution associativity, commutativity at the identity and the inverse-at-identity square-integral formula. The convolution (1_(A^-1)*1_A)(x) equals the autocorrelation integral integral 1_A(y)1_A(y*x)dH(y), and is invariant under x->x^-1.

Popular-overlap volume. Suppose 0<H(A)<infinity, 0<K<infinity and H(AA^-1)<=K H(A). Set t=H(A)/(2K) and T={x:(1_(A^-1)*1_A)(x)>t}. Then H(A)<=2K H(T) and H(T)<=2K H(A). The energy lower bound and strict popular-tail estimate give the lower volume bound; Markov gives the upper bound.

All sandwich powers. Let C=AA^-1 and define I_0=1_C, I_(n+1)=1_C*I_n. Then integral I_n=H(C)^(n+1). If every s in T has overlap at least t, then I_n(a*s*b^-1)>=t^n for all a,b in A and s in T^n. In the induction, the substitution y=a*u^-1 restricts u to those with u and u*s_1 in A; the remaining product is handled by the preceding iterate. Integrating gives
 t^n H(A*T^n*A^-1)<=H(AA^-1)^(n+1).
For the actual popular region this implies, for every n>=0,
 H(A*T^n*A^-1)<=2^n K^(2n+1)H(A).

SL2 core. For open A subset Box(Q), H(A)>0, finite K>=1 and H(AA^-1)<=K H(A), this T contains1, is open and inversion-symmetric, has positive finite volume and compact closure in Box(2Q^2). The volume comparisons above hold, and
 H(A*T)<=2K^3 H(A),
 H(T^3)<=16K^8 H(T).
No tripling hypothesis was assumed; it follows from the constructed core and sandwich representations.

Direct self-energy composition. If open O subset Box(Q), w=H(O)>0, finite L>=1 and w^3<=L E(O,O), put K=2^55 L^21. There are A subset O and T satisfying all core conclusions, with A open of positive finite volume and compact closure in Box(Q),
 w<=64L^2 H(A), H(AA^-1)<=K H(A),

The quotient bound follows from R1797's small-product subsets and the new Ruzsa inequality. All polynomial constants and finite cancellations are checked.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Finite Haar packing. For a group G with measurable multiplication and left-invariant measure H, let T be measurable with 0<H(T)<infinity. If F is a finite subset of B and its translates x*T are pairwise disjoint, card(F) H(T)<=H(B*T). If H(B*T)<=R H(T) with finite R, there exists a finite F subset B with card(F)<=R and B subset F*T*T^-1. The proof constructs a maximum-cardinality finite packing from a bounded set of natural cardinalities; maximality implies the covering.

Large overlap from a finite cover. For any measure H on a group, nonempty A subset O and a finite F with A subset F*U, there exists x in F such that H(A)<=card(F) H(O intersect x*U). This uses finite-union subadditivity and a finite maximum; it does not assume a large overlap as input.

Symmetric cube. If T is measurable, contains1, T^-1=T, has positive finite Haar volume, and H(T^7)<=R H(T) with R finite, there exists a finite symmetric Y subset (T^3)^2 with card(Y)<=2R and (T^3)^2 subset Y*T^3. Consequently T^3 satisfies mathlib's IsApproximateSubgroup (2R).toReal predicate. The stronger symmetric witness inside the square is also retained explicitly. Construct X by packing translates x*T for x in T^6 and set Y=X union X^-1.

The proof takes the R1798 actual core T and sets U=T^3. Its n=7 sandwich bound gives H(T^7)<=256K^16 H(T), so the finite cube theorem applies. A second packing covers A and selects the translate. Every loss and matrix-entry bound is checked in Lean.

In progress. R1801 proves that every actual autocorrelation iterate retains a rightmost original smoothing kernel. EXACT STATEMENTS
Actual endpoint smoothing. For mu probability, eta>0 and every natural k, there exists a probability measure nu such that H.withDensity(rho_k)=nu*P_eta. Explicitly, set sigma=mu*P_eta, alpha=sigma.inv*sigma, beta=alpha^(2^k-1), and nu=(beta*sigma.inv)*mu. The proof uses the positive exponent, the right-successor convolution-power identity and associativity. No factors are commuted and no inversion symmetry of P_eta is required.

Haar smoothing average. For a group with measurable multiplication, left-invariant SFinite measure H, measurable Z and H(S)>0,
 (nu*(H(S)^-1 H|S))(Z)=H(S)^-1 integral H(Z intersect g*S)dnu(g).
If nu is a probability measure, H(S)<infinity, 0<p<infinity and p is at most that smoothed probability, there exists g with
 p H(S)<=2H(Z intersect g*S).
The proof is an averaging contradiction with all finite-positive cancellations explicit.

Finite local packing. A finite left cover B subset F*U implies H(B)<=card(F)H(U). If T is measurable, T subset U, H(U)<infinity, c finite, a>0, a<=2H(T), and H(U^2)<=cH(U), then an actual finite F subset U satisfies
 card(F)*a<=2cH(U), U subset F*T*T^-1.
This reuses the previously checked maximal finite-packing construction.

SL2 local geometry. If Q>0, 0<eta<=1, U subset Box(Q), and T=U intersect z*Ball(eta) is nonempty, then
 T*T^-1 subset Ball(64Q^2 eta).
The common translated ball bounds z by Box(4Q), gives entry differences <16Q eta, and the reused inverse-multiplication bound controls the quotient. The auxiliary strict right-quotient lemma uses the maximum of four entry differences and the existing inversion invariance of the identity ball.

Concrete smoothing cover. For a probability nu, 0<eta<=1, Q>0, measurable U subset Box(Q) of finite Haar volume, finite Y with U^2 subset Y*U and card(Y)<=c<infinity, and 0<p<infinity with p<=(nu*P_eta)(x*U), there exists F finite subset U such that

EXACT STATEMENTS
Free-group centralizers and powers. For any alphabet, the centralizer of a nonidentity element of FreeGroup(alpha) is cyclic. The proof reuses the native index-of-letter formulas and Nielsen--Schreier: a nonidentity central word forces a free basis to have exactly one generator. For every z!=1 and integer n, |n|<=norm(z^n), by the native cyclic reduction formula. No centralizer, commutativity or word-power bound is left as an assumption.

Short-word counts. A finite subset F of a cyclic subgroup, all of whose reduced words have norm<=L, has |F|<=2L+1. The same bound holds for a finite subset of the centralizer of any nontrivial word, and for any pairwise-commuting finite word set of radius L.

Quadratic exceptional bound. Let F be any finite word set of norm<=L, and let a!=1 have norm<=L; a need not belong to F. If
 [[a,x],[a,y]]=1 for every x,y in F,
then
 |F|<=(8L+1)(4L+1).
Here [u,v]=u*v*u^-1*v^-1. The image of x -> [a,x] is pairwise commuting at radius4L, so has size<=8L+1. Each fiber, translated by one representative, lies in the centralizer of a at radius2L, so has size<=4L+1. Consequently, if |F|>(8L+1)(4L+1), there exist a,x,y in F with [[a,x],[a,y]]!=1 and norm([[a,x],[a,y]])<=16L. A nonidentity a in F is derived, not assumed.

Uniform scale threshold. For EVERY tau>0 there is J such that for all j>=J and L<=2j,
 (8L+1)(4L+1)<((1/4)^j)^(-tau).
This is proved using the native quadratic-over-exponential limit. Thus any word set of radius L<=2j with cardinality at least that power contains the stated nontrivial bicommutator. J depends only on tau, not the alphabet, free representation or later word set.

 |eval(B)_(i0,j0)-I_(i0,j0)|>=1/D_r^(32t).
The explicit coefficient budgets of the profile theorem remain; no new counting or noncommutativity premise is introduced. The scale cutoff is fixed before all r,g,j,ell,i and profiles.

Rational arithmetic. If a,x,y each have denominator D, their commutators have denominator D^4 and their bicommutator has denominator D^16. A nontrivial bicommutator therefore differs from identity in an ORIGINAL-coordinate entry by at least1/D^16. This is proved directly from existing denominator multiplication/inversion and rational separation. No arbitrary change of basis is claimed to preserve it.

R1812 — BASIS-INVARIANT TRACE CERTIFICATE FOR THE ACTUAL WORD FAMILY
In progress. R1812 proves that any nonidentity SL2 bicommutator B=[[a,x],[a,y]] has tr(Bg)!=tr(g) for some g in {I,a,x,y}, over every field. The trace2 case is proved by explicit simultaneous triangularization from the vanishing tests, followed by the triangular bicommutator identity. If a,x,y have common rational denominator D>0, the trace difference has magnitude at least D^(-17). The SAME witness works after EVERY invertible complex change of basis, with no condition-number assumption. Composition with R1811 retains all actual profile outputs and supplies a word v in {1,a,x,y} intersect F with trace gap at least D_r^(-34t), uniformly over complex bases. Quantitative off-diagonal-product escape, its small scale exponent, product growth, strict flattening, unconditional gap and paid padding remain. No new transposition bound.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Triangular calculation. For any field K, upper triangular matrices a,x in SL2(K) have upper-unitriangular commutator. Two upper-unitriangular SL2 matrices commute. Hence three simultaneously upper triangular, or simultaneously lower triangular, SL2 matrices have [[a,x],[a,y]]=I. The lower case follows by an explicit determinant-one rotation and the native conjugation automorphism.

Four trace tests. For every field K and a,x,y in SL2(K), set B=[[a,x],[a,y]]. If B!=I, then there is g in {I,a,x,y} with tr(Bg)!=tr(g). No characteristic, diagonalizability, spectral-gap, or trace(B)!=2 assumption is imposed. If tr(B)=2 and all three remaining tests vanish, the entry equations p=B00-1,q=B01,r=B10 give p^2+qr=0. If q=0, p=0 and r!=0 force a,x,y lower triangular. Otherwise the same explicit shear with lower entry p/q makes them upper triangular. In either case their bicommutator is I, a contradiction. This is an exact field-algebra proof.

Arithmetic and conjugation. If a real SL2 matrix has common rational denominator D, then D times its trace is an integer. Two unequal such traces differ by at least1/D when D>0. If a,x,y have denominator D and B!=I, the four-test witness g satisfies |tr(Bg)-tr(g)|>=1/D^17, because B has denominator D^16 and Bg and g can both be placed over denominator D^17. For EVERY invertible complex matrix P, the magnitude of tr(P(Bg)P^-1)-tr(PgP^-1) is exactly the original absolute real trace difference. Entrywise real-to-complex embedding is explicit in Lean. No transformed matrix entry is assumed rational, and P need not be unitary or well-conditioned.

Word-family transfer. For any monoid homomorphism f from a free group into real SL2, a finite word family F containing1, common denominator D for all f(F), and a,x,y in F with f(B)!=I, there is a word v in F and in {1,a,x,y} such that the same lower bound1/D^17 holds for the complex-conjugated trace difference of f(Bv) and f(v), for ALL invertible complex P. Injectivity is not required in this transfer lemma because nontriviality of f(B) is explicit.

Actual localized profile. The fixed absolute threshold J and ALL hypotheses and outputs of R1811 are retained: actual u,F;1 in F; every word length<=2t, denominator D_r^(2t), common conjugates in A^2; cardinality>=eta^(-1/122880); and actual a,x,y with nontrivial free and represented B, norm(B)<=32t and original-coordinate entry gap>=D_r^(-32t). In addition there is v in F intersect {1,a,x,y} such that for every invertible complex P,
 |tr(P eval(Bv) P^-1)-tr(P eval(v) P^-1)| >= D_r^(-34t).
Here eta=(1/4)^j,t=initialWalkLength(r,j),A=U^2 intersect Ball(alpha). The same v precedes the universal P quantifier. The old profile theorem is reused, not reproved; no new algebraic-certificate premise is added.

R1813 — QUANTITATIVE COMPLEX-BASIS ESCAPE IN THE ACTUAL A^4
In progress. R1813 converts the verified trace certificate into an explicit off-diagonal-product lower bound, without any condition-number assumption. The proof supplies diagonal bounds, finite-family rescaling, exact upper-triangular SL2 approximants, inverse-error preservation, and a sixteen-factor product perturbation estimate. For a finite complex SL2 family with traces bounded by T and individual/pair-product off-diagonal products bounded by epsilon, its bicommutator trace tests are bounded by2^43*(T+2)^21*epsilon under the stated smallness conditions. The contrapositive gives escape in S union S*S. For common-denominator rational matrices whose common real conjugates lie in A^2 with A in entry-box2, escape is in the actual A^4 after EVERY invertible complex basis change. Composed with the actual profile, the lower bound is min(1/(32*18^4),D_r^(-34t)/(2^44*18^21)). Every prior word/cardinality/trace output and the fixed cutoff are retained. The requested small eta exponent, product growth, strict flattening, unconditional gap and paid padding remain. No new transposition bound.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Diagonal bounds. If g is in SL2(C), T>=0, |tr(g)|<=T and |g01*g10|<=epsilon<=1/2, then both diagonal magnitudes are at most T+2 and at least1/(2(T+2)). The determinant identity and the norm inequality for a^2=a(a+d)-ad supply the upper bound; |ad|>=1/2 supplies the lower bound.

Finite-family normalization. The exact map (a,b;c,d) -> (a,b/z;zc,d), z!=0, is proved to be an SL2 homomorphism preserving trace and the off-diagonal product. For a finite family with some nonzero upper-right entry, an actual maximum selects z so all upper-right magnitudes are at most1 and one equals1. If diagonal magnitudes are at most M>=1 and the lower diagonal bounds hold, small off-diagonal products for u,x,ux force |x10|<=16*M^4*epsilon. The proof expands the two-factor product and uses the maximal upper-right entry. No norm bound on the rescaling parameter is imposed. The zero-maximum case is handled separately by the exact lower-triangular bicommutator identity.

Exact triangular approximants. Under the normalized bounds and16*M^4*epsilon<=1, each matrix g has an explicit upper-triangular SL2 approximant (g00,g01;0,1/g00). Every entry of both matrices is bounded by2M; every entrywise difference is at most16*M^4*epsilon. Nonvanishing of g00 is derived from the diagonal lower bound, not assumed. The approximant has determinant1 exactly.

Product and inverse errors. Entrywise multiplication costs a factor2. For a list of n matrix pairs with entries bounded by R>=1 and paired entry differences bounded by delta>=0, the product-entry difference is at most n*(2R)^n*delta. In SL2, inversion preserves the entry bounds and entry differences by the explicit adjugate formula. Expanding [[a,x],[a,y]] into its actual16 factors gives entry error<=16*(2R)^16*delta. For upper-triangular comparison matrices, their bicommutator is exactlyI, so each trace test against a matrix with entries bounded by R has magnitude<=64*R*(2R)^16*delta.

Quantitative finite-family implication. Let S be any finite subset of SL2(C), with |tr(h)|<=T for every h in S, T>=0. Suppose0<=epsilon<=1/2,16*(T+2)^4*epsilon<=1, and |h01*h10|<=epsilon for every h in S and every product of two members of S. For ALL a,x,y,g in S,
 |tr([[a,x],[a,y]]g)-tr(g)| <=2^43*(T+2)^21*epsilon.
Every normalization and triangular approximation needed for this conclusion is constructed by the proof. It is not an abstract perturbation hypothesis.

Explicit contrapositive. If the same trace test is at least L>0, some h in S union S*S satisfies
 |h01*h10| >= min(1/(32*(T+2)^4),L/(2^44*(T+2)^21)).
Only individual matrices and TWO-factor products occur in the escape conclusion, although the test itself uses a16-factor bicommutator.

Rational family and exact A^4. Suppose D>0,1 in A,A contained in real entry-box2, a finite rational family F containsI and every member has denominator D, and one common real conjugation u^-1 F u lies in A^2. If a,x,y in F have nontrivial bicommutator, then for EVERY invertible complex matrix P there is a real h in A^4 such that
 |(P h P^-1)01*(P h P^-1)10| >=min(1/(32*18^4),D^(-17)/(2^44*18^21)).
The embedding into complex matrices is explicit. Trace bound16 is derived from A^2 contained in entry-box8; no extra trace assumption is added. The h belongs to the original A^4, not a larger power. It may depend on P. Conjugation is implemented as an actual SL2 homomorphism using native determinant and trace invariance.

In progress. R1815 proves a quantitative four-matrix spanning certificate using the existing rational trace witness. EXACT STATEMENTS
Exact coordinate identities. pairSpanMatrix(a,b) is the4-by4 matrix whose columns are the row-major coordinates of I,a,b,ab. For arbitrary2-by2 matrices over a field,
 det(pairSpanMatrix(a,b)) = det(ab-ba)
 =4det(a)det(b)-tr(a)^2det(b)-tr(b)^2det(a)-tr(ab)^2+tr(a)tr(b)tr(ab).
For a,b in SL2, this equals2-tr([a,b]). If tr(a)=2, it equals-(tr(ab)-tr(b))^2. Its determinant is invariant under simultaneous SL2 conjugation. These are exact field identities; no spectral or diagonalizability hypothesis is used.

Rational witness. Let a,x,y lie in the real common-denominator carrier D>0 and B=[[a,x],[a,y]]!=I. There are p,q with det(pairSpanMatrix(p,q)) of absolute value at least D^(-34). More precisely, either p=[a,x],q=[a,y], or p=B and q is one of I,a,x,y. If tr(B)!=2, use the first pair, the identity2-tr(B), and the denominator-D^16 trace separation, which is at least D^(-34). If tr(B)=2, use the existing trace-test witness q with |tr(Bq)-tr(q)|>=D^(-17), and square it using the second identity. The trace2 case is handled directly, including nonidentity unipotents.
