R1816 — QUANTITATIVE THREE-TRACE COVERING
In progress. R1816 proves a quantitative projection and covering theorem on the real determinant-one surface. For a bounded set A with |x00|>=1/2 and four bounded SL2 matrices whose coordinate determinant has magnitude at least d>0, a product of three actual scalar trace covering numbers controls the actual Frobenius covering number of A. With 0<d<=1 the loss is explicit C(M)/d^7. The proof uses exact determinant identities, quantitative adjugate bounds, small patches, and finite covering refinements. It keeps three trace factors, preserving the dimension-three exponent needed downstream. Four new modules add22 theorems and3 definitions. Instantiation with the full fixed rational family remains next; product growth and paid padding are unfinished. No new transposition bound, literature novelty, or completed fourth original family is asserted.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Quantitative linear algebra. MatrixFourBounds proves determinant bounds6M^3 and24M^4 for3-by3 and4-by4 real matrices with entries bounded by M, an adjugate entry bound24M^4 for M>=1, and the inverse estimate ||v||_infinity<=96M^4 Y/d when |det T|>=d>0 and all coordinates of Tv have magnitude<=Y. If a normal vector has a coordinate of magnitude>=1/2, replacing some row of T by that normal leaves determinant magnitude>=d/(8M).

Local geometry. Write coords(x)=(x00,x01,x10,x11) and normal(z)=(z11,-z10,-z01,z00). For x,y on the same determinant level within entrywise radius r of z, the exact quadratic identity gives |normal(z) dot(coords(x)-coords(y))|<=4r||coords(x)-coords(y)||_infinity. If the four trace rows T_i=normal(coords(g_i)) have entries bounded by M>=1 and |det T|>=d>0, and z has entries bounded by M and |z00|>=1/2, then for6144M^5r<=d one can omit a single row i, chosen before x,y, such that the three remaining trace differences bounded by t imply Frobenius distance(x,y)<=3072M^5 t/d throughout the determinant-one patch. This uses an exact remainder estimate and absorption, not an assumed inverse-function theorem.

Trace identities. The scalar measurement is exactly f_i(x)=tr(g_i^(-1)x). The determinant of its four-row frame equals the determinant of the four row-major matrix-coordinate columns. In particular the frame for I,p,q,pq has determinant equal to the already verified pairSpanMatrix determinant, so the existing rational spanning certificate has the correct orientation and normalization.

Finite covers. A general three-measurement reconstruction estimate with constant C yields a finite eta-cover from finite scalar eta-covers F_0,F_1,F_2, with cardinality at most product|F_i| times binCount(eta,eta/(C+1))^3. The bin count is at most2C+3. Applying this patchwise and taking the largest of the four possible triple products gives a global finite cover with loss (2(M+1)/r+1)^4*(6144M^5/d+3)^3. Representatives are taken from A; the argument also handles empty A.

Native global theorem. Let A be ANY subset of SL2(R); let g_0,...,g_3 be in SL2(R). Suppose every entry of A and all g_i has magnitude<=M, M>=1, and every x in A satisfies |x00|>=1/2. Let0<d<=1 be no greater than the absolute determinant of the four coordinate columns, and let eta>0. Then there is an omitted index i such that
 N_eta(A) <= C(M)/d^7 * product_(j!=i) N_eta({tr(g_j^(-1)x):x in A}),
 C(M)=(12288(M+1)M^5+1)^4*(6144M^5+3)^3.
Here the left side is the actual ambient Frobenius external covering number and the scalar side uses the ordinary real metric; both are finite. No finite-cover or precompactness premise is hidden: the scalar images are bounded by4M^2, minimal finite covers are attained, and the matrix cover is then constructed. The proved inequality uses the real-valued coercions of the native covering numbers, with their finiteness established before conversion. The polynomial loss follows by choosing r=d/(6144M^5).

Scope. This is a supporting projection theorem for the product-growth route to paid padding. Selecting a single large trace factor and composing with the actual fixed rational family remain next. Four new modules add22 theorems and3 definitions; no existing mathematical module is modified. No literature novelty claim is made.

R1818 — QUANTITATIVE EXACT COMMUTING APPROXIMANTS
In progress. R1818 proves a direct quantitative projection to the real commuting algebra span{I,g}, restores determinant one by positive scalar normalization, and supplies whole families of pairwise commuting SL2 approximants. If g lies in the Frobenius identity ball of radius alpha<=1/2 and dist(g,I)>=r>0, a family with entries bounded by B>=1 and entrywise commutator error<=epsilon has such approximants with Frobenius error<=400B^2*epsilon/r, provided96B*epsilon<=r. No eigenvalue separation, diagonalization or conditioned eigenbasis is required. Three new modules add14 theorems and2 definitions. EXACT STATEMENTS
Commuting algebra. Define scalarAffine(g,s,t)=sI+t*g for a real2-by2 matrix g and real scalars s,t. Any two such matrices commute. Scalar multiplication preserves this form. Define noncentralCoordinates(g)=(g00-g11,g01,g10). If one of these coordinates has magnitude>=rho>0 and all entries of the matrix commutator g*x-x*g have magnitude<=epsilon, epsilon>=0, then there are s,t such that every entry of x-scalarAffine(g,s,t) has magnitude<=epsilon/rho. The proof reduces the three coordinates to a scalar multiple using one pivot and the three exact cross-product identities. No determinant or spectral hypothesis is needed for this projection.

Determinant correction. If x is in SL2(R), its entries are bounded by B>=1, and y is entrywise within delta>=0 of x, then |det(y)-1|<=4B*delta+2delta^2. If12B*delta<=1, this is at most6B*delta<=1/2, so det(y)>=1/2. The positive scalar r=1/sqrt(det(y)) is at most2, det(r*y)=1, and x-r*y has entry error<=25B^2*delta. The inverse-square-root error is proved directly from the square identity; no normalization theorem is assumed.

Single and family approximants. Under12B*(epsilon/rho)<=1, combine the preceding statements to produce y in SL2(R) in span{I,g}, with entry error<=25B^2*epsilon/rho and Frobenius distance<=50B^2*epsilon/rho. For ANY set A of bounded real SL2 matrices satisfying the same commutator bound against this fixed g, there is a function f:A->SL2(R) with these pointwise bounds and with f(x),f(y) commuting for every pair. Each image is explicitly represented as sI+t*g. No finiteness, measurability, diagonalizability or injectivity of the approximation map is asserted or required.

Geometric pivot. If g belongs to the actual Frobenius identity ball of radius0<alpha<=1/2 and all noncentral coordinates have magnitude<=theta, then dist_F(g,I)<=8theta. This uses det(g)=1, g00>=1/2 and the bounded near-identity entries. Consequently r<=dist_F(g,I) implies that some noncentral coordinate has magnitude>=r/8. This works for nonidentity unipotents; distance from identity is never converted into an unjustified eigenvalue gap.

Combined theorem. Let0<alpha<=1/2 and g in SL2(R) lie in that identity ball. Suppose0<r<=dist_F(g,I). Let A be ANY set in SL2(R) whose entries are bounded by B>=1 and whose commutators g*x-x*g have every entry bounded by epsilon>=0. If96B*epsilon<=r, there is f:A->SL2(R) such that all f(x) commute pairwise, each f(x) lies in span{I,g}, every entry of x-f(x) has magnitude<=200B^2*epsilon/r, and dist_F(x,f(x))<=400B^2*epsilon/r. This is exists_near_identity_commuting_approximants. The matrix g itself remains fixed throughout the entire family.

R1819 — ACTUAL LARGE CONJUGACY FIBERS AND COVERING TRANSFER
In progress. R1819 derives the commutator error from an actual normalized conjugacy fiber, transfers external covers through its noninjective commuting approximation, and selects a fiber with at least the average covering complexity. Given a finite cover F of the conjugacy orbit of a bounded nonempty set A, the theorem produces a nonempty fiber and exact pairwise commuting SL2 matrices near A^-1*A, with an explicit lower covering bound in terms of N_eta(A), |F| and the approximation radius. EXACT STATEMENTS
Actual conjugacy identity. For real SL2 matrices g,x0,x and y=x0^-1*x,
 y*g-g*y = x0^-1*((x*g*x^-1)-(x0*g*x0^-1))*x.
This is proved for actual coerced matrices from the group identity. If x0 and x have entries bounded by B>=0 and their conjugates of g have Frobenius distance<=delta, every entry of y*g-g*y has magnitude<=4B^2*delta. Matrix inversion preserves the SL2 entry bound; native Frobenius multiplication supplies the distortion. The normalized y has entries bounded by2B^2.

Commuting approximation for a fiber. Suppose g is in the Frobenius identity ball of radius0<alpha<=1/2 and dist_F(g,I)>=r>0. Suppose A has entries bounded by B>=1, x0 belongs to A, every conjugate x*g*x^-1 for x in A is within delta>=0 of x0*g*x0^-1, and768B^4*delta<=r. There is f:A->SL2(R), with every f(x) in span{I,g}, all f(x) commuting pairwise, x0^-1*x in A^-1*A, and dist_F(x0^-1*x,f(x))<=6400B^6*delta/r. This composes the actual commutator bound with R1818 rather than assuming near commutation.

Native covering transfer. For arbitrary maps a,b:X->Mat2(R), a map L on matrices and nonnegative Q,D,K, suppose b has entries bounded by Q and dist(a(x),L(c))<=D+K*dist(b(x),c) for all x,c. At every eta>0 both covering numbers are finite and
 N_eta(range(a)) <= (4(D+K*eta)/eta+1)^4 * N_eta(range(b)).
The proof attains a minimal finite cover of range(b), maps its centers by L, and refines the resulting coordinate patches at eta/2. It does not assume injectivity or substitute cardinality for a covering number. In particular, if f:A->SL2(R) approximates x0^-1*x within R>=0 and x0,A have entries bounded by B>=1, then
 N_eta(A) <= (8B(R+eta)/eta+1)^4 * N_eta(range(f)).
The original set uses the ambient Frobenius matrix embedding, and range(f) uses the same metric. Finiteness is derived from the bounds and the constructed covers.

Finite-cover selection. In any pseudo-emetric space, if A is covered by finitely many pieces S_i indexed by a nonempty finite F and each N_eta(S_i) is finite, then some i in F satisfies N_eta(A)<=|F|*N_eta(S_i). The proof takes minimal external covers of the pieces, unions them and selects a maximal cardinality. The radius is unchanged.

Combined actual large fiber. Let A be a nonempty entry-bounded subset of real SL2 with B>=1. Let g be in the identity ball0<alpha<=1/2 with dist_F(g,I)>=r>0. Let F be a finite set of ambient matrix centers covering all x*g*x^-1, x in A, within radius delta>=0. Suppose1536B^4*delta<=r. For every eta>0 there is c in F, a nonempty actual fiber S={x in A:dist_F(x*g*x^-1,c)<=delta}, x0 in S, and f:S->SL2(R), with all f(x) pairwise commuting and in span{I,g}. Each x0^-1*x lies in A^-1*A and is within
 R=12800B^6*delta/r
of f(x). With V=range(f), both covering numbers are finite and
 N_eta(A) <= |F|*(8B(R+eta)/eta+1)^4*N_eta(V).
The finite cover is filtered to nonempty fibers before selection, and the factor from that filter is bounded by the original |F|. No injectivity of f is assumed. The conjugacy-cover radius delta and the final covering radius eta remain independent.

R1820 — TRACE-DRIVEN MIXED-PRODUCT COMMUTING EXTRACTION
In progress. R1820 selects a conjugacy orbit with a small cover by counting disjoint trace buckets, controls the number of separated traces by the native scalar covering number, and composes these with the actual large-fiber approximation. The resulting theorem uses an independent trace candidate set D and conjugating set A, so A may contain the identity. It produces exact pairwise commuting real SL2 matrices near A^-1*A, and bounds their covering complexity using N_eta(tr D), N_eta(A) and N_eta(A*D*A^-1), with explicit loss polynomial in the inverse distance of D from the identity. Three new modules add8 theorems and no definitions; existing mathematical modules are unchanged. Suitable candidates for the actual walk profile, product growth and paid padding remain unfinished. No fourth original family or new transposition result is claimed.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Trace buckets. For real two-by-two matrices a,b, |tr(a)-tr(b)|<=2 dist_F(a,b). For a nonempty finite real set T whose distinct elements have distance>4delta, the sets of matrix centers with |tr(c)-t|<=2delta are pairwise disjoint. Consequently, from any finite center set F one can choose t in T with |T| times its bucket cardinality <=|F|. If T is contained in tr(D) and F covers A*D*A^-1 at radiusdelta, this chooses g in D and E subset F with |T|*|E|<=|F| such that E covers every x*g*x^-1, x in A, at the same radius. A and D are independent. Membership in the mixed product and invariance of trace under conjugation are proved for the actual group elements.

Scalar covering comparison. If a scalar set S is covered by N-radius intervals around a finite F, then for eta>0 its native external covering number is finite and N_eta(S)<=(2N/eta+1)|F|. The proof constructs a finite grid using the existing binCount bounds. For any nonempty bounded S, a native maximal4eta-separated set gives a nonempty finite T subset S with all distinct distances>4eta and N_eta(S)<=9|T|. Thus the separated-trace count is controlled without a new finiteness premise or an unproved scale comparison.

Combined real commuting extraction. Let A,D be nonempty subsets of SL2(R), both with entries bounded by B>=1. Assume D lies in the Frobenius identity ball of radius0<alpha<=1/2, every g in D has dist_F(g,I)>=r>0, and1536B^4*eta<=r with eta>0. There are g in D, an ambient matrix c, a nonempty actual fiber
 S={x in A:dist_F(x*g*x^-1,c)<=eta},
x0 in S, and f:S->SL2(R). Every f(x) has the form sI+t*g, all f(x) commute pairwise, and every x0^-1*x belongs to A^-1*A with
 dist_F(x0^-1*x,f(x))<=12800B^6*eta/r.
Let V=range(f) and C=A*D*A^-1. The native external covering numbers of A,tr(D),C,V at eta are finite, and
 N_eta(tr(D))*N_eta(A) <= 9*N_eta(C)*(102400B^7/r+8B+1)^4*N_eta(V).
The group sets use their ambient Frobenius matrix embeddings, traces use the ordinary real metric, and every N denotes the finite native covering number coerced to a real. The proof attains a minimal finite cover of C, applies the low-cost bucket theorem, and uses R1819's actual large conjugacy fiber. No injectivity is required, and conjugation is not assumed isometric. Taking D=A recovers the same-set version when A satisfies the explicit separation hypotheses; the two-set version also permitsI in A.

Polynomial loss. For B>=0 and0<r<=1,
 9*(102400B^7/r+8B+1)^4 <= 9*(102400B^7+8B+1)^4/r^4.
Thus the covering penalty is a fixed polynomial of degree4 in1/r, while the approximation radius is a fixed multiple of eta/r. Absorbing its constants and choosing r as a small power of eta for the actual application remain separate tasks.

Scope. Three modules add8 theorems and no definitions. Existing mathematical modules are unchanged. This is a supporting quantitative extraction theorem under explicit candidate-set hypotheses, not a completed paid-padding construction, product-growth theorem or literature novelty claim.

SOURCE AND SCOPE
Direct proof from trace invariance and its Frobenius Lipschitz bound, finite disjoint-bucket counting, native maximal separated sets, explicit one-dimensional cover refinement, and the verified R1819 conjugacy-fiber extraction. The trace candidate set D and conjugating set A are independent; all D are assumed near the identity and separated from it. This supplies the trace-counting and commuting-cover extraction step in the route associated with Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, Lemma5.2. R1821 — QUANTITATIVE NONCONCENTRATION AND FINITE-CENTER TRIMMING
In progress. R1821 proves that many separated translates force a small cluster to have low covering complexity, with explicit Frobenius distortion and covering-refinement costs. It then proves that deleting neighborhoods of finitely many prescribed centers leaves a nonempty subset carrying at least half the original covering complexity. A uniform dyadic theorem derives the required inequalities from small tripling and the intermediate-scale separated-subset condition, under the explicit budget beta<zeta*kappa and epsilon<zeta<1. Four new modules add10 theorems and no definitions; existing mathematical modules are unchanged. Application to the same walk profile and spanning frame, separated near-identity trace candidates, product growth and paid padding remain unfinished. No fourth original family or new transposition result is claimed.

EXACT STATEMENTS
Native finite-cover bounds. In any pseudo-emetric space, if A is covered by finitely many pieces S_i, each having finite external eta-covering number, then N_eta(A)<=sum_i N_eta(S_i), and N_eta(A) is finite. For finitely many pieces inside a set C with finite covering number in a pseudo-metric space, if every point in one piece has distance>2eta from every point in another, then sum_i N_eta(S_i)<=N_eta(C). The latter proof filters a minimal cover of C to centers whose eta-balls meet each piece; these filtered sets are pairwise disjoint. A remainder version proves N_eta(A)<=N_eta(R)+sum_i N_eta(S_i), where R consists of points of A belonging to none of the pieces. These statements derive or retain the required finiteness and use the same eta throughout.

Translation and geometry. If t in SL2(R) has entries bounded by B>=0 and S is any entry-bounded SL2 set, then for eta>0,
 N_eta(S)<=(8B+1)^4*N_eta(t*S).
Both covering numbers are finite. Pull the cover back through actual left multiplication by t^-1, whose Frobenius norm is at most2B, then apply the existing explicit coordinate refinement. If t,u have entries bounded by B, h has entries bounded by H, x,y are within r of h, and
 dist_F(t,u)>8BH*r+4H*eta,
then dist_F(t*x,u*y)>2eta. The proof also derives the nonnegativity of r from the nonempty cluster hypotheses. It does not assume that multiplication is an isometry.

Cluster nonconcentration. Let A have entries bounded by B>=0, let h have entries bounded by H>=0, and let T be a finite subset of A with distinct distances>rho. If eta>0 and8BH*r+4H*eta<=rho, then for S=A intersect the closed Frobenius r-ball around h,
 |T|*N_eta(S)<=(8B+1)^4*N_eta(A^2).
The relevant covering numbers are finite. The pieces t*S lie in A^2 and are more than2eta apart, so their covering costs sum to at most N_eta(A^2). Pulling each piece back gives the displayed estimate. T and S need not be maximal or injectively encoded by cover centers.

Finite-center trimming. Let F be a finite set of SL2 centers with entries bounded by H. Let T be a nonempty rho-separated finite subset of an entry-B-bounded A. Suppose the preceding geometric scale condition holds and
 N_eta(A^2)<=K*N_eta(A),
 2*|F|*(8B+1)^4*K<=|T|.
Then R={x in A:dist_F(x,h)>r for all h in F} is nonempty, has finite covering number, and
 N_eta(A)<=2*N_eta(R).
The proof bounds the sum of all removed cluster costs, applies the native remainder-cover inequality, and uses positivity supplied by T. F may be empty; no pairwise separation among its centers is assumed.

Uniform dyadic theorem. Fix m in N, B,H>=1 and real kappa,zeta,beta,epsilon with0<zeta<1, epsilon<zeta and beta<zeta*kappa. There is J depending only on these fixed parameters such that for every j>=J, eta=4^(-j), every identity-containing A with entries bounded by B, and every F with |F|<=m and entries bounded by H, the following hypotheses suffice:
 N_eta(A^3)<=eta^(-beta)*N_eta(A);
 for every eta<rho<eta^epsilon there is a finite T subset A, separated by more than rho, with |T|>=rho^(-kappa).
Then removing all closed balls of radius eta^(2zeta) around F leaves a nonempty R with finite covering number and N_eta(A)<=2N_eta(R). The proof uses rho=eta^zeta, derives the geometric separation condition by making16BH*eta^zeta and8H*eta^(1-zeta) at most1, and absorbs the count cost using eta^(zeta*kappa-beta). Small doubling follows from small tripling becauseI belongs to A; finiteness of the triple-product cover follows from actual entry bounds. The threshold is chosen before A and F. For the existing walk profile, kappa=1/122880, so the budget is beta<zeta/122880. The profile must still be instantiated with these choices and the SAME frame.

R1827 — VERIFIED CENTRALIZER CHART, INVERSE AND CONDITIONAL CUBIC PACKING
In progress. R1827 proves explicit positive-trace centralizer chart estimates, a two-point remainder for triple products, a quantitative inverse estimate under a specified nondegenerate frame, and a cubic packing corollary using native external covering numbers. Four modules add ten theorems and no definitions. The estimates use no inverse discriminant and include nilpotent directions. EXACT STATEMENTS
All two-by-two matrix norms and distances below are the native Frobenius ones; parameter vectors use the supremum norm. The identity has norm sqrt(2), bounded by 2 in the proof, never incorrectly set to 1.

1. POSITIVE-TRACE CENTRALIZER CHART.
Let b be a real traceless two-by-two matrix. For u=cI+t b in SL2(R),
  c^2+det(b)t^2=1.
If M>=1, 0<=r<=1, norm(b)<=M, |det(b)|<=M, and
  u=cI+t b, v=pI+q b are in SL2(R), c,p>=1/2, |t|,|q|<=r,
then
  norm(u-I),norm(v-I)<=3Mr,
  norm(u-v)<=5M|t-q|,
  norm(u-v-(t-q)b)<=4Mr|t-q|.
The more precise separate coefficient and matrix bounds are also proved. No division by det(b) or by a discriminant is used.

2. TRIPLE-PRODUCT REMAINDER.
In any normed ring with norm(1)<=2, if r<=1, all u_i,v_i lie within r of 1, and all norm(u_i-v_i)<=Y, i=0,1,2, then
  norm(u0u1u2-v0v1v2-sum_i(u_i-v_i))<=12rY.
The proof is an exact ordered telescoping identity plus existing norm inequalities.
For three centralizer charts as in (1), with 3Mr<=1, put
  U=u0u1u2-v0v1v2,
  L=sum_i(t_i-q_i)b_i, N=norm(t-q).
Then norm(U-L)<=192 M^2 r N.

3. EXPLICIT FRAME INVERSE.
Let T be a real four-by-four matrix whose columns 1,2,3 are the four matrix coordinates of b0,b1,b2. Column0 is arbitrary. Assume every |T_ij|<=M, d>0, |det(T)|>=d, and
  36864 M^6 r<=d.

4. CUBIC PACKING.

  |x-y|>384 M^4 eta/d for distinct x,y in F.
For S={u0(x0)u1(x1)u2(x2):x0,x1,x2 in F},
  N_eta(S) is finite and N_eta(S)>=|F|^3.
The actual map is injective and its distinct outputs have distance>2eta. The theorem also permits empty F and eta=0. It uses mathlib's externalCoveringNumber and the existing separated-sample comparison, not a new covering-number definition.

R1830 — VERIFIED ACTUAL SOURCE-WORD TRANSFER AND COARSENING
In progress. R1830 transfers the exact normalized cubic product to actual shared-center source words in A^142, including the error of the normalization center, conjugation factors and Frobenius right-translation distortion. It composes this transfer with R1829 to prove an actual-power covering lower bound. A separate source-preserving coarsening theorem explicitly pays for the larger input spacing. Four modules add7 theorems. Strict amplification, full budget composition and the fourth original theorem family remain incomplete.

EXACT STATEMENTS
All norms and distances below are native Frobenius matrix norms and distances. N_eta denotes the native external covering number, interpreted as a real number only after finiteness is proved.

1. TEN-FACTOR PRODUCT ERROR, INCLUDING THE CENTER.
Let c,d,f_i,a_i,u,v be in SL2(R), i=0,1,2. Assume all their entries have absolute value at most R>=1, dist(c,d)<=epsilon and dist(f_i,a_i)<=epsilon, epsilon>=0. Define
  P_f=(c^-1 f_0)(u c^-1 f_1 u^-1)(v c^-1 f_2 v^-1),
  P_a=(d^-1 a_0)(u d^-1 a_1 u^-1)(v d^-1 a_2 v^-1).
Then
  dist(P_f,P_a)<=20(2R)^10 epsilon.
The proof specializes the EXISTING complex finite-product error theorem and EntryApprox.inv to the actual list of ten factors, then uses the existing entrywise-to-Frobenius bound. No new generic product or inverse-metric chain is built.

2. ACTUAL SOURCE WORD LENGTH AND COVER TRANSFER.
Let A be symmetric with entries bounded by2. Let x_i belong to A and a_i=base^-1*x_i. Let f_i be epsilon-approximants to a_i, with entries of both families, u and v bounded by R>=1. Let u belong to A^34 and v to A^68. Choose a center i0 and any selected source map s (the selected index type need not be finite). Put
  w_j=f_i0^-1*f_(s(j)), W_j=x_i0^-1*x_(s(j)).
The source-center cancellation is exact:
  a_i0^-1*a_i=x_i0^-1*x_i in A^2.
For any triple, the actual word
  Q=W_0 u W_1 (u^-1 v) W_2
belongs to A^142. More generally, if u in A^j and v in A^k, its length is6+2j+k. Its right normalization Q*v^-1 is the same conjugated product built from the W_i; normalized length is210 in the actual case.
For the exact product set
  P={w_0 (u w_1 u^-1)(v w_2 v^-1)},
and eta>0, both relevant covering numbers are finite and
  N_eta(P)<=C(R,epsilon,eta)*N_eta(A^142),
  C(R,epsilon,eta)=[4*(20(2R)^10 epsilon+2R eta)/eta+1]^4.
Equivalently C=[80(2R)^10 epsilon/eta+8R+1]^4. The term2R is the norm bound on v^-1, not an assumed metric invariance. The fourth power is the already-proved four-coordinate cover refinement cost. This theorem reuses coveringNumber_le_bounded_transport directly.

3. COMPOSITION WITH THE ACTUAL-FRAME PACKING ENDPOINT.
Under ALL finite-sample, actual-frame, localization, cardinality and spacing hypotheses of R1829 exists_actual_localized_cubic_packing, suppose additionally that the source center base and every X_i belong to A and
  dist(f_i,base^-1*X_i)<=epsilon.
Choose R>=B and R>=4^68; the latter also bounds the entries of base^-1*X_i by8. Then
  m^3<=C(R,epsilon,eta)*N_eta(A^142),
and N_eta(A^142) is finite. The Lean endpoint is actual_localized_source_packing. Thus the lower bound now reaches an actual power of the original A; it is no longer only a statement about exact commuting approximants.

4. COARSER SEPARATED SAMPLE WITH SOURCE WITNESSES.
For any matrix set V with finite N_sigma(V), eta>0, coordinate refinement gives
  N_eta(V)<infinity,
  N_eta(V)<=[4sigma/eta+1]^4*N_sigma(V).
For a nonempty bounded image V=range(g), and eta,sigma>0, there is a nonempty finite F subset V and a source map s:F->domain(g) satisfying g(s(y))=y, pairwise distances strictly greater than2sigma, and
  N_eta(V)<=6561[4sigma/eta+1]^4*|F|.
The source map preserves the original approximant, source word and scalar coordinates when applying the actual packing theorem to F. Existing separated_matrix_sample and coordinate-patch refinement are reused, rather than re-proving maximal packing or bins.
For R1829's required spacing, take
  2sigma=10BM*(384M^4/d)*eta.
Then the explicit sampling coefficient becomes6561[7680BM^5/d+1]^4. Localization additionally costs binCount(B,delta)^4. These two lemmas have not yet been assembled with the integer choice of m into a single bound on N_eta(V)^3; that remaining composition must retain the small-cardinality case.

DRIFT CHECK — WHY THIS IS NECESSARY BUT NOT THE MISSING GROWTH.
Let A0=N_eta(A), V0=N_eta(V). Existing extraction, after bounding N_eta(A D A^-1) by an envelope times A0, has the form
  V0^3 >= L_lower * A0,
where L_lower is small (positive scale powers and inverse envelope costs). The current packing, source transfer, coarsening and localization have the complementary form
  V0^3 <= L_upper * A0
once the actual A^142 envelope is applied, up to a harmless small-cardinality branch; L_upper is large. These inequalities are compatible. They do not become contradictory merely by paying the constants more sharply, and no strict product growth has been proved here.
The remaining substantial ingredient must amplify a scalar/commuting set or otherwise gain a positive scale exponent beyond this cube-root-size balance. In particular, the scalar projection theorem needs a genuine nonconcentrated coefficient family and a comparison at the extracted scalar-set scale. An upper bound on traces relative to A0 is not automatically an upper bound relative to V0. Concentration of A does not automatically transfer to V. Do not repeat the cubic argument in another wrapper and describe it as amplification.

R1831 — VERIFIED WHOLE-FAMILY CUBIC BOUND AND SCALAR IDENTITY
In progress. R1831 completes the cubic upper bound for the whole possibly infinite commuting family, composing source-preserving sampling, localization, integer rounding, actual A^142 transfer and the existing arbitrary-power envelope. The small-cardinality case is retained. It also verifies the inverse-final-factor identity: the trace expression is a scaled X+lambda_g X for the same squared-coordinate set X, with an explicit nilpotent specialization. Three modules add6 theorems. Nonconcentrated coefficient selection, conversion of scalar amplification to matrix growth and the fourth original theorem family remain incomplete.

EXACT STATEMENTS
1. WHOLE COMMUTING-FAMILY CUBIC UPPER BOUND.
Let V=range(f) be the exact commuting approximants associated with the shared source words base^-1 X_i, with base,X_i in A. The index type may be infinite. Retain the actual-frame and chart hypotheses of R1830: A symmetric, I in A, A inside a sufficiently small identity ball; p,q,pq in A^34 with a positive spanning determinant; the SAME near-identity generator z bounded away from I; every f_i scalar-affine in z; entries bounded by B; chart radius r, localization radius delta and frame bound d meeting the explicit inequalities in commuting_family_cubic_bound. Let epsilon bound dist(f_i,base^-1 X_i), and R>=max(B,4^68).
Assume V is nonempty, eta,sigma>0 and
  10BM*(384M^4/d)*eta <= 2sigma.
Define
  C=6561(4sigma/eta+1)^4,
  L=binCount(B,delta)^4,
  E=[4*(20(2R)^10 epsilon+2R eta)/eta+1]^4.
Then N_eta(V) and N_eta(A^142) are finite and
  N_eta(V)^3 <= 4(CL)^3 * (E*N_eta(A^142)+1).
There is no remaining finite-cardinality or separated-input assumption: the finite source sample is constructed inside the proof. The integer choice m=|F|/L is made using natural-number division. When m=0 the bound follows from nonnegativity; the additive1 retains this branch. Mathlib add_pow_le gives (m+1)^3<=4(m^3+1), so no separate rounding/power chain is proved.

2. ACTUAL A^142 ENVELOPE.
For A=U^2 intersect the identity ball of radius alpha, assume U is symmetric, its entries are bounded by Q>=1, and a finite Y subset U^2 satisfies U^2 subset Y*U. The existing arbitrary-power theorem at n=141 gives
  N_eta(A^142) <= P*N_eta(A),
  P=(8(2Q)^567+1)^4 * |Y|^283 * (33^4 Q^8/alpha^4).
The new composition theorem substitutes this into any proved cubic bound K*(E*N_eta(A^142)+1), yielding K*(E*P*N_eta(A)+1), and proves finiteness of N_eta(A). It is applied at the actual word length; the shorter37-factor specialization is not used. Combined with1, K=4(CL)^3. No sharp polynomial simplification of P is needed for this step.

3. EXACT INVERSE-FINAL-FACTOR IDENTITY.
Let b be a real trace-free two-by-two matrix and u=sI+t b, v=pI+q b, g be determinant-one matrices. Define
  D_g=det(bg-gb).
Then, with all products taken in SL2(R),
  tr(v u^-1 g v u g^-1)=2+(D_g-4det(b))*q^2-D_g*t^2.
This is verified by a general polynomial identity that retains determinant factors before specializing to SL2. It uses neither diagonalization nor a nonzero discriminant hypothesis.
If D_g!=0, the same identity reads
  tr(v u^-1 g v u g^-1)=2-D_g*(t^2+lambda_g*q^2),
  lambda_g=4det(b)/D_g-1.
Thus if X is the set of squared scalar coordinates of a common centralizer family, varying u,v over that same family gives an exact affine image of X+lambda_g X. This removes the moving-base-set issue in the earlier Y_g+D_g X formula. It does NOT establish that enough distinct/nonconcentrated lambda_g are realized by actual bounded words.

4. NILPOTENT SPECIALIZATION.
When trace(b)=det(b)=0, the identity becomes
  tr(v u^-1 g v u g^-1)=2+D_g*(q^2-t^2).
For D_g!=0 the normalized coefficient lambda_g is identically-1. Therefore this particular coefficient family cannot supply nonconcentrated scalar projections in the nilpotent case. This is an obstruction to this mechanism, not an impossibility theorem for multiplication, transposition or group growth. Near-nilpotent b may also cause a quantitatively narrow coefficient family and requires an explicit budget or separate branch.

The current new formal statements are commuting_family_cubic_bound, commuting_cubic_bound_with_envelope, scalarAffine_inverse_final_identity, sl2_inverse_final_scalar_identity, sl2_inverse_final_scaled_projection and sl2_inverse_final_nilpotent_identity.

Do not describe the identity as having solved either bridge.

R1832 — VERIFIED SECOND EXTRACTION AND TRACE-CUBIC THRESHOLD
In progress. EXACT STATEMENTS
TRACE-CUBIC BOUND WITH ACTUAL PRODUCT ENVELOPES.
The new theorem is trace_reextraction_cubic_bound in TraceReextractionCubicBound.lean.
Let U be a symmetric subset of SL2(R) whose entries are bounded by Q>=1. Let finite Y be contained in U^2 and U^2 be contained in Y*U. Set A=U^2 intersect the Frobenius identity ball of radius alpha, assume I belongs to A and A is symmetric. Assume0<alpha<=1 and2*5^34*alpha<=1. Let p,q,pq belong to A^34 and assume |det(pairSpanMatrix(p,q))|>=d0>0.
Let D be NONEMPTY, contained in A^k, and contained in the open identity ball of radius1/2. Every g in D satisfies dist(g,I)>=r0>0. Let eta,sigma>0 and819200*eta<=r0.
The cubic chart parameters retain their explicit obligations:
  M>=1 and M>=128*(4^68)^2;
  delta>0,0<=r<=1,72*delta<=1,72*delta<=(r0/8)*r;
  d>0 and d<=(r0/8)^3/[3456*(96*(4^34)^4/d0)^3];
  3Mr<=1,36864*M^6*r<=d;

Write N=N_eta(A), T=trace(D), where all covers are native external covering numbers. Define

  H=(102400*2^7/r0+17)^4,

Then N_eta(T),N_eta(A) are finite and
  N_eta(T)^3 <= (9*P(k+1)*H)^3 * 4*(C*L)^3 * (E*P(141)*N+1).
The displayed losses are not automatically constants independent of eta. This is an explicit quantitative threshold, not an unconditional claim that every bounded word set has trace size O(N^(1/3)). No assumption that D has a large matrix covering number is needed.

PROOF COMPOSITION.
1. The existing extraction theorem uses independent sets A and D. Apply it with entry bound2. It produces a generator g in D and exact commuting approximants f(x) to base^-1*x for base,x in A, with error epsilon. The error budget gives epsilon<=1. Actual source entries are at most8, hence approximant entries are at most9.
2. Existing extraction gives N_eta(T)*N <=9*N_eta(A D A^-1)*H*N_eta(V).
3. D subset A^k and symmetry give A D A^-1 subset A^(k+2). The existing arbitrary-power envelope at n=k+1 gives N_eta(A D A^-1)<=P(k+1)*N. Mathlib positivity of the external covering number, finiteness and I in A establish N>0, allowing cancellation. Thus N_eta(T)<=9*P(k+1)*H*N_eta(V).
4. Apply commuting_family_cubic_bound to this SAME extracted family and the original spanning frame. Its source words are in A, and its generator is the same g in D, so all hypotheses match without pretending exact approximants are actual words.
5. Apply the actual A^142 envelope at n=141. Cube the trace inequality and substitute the cubic bound. The additive1 retains the small-cardinality case.

This result uses no diagonalization and no lower bound on the discriminant of the centralizer generator. It therefore does not exclude a nilpotent generator. It also does not itself supply scalar amplification, distribution of scalar coordinates, or control of all scale exponents. No novelty is claimed for this adaptation.

R1833 — VERIFIED ACTUAL FIXED-MATRIX SCALAR ARITHMETIC
In progress. R1833 verifies selection of one actual bounded-word trace coefficient, fixed-matrix scalar addition and multiplication in the nilpotent centralizer, explicit stability for a small nonzero determinant, and transfer to actual words with lengths2m+n and2m+2n. Three modules add9 theorems, reusing the existing frame expansion, coordinate equation and native Frobenius bounds. This removes the algebraic collapse of the earlier varying-coefficient mechanism in the nilpotent case. It does not yet prove scalar amplification or finish paid padding.

EXACT STATEMENTS
1. A NONZERO COEFFICIENT FROM AN ACTUAL WORD.
For a four-matrix frame g_i in SL2(R) with entries bounded by M>=1, coordinate determinant at least d>0, and a matrix b with some noncentral coordinate of absolute value at least rho>0, one frame element satisfies
  |tr(b g_i)| >= rho*d/(1152*M^4).
The proof reuses exists_nilpotent_trace_test and exists_bounded_matrix_frame_coordinates: a bounded test matrix e has |tr(eb)|>=rho/3 and is a bounded linear combination of the frame. Taking the largest of the four trace pairings gives the bound.
For A inside the identity ball of radius0<alpha<=1, I in A, and p,q,pq in A^34 with spanning determinant at least d, this selects an ACTUAL g in A^34 with
  |tr(bg)| >= rho*d/[1152*(4^34)^4].
There is no assumption that an arbitrary noncommuting matrix is an allowed word. No nilpotence or trace condition on b is needed for coefficient selection. In the centralizer application tr(b)=0 and the earlier near-identity pivot lemma supplies rho.

2. EXACT FIXED-g TRACE ARITHMETIC.
Let tr(b)=0, u=cI+t b, v=pI+q b be in SL2(R), and let g be in SL2(R). Write
  ell=tr(bg), tau=tr(g), Delta=det(b).
Then
  tr(u v g) = (cp-Delta*t*q)*tau + (c*q+t*p)*ell,
  tr(u g v g^-1) = 2cp+t*q*((2-tau^2)*Delta-ell^2).
The second formula is proved first as a polynomial identity retaining det(g), then specialized using the existing determinant-of-commutator trace polynomial. No diagonalization is used.
If Delta=0 and c,p>=1/2, the existing determinant-one coordinate equation implies c=p=1, and the formulas become
  tr(u v g) = tau+ell*(t+q),
  tr(u g v g^-1) = 2-ell^2*(t*q).
Thus the SAME quantitatively nonzero ell reads addition and multiplication. The coefficient lambda=-1 in R1831 was specific to its inverse-final projection expression; it does not remove these ring operations. These algebraic identities are supporting tools, not novel impossibility or expansion theorems.

3. STABILITY NEAR NILPOTENCE.
Assume0<=kappa,0<=r,|Delta|<=kappa,kappa*r^2<=1,|t|,|q|<=r,c,p>=1/2. Let |tau|<=T with T>=0 and |ell|<=L. Then
  |tr(u v g)-(tau+ell*(t+q))| <=4*kappa*r^2*T+2*kappa*r^3*L,
  |tr(u g v g^-1)-(2-ell^2*t*q)| <=kappa*r^2*(8+T^2).
The prior positive-chart bound yields |c-1|,|p-1|<=kappa*r^2 and |cp-1|<=3*kappa*r^2. The new estimates use these bounds directly, without replacing b by an unproved nilpotent approximation and without division by Delta. They do not establish that these errors fit the eventual amplification scale; that budget remains.

4. CHARGED ACTUAL WORDS.
Let A be symmetric, u',v' belong to A^m, and g belong to A^n. Assume dist(u,u'),dist(v,v')<=epsilon in the native Frobenius metric, with epsilon>=0. Let R>=0 bound the entries of v,u',g. Bounds on u and v' are unnecessary in this asymmetric estimate.
Under the hypotheses in3, actual words exist:
  wAdd=u'v'g in A^(2m+n),
  wMul=u'g v'g^-1 in A^(2m+2n),
with
  |tr(wAdd)-(tau+ell*(t+q))|
    <=16*R^2*epsilon+4*kappa*r^2*T+2*kappa*r^3*L,
  |tr(wMul)-(2-ell^2*t*q)|
    <=32*R^3*epsilon+kappa*r^2*(8+T^2).
These use existing left/right Frobenius multiplication and trace-Lipschitz bounds. There is no complexification or copied finite-product error chain. For kappa=0 only the actual-word approximation costs remain. Selecting g via1 gives n=34. For source words in A^2, the word lengths are38 and72; for re-centered source words in A^4, they are42 and76. Choose the actual source representation before using either specialization.

R1834 — VERIFIED SCALAR SUM/PRODUCT ALTERNATIVE BY PROJECTION REUSE
In progress. R1834 completes the rounded-dilate overlap/Ruzsa bridge and composes it with the already imported scalar projection theorem. Four modules add10 theorems, including a scalar sum/product alternative for a separated set in[1,2] with an explicitly assumed scalar distribution and explicit loss budgets. All incidence counts, repeated row indices, floor quantization, dilation, coefficient selection, distribution transfer, normalization and finer-scale losses are charged. This closes the missing scalar counting/projection connection; it does not establish that our extracted matrix family satisfies the premises or complete paid padding.

EXACT STATEMENTS
NOTATION. For a finite real set S and delta>0, cells_delta(S) is the number of integer cells {floor(x/delta):x in S}. This is the imported floor-cell count, not a native external covering number; the previously proved metric comparison is still needed when changing conventions. N below is |X|. The new scalar ring theorem is a consequence of the imported projection theorem, not a new claim of mathematical novelty.

1. INDEXED ROW ENERGY AND POPULAR OVERLAPS.
For finite index set I, finite universe P, and rows R_i subset P, including repeated rows,
  (sum_i |R_i|)^2 <= |P| * sum_i sum_j |R_i intersect R_j|.
This composes mathlib Cauchy--Schwarz with finite indicator double counting. Retaining indices is essential; replacing the row family by a set of distinct rows would lose multiplicity.
If I is nonempty, K>0, every row has |I| elements and |P|<=K|I|, there exist i in I and E subset I such that
  |I| <= 2K|E|,
  |I| <= 2K|R_i intersect R_j| for every j in E.
The bounds are stated without division, so there is no unrecorded integer rounding loss.

2. TWO IMPORTED RUZSA INEQUALITIES.
For finite A,B in any additive commutative group,
  |A+B| * |A intersect B| * |A| <= |A+A|^2 * |B+B|.
For A nonempty and K>0, if both |A+A| and |B+B| are at most L|A| and |A|<=2K|A intersect B|, then
  |A+B| <= 2K L^3 |A|.
No independent sign assumption on L is needed: the meaningful size hypotheses already constrain it. This is a short composition of mathlib's sub/add/add and add/sub/add Ruzsa inequalities, not a reproof of Ruzsa.

3. ROUNDED DILATES GIVE MANY SMALL PROJECTIONS.
Let delta>0,K>0 and X be a nonempty finite delta-separated subset of[1,2]. Assume
  cells_delta(X+X) <= K N,
  cells_delta(X*X) <= K N.
There exist a in X and E subset X with N<=2K|E| and, for every b in E,
  cells_delta(X+(b/a)X) <= 54880 K^4 N.
Actual rounded rows are R_a=cells_delta(aX). The imported separated-cell injectivity gives |R_a|=N, and all rows lie in the actual product-cell universe. The imported dilation bound and carry lemma give
  |R_a+R_a| <= 14 K N.
Popular overlap and item2 give
  |R_a+R_b| <= 5488 K^4 N.
Returning to real sum cells and dividing by a costs at most10, giving54880. This uses the existing conservative dilation bound rather than starting a sharper rounding proof; the former note's speculative6,432 and subsequent constants are superseded by these verified14,5488,54880 constants.

4. DISTRIBUTION OF THE ACTUAL COEFFICIENT FAMILY.
In addition to3, let C>=1,s>=0 and assume the PROVED-OR-TO-BE-PROVED input profile
  ballMass(X,u,r) <= C r^s N for every delta<=r<=1 and every real u.
There is a nonempty coefficient family F of the form {b/a:b in E}, with
  N <= 2K|F|,
  |f|<=2 for every f in F,
  ballMass(F,u,r) <= (2K C 2^s) r^s |F| for every r>=delta,
  cells_delta(X+fX) <= 54880 K^4 N for every f in F.
The existing scalar_ratio_family_ball is reused with denominator -a, so -b/(-a)=b/a. It already handles subset retention, dilation and radii larger than1. This avoids reproducing that chain. The theorem does NOT infer the input profile from cardinality or from the distribution of the original matrix set.

5. SCALAR SUM/PRODUCT ALTERNATIVE, BY REUSING THE IMPORTED ENDPOINT.
For every 0<kappa<=1, there exist epsilon>0 and an integer J>0 such that the following holds for every n>=J. Put
  delta=2^(-n),
  W=exp(epsilon*(n+1)*log(2)).
Let K,C>=1 satisfy ALL THREE explicit budgets
  109760 K^4 <= W,
  2^(2 kappa) C <= W,
  2^(2 kappa) * (2K C 2^(2 kappa)) <= W.
Let X be a nonempty finite delta-separated subset of[1,2] satisfying
  log N <= (1-kappa)*n*log(2),
  ballMass(X,u,r) <= C r^(2 kappa) N for every delta<=r<=1 and every real u.
Then at least one strict growth conclusion holds:
  K N < cells_delta(X+X), OR K N < cells_delta(X*X).

Proof interface: if both counts were small, item4 supplies F. Normalize Y=X/2 using the imported scalarZoom lemmas and apply scalar_weak_radius_projection to Y,F at scale delta/2, i.e. dyadic depth n+1. The cardinality logarithm, point range, separation, small doubling, scalar point distribution, coefficient range and coefficient distribution all have formal checks. The imported refinement lemma charges the coefficient profile's extension from radii>=delta down to radii>=delta/2. Each normalized projection count is at most twice its original count. The first budget109760=2*54880 therefore contradicts the strict projection gain. The second and third budgets respectively cover point and coefficient concentration after scaling.
The conclusion uses the SAME original delta as the sum/product input. The finer scale is internal to the proof. The three budgets are explicit hypotheses, not an unproved statement that K and C automatically fit. They can be met by sufficiently small power losses; a simplified power-law corollary is not needed before checking the actual matrix application.

R1835 — VERIFIED ACTUAL NILPOTENT TRACE AMPLIFICATION
In progress. R1835 composes the scalar sum/product alternative with exact nilpotent centralizer arithmetic and actual source-word approximation. It proves growth of a native trace covering number for an actual word family, under explicit scalar range, separation, cardinality, distribution and error budgets. Three new modules and one refactored module add6 theorems; the old inverse-final-word error calculation and the new repeated-word calculation share one proof. Nilpotence remains an explicit case assumption. The resulting word family is not yet proved to satisfy all near/far and retained-mass hypotheses of the final trace-cubic contradiction.

EXACT STATEMENTS
1. EXACT SHIFTED TRACE PRODUCT, WITH ITS GENERAL CORRECTION RETAINED.
For any real2x2 b with tr(b)=0, any real2x2 g, and real c,t,p,q, write U=cI+t b,V=pI+q b, ell=tr(bg),tau=tr(g),Delta=det(b). Then
  tr(U g V g)=(c*tau+t*ell)(p*tau+q*ell)-2(cp+Delta*t*q)det(g).
This polynomial identity does NOT assume det(b)=0 or det(g)=1.
For u,v,g in SL2(R), det(b)=0, c,p>=1/2 and the above forms, the already proved determinant-one coordinate equation forces c=p=1. Consequently
  tr(u v g)+tau=(tau+ell*t)+(tau+ell*q),
  tr(u g v g)+2=(tau+ell*t)(tau+ell*q).
These are the shifted identities needed for the SAME scalar input set, including its positive offset. They are standard trace algebra, not a claim of novelty.

2. ONE SHARED SOURCE-WORD ERROR CALCULATION.
The existing native Frobenius calculation was generalized to an arbitrary final fixed factor h and moved into two_source_trace_word_errors. If entries of v,u',g,h are at most R>=0 and dist(u,u'),dist(v,v')<=epsilon>=0, then
  |tr(u'v'g)-tr(uvg)|<=16R^2*epsilon,
  |tr(u'g v'h)-tr(ugvh)|<=32R^3*epsilon.
It does not require bounds on entries of u or v'. The previous centered_actual_arithmetic_words now calls this helper with h=g^-1; the new argument calls it with h=g. The previous theorem statement and constants are unchanged. This avoids duplicating the product-distance proof or converting to complex matrices.

3. ACTUAL TRACE CELL TRANSFER.
Let I be a finite index set, u_i=c_i I+t_i b in SL2(R), tr(b)=det(b)=0,c_i>=1/2, and let z_i be actual approximants with Frobenius dist(u_i,z_i)<=epsilon. Let R>=1 bound entries of all u_i,z_i,g. Put
  x_i=(2/3)(tau+ell*t_i), X={x_i:i in I},
  Tadd={tr(z_i z_j g):i,j in I},
  Tmul={tr(z_i g z_j g):i,j in I}.
If delta>0 and32R^3*epsilon<=delta, then
  cells_delta(X+X)<=50*cells_delta(Tadd),
  cells_delta(X*X)<=50*cells_delta(Tmul).
The affine trace readouts are(2/3)(tr(word)+tau) and(4/9)(tr(word)+2). Their slopes have absolute value at most1. The factor50 is entirely charged:5 for delta approximation,5 for the imported bounded-dilation lemma,2 for a translated grid. No separation or scalar distribution is needed for these upper transfers.
The supporting scalar_cells_le_affine_near is general: if each x in finite S lies within delta of a*y+b for some y in finite T and |a|<=1, then cells_delta(S)<=50*cells_delta(T).

4. NATIVE COVERING GROWTH OF AN ACTUAL WORD FAMILY.
For every0<kappa<=1, there exist epsilon0>0,J>0 such that the following holds at every j>=J. Let
  delta=2^(-j), W=exp(epsilon0*(j+1)*log2).
Take the matrix data from3 with I nonempty, and assume z_i in A^m and g in A^n. No symmetry or identity-inclusion assumption on A is required for this word-membership conclusion.
Let K,C>=1 satisfy the existing scalar theorem's three budgets:
  109760K^4<=W,
  2^(2kappa)C<=W,
  2^(2kappa)*(2K C 2^(2kappa))<=W.
The ACTUAL scalar set X from3 must satisfy
  X subset[1,2], delta separation,
  log|X|<=(1-kappa)j log2,

Define actual finite word families

where N_delta is the NATIVE external covering number with arbitrary real centers, converted to a finite real value. The extra factor5 uses the already proved scalar cell/native-cover bridge. This proves a conditional nilpotent-case amplification theorem, not an unconditional expansion theorem. In particular, it does not supply X's profile or enough retained cardinality from an arbitrary commuting extraction.

EXACT STATEMENTS
1. EXACT DISTANCE ON A FIXED AFFINE MATRIX LINE.
For any real 2x2 matrix b and real c,t,q,
  dist(cI+tb,cI+qb)=|t-q|*||b||.
This elementary result needs neither nilpotence nor determinant one. The proof uses existing scalarAffine_eq_smul_add and mathlib norm_smul; it does not reprove norm or matrix component machinery.

2. NILPOTENT SCALAR SPACING.
Let tr(b)=det(b)=0, u=cI+tb,v=pI+qb in SL2(R), c,p>=1/2, and g in SL2(R). Put ell=tr(bg),tau=tr(g). Suppose B>0, ||b||<=B, L>0, L<=|ell|. If
  2sigma<dist(u,v), and 3B delta<=4L sigma,
then
  delta<|(2/3)(tau+ell*t)-(2/3)(tau+ell*q)|.
The determinant-one equation already proved forces c=p=1. The argument then uses the exact distance in1. It samples exact approximants: no epsilon subtraction is needed for this scalar spacing step. Approximation error still must be charged in the later actual-word transfer.

3. SOURCE-PRESERVING SCALAR SAMPLE WITH BOTH CARDINALITY BOUNDS.
Let f_i=c_i I+t_i b be an arbitrary nonempty family of exact SL2 commuting approximants, with tr(b)=det(b)=0,c_i>=1/2 and entry bound H>=0. Let V=range(f). Retain g,B,L from2.   X={(2/3)(tau+ell*t_(s(y))):y in F}.
Then X is nonempty, |X|=|F|, and distinct x,y in X satisfy delta<|x-y|. Native-cover finiteness is proved and
  |X| <= N_eta(V) <= S * |X|,
  S=6561*(4sigma/eta+1)^4.
The left inequality uses the existing separated-matrix cardinality theorem and sigma>=eta. The right inequality reuses exists_coarse_source_sample. Every actual source word associated with the original index s(y) is retained; no new source selection, perturbation or additional error is introduced.
The theorem does NOT assert normalized scalar ball counts or invent an upper dimension gap. Its upper cardinality inequality allows the existing commuting cubic bound and the ambient dimension gap to be used for that later obligation.

 tr(g^n)-2=(tr(g)-2)det(sum_{k<n} g^k).

AdjointCoefficientSelection.lean (8 declarations)

For traceless real 2x2 matrices b,x,y, let G be their 3x3 trace Gram matrix,
G_ij=tr(b_i b_j), b_0=b,b_1=x,b_2=y. Then
 det(directionFrame(b,x,y))^2 = -2 det(G).
If all three matrices have entries bounded by B>0, their diagonal trace
pairings equal tr(b^2), and |det(directionFrame)|>=gamma>=0, at least one
of the three deviations
 tr(bx)-tr(b^2), tr(by)-tr(b^2), tr(xy)-tr(b^2)
has absolute value at least gamma^2/(832 B^4).
The proof writes the Gram matrix as a rank-one constant matrix plus three
off-diagonal perturbations; the determinant bound is explicit.

For x=Ad_u b and y=Ad_v b, write D(g)=det(bg-gb).
The trace-pair identity is
 tr(Ad_u b Ad_v b)=D(u^-1 v)-2det(b).
Hence the selected coefficient comes from one of the ACTUAL words
u,v,u^-1 v. It is not a coordinate-direction test outside the group.

MixedReadoutDistance.lean (10 theorems)

All distances and norms below are native real 2x2 Frobenius distances/norms.
Inversion in SL2(R) is an exact distance isometry, proved using the imported
adjugate formula and existing squared-distance formula. In particular,
dist(u^-1,I)=dist(u,I). The proof reuses norm multiplication and addition
inequalities, the existing centralizer chart, and the R1846 determinant
identity; no general matrix inverse theorem is redeveloped.

Auxiliary bounds:
 |det a| <= 2||a||^2;
 ||[b,E]|| <= 2||b||||E||;
 if E=sI+t c-q b, ||b||,||c||<=M, rho>0 and
 rho^2<=|det([b,c])|, then
 |t|,|q| <= 4M||E||/rho.
The scalar coefficient s needs no bound.
For traceless b with ||b||,|det b|<=M and M>=1, if
 u=sI+t b is in SL2 and dist(u,I)<=1/2, then
 dist(u,I)<=3M|t|. This does NOT assume |t|<=1: the existing
small chart handles that case, and the near-identity bound handles the rest.
For dist(u,I)<=1, dist(u,I)<=dist(u^2,I).

MAIN METRIC THEOREM: mixed_readout_distance_bound
Let b be traceless, M>=1, rho>0, ||b||,|det b|<=M, and
 ||Ad_g(b)||<=M. Let u=sI+t b and v=pI+q b be determinant-one
matrices with dist(u,I),dist(v,I)<=1/8. Write
 Delta=det b, D=det(bg-gb), W=v u^-1 g(vu)g^-1.
If |D|>=rho and |D-4Delta|>=rho, then
 max(dist(u,I),dist(v,I)) <= (144 M^2/rho) dist(W,I).
The conclusion bounds BOTH inputs. Either input may equal I. No
nonzero-determinant assumption on b is needed for this metric statement.

Proof: a=vu,w=uv^-1,E=Ad_g(a)-w=w(W-I). Commutativity gives
u^2=aw,v^2=aw^-1. The earlier identity gives
|det([b,Ad_g b])|=|D||4Delta-D|>=rho^2.
Instead of a 4x4 frame inverse, the norm bound gives
||[b,Ad_g b]||>=rho/2. Commuting E with b and Ad_g b bounds the
two noncentral coefficients by4M||E||/rho. The chart bounds a,w
by12M^2||E||/rho; their norms and the inverse norm are<=3.
Squaring costs4 and E costs3, yielding144M^2/rho.

DECISIVE DRIFT / FEASIBILITY AUDIT

A single-pass concentration endpoint was implemented and passed targeted
Lean builds. It correctly constructs the R1848 sample and applies the
shared concentration theorem under explicit trimming and concentration
budgets. An independent algebraic check of the simultaneous budgets then
showed that this ORDER of operations is unsuitable for the intended scales.
The conditional theorem was true, but its required trimming inequality
could not be made small in that regime. The unused specialization was
removed from active Lean sources; diagnostic source is saved locally at
external/temporary/r1849_single_pass_prototype.lean. The shared proof and the
normalization lemmas remain useful and are audited here.

Why the budget fails:
For the trace-square inverse, Kinv=3072/(lambda*s), lambda<=32.
The final scalar spacing requires2sigma>=Kinv*delta_s. In the intended
regime delta_s>=eta this forces sigma/eta>=48/s. Hence the coarse
retention factor C=6561(4sigma/eta+1)^4 satisfies C*s^4>=1.
Its CUBIC normalization cost therefore contains s^-12.
Meanwhile Anear has decay only s^kappa. With the usual nonnegative profile
bounds E>=1,K,J>=1,eta<=1,gamma,kappa>=0,R>=1, one has Anear>=s^kappa.
Taking the harmless larger fixed constants/envelopes ensures W,L>=1.
The newly proved obstruction applies for kappa<=12, covering our range.
Thus decreasing s to remove the trace-square critical point cannot make
this single-pass trimming estimate succeed. Earlier optimism about just
choosing smaller exponents overlooked that sigma itself depends on1/s.

This DOES NOT refute the R1848 conditional sampler. It also does not rule
out special inputs or spacings outside the stated regime. It says not to
try to close the main argument with this coupled single-pass budget.

Repair: TRIM FIRST, COARSEN SECOND.
The initial fine scale sigma0 only has to meet cubic packing. Its trimming
factor C0 is independent of1/s. After choosing a far, single-sign branch,
a second coarse sampling at sigma1 pays the trace-square inverse loss.
The factor C1(s) then enters the FINAL cardinality/concentration budget,
not the earlier condition that creates the far branch. This is the next
construction to prove; it is not yet formalized in this checkpoint.

The verified obstruction is to this displayed budget, not to matrix growth or transposition. R1857 — VERIFIED FINITE PRIORITY COUPLING AND AFFINE GRID ESTIMATES
R1857 begins affine return motion200/210 with three checked modules: exact finite minimum-coupling counts, selection of one global ordering for an arbitrary weighted measure, and affine grid-cell/collision bounds. The original motion theorem is not yet formalized. Four of six original families remain complete; final referees pending.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
CHECKED LOCAL STATEMENTS
1. FiniteMinimumCoupling.lean: For nonempty subsets A,B of a finite linearly ordered universe, select the least element under a permutation sigma. The exact number of permutations producing distinct selections, multiplied by |A union B|, equals |Perm| times |(A union B) minus (A intersection B)|. The proof uses equal minimum fibers, a swap bijection and mathlib finite fiberwise counting; no factorial formula or unproved random-oracle hypothesis.
2. WeightedMinimumCoupling.lean: Let mu be any measure on a measurable space Omega, let A(x),B(x) be nonempty finite sets, and let bad be measurable. If |A(x) triangle B(x)|<=delta|A(x) union B(x)| off bad, and each ordering's disagreement event is measurable, then ONE ordering sigma satisfies mu{first_sigma A(x)!=first_sigma B(x)}<=delta mu(Omega)+mu(bad). Neither finite total measure nor invariance is a hypothesis of this general lemma. Finiteness is needed later to obtain a small numerical error.
3. AffineGridMass.lean: For a!=0 and h>0, volume{x:floor((ax+b)/h)=z}=h/|a|. If a label at each x in I selects a grid cell from one of finitely many invertible affine maps, each label class has outer measure at most h sum_i 1/|a_i|, regardless of priorities. Distinct slopes a,c give collision measure at most 2h/|a-c|. Equal slopes and offsets separated by at least h give an empty collision set. Negative slopes and arbitrary measurable/nonmeasurable domains in the class bound are covered. These results reuse mathlib's affine change of variables and finite-union measure bound.

DIRECT FINITE ROUTE: WRITTEN DEPENDENCY MAP, NOT YET FORMALIZED
The original argument invokes CFW for the affine return relation. The needed conclusion is only a finite interval label with tiny classes and tiny total return cut. A finite Foelner/minimum construction appears to obtain that conclusion directly.
A. For a finite family H of return affine maps s, obtain a nonempty finite family F of invertible affine maps with |F triangle Fs|/|F union Fs| small for every s in H. This is a finite group-counting condition, not Lebesgue invariance.
B. For x in compact I, form the cells {floor(f(x)/h):f in F}. All cells fit in a single finite universe. A single random ordering of that universe assigns the minimum cell to x. The checked weighted lemma chooses ONE ordering for the entire return-pair measure, including all heads. It does not choose a separate ordering for each pair.
C. For each s, off collisions among distinct maps in F union Fs, the two cell sets at x and sx have the same union and symmetric-difference cardinalities as F and Fs. The checked grid collision bounds make the bad source-time set small. A proved marginal bound converts this to a small return-pair mass. That marginal bound is still required.
D. Every selected cell class has mass <=h sum_f 1/|slope(f)|, already checked. Finitely many affine grid thresholds on compact I make the selected label constant between finitely many breakpoints. Prove this for the ORIGINAL PiecewiseConstOn definition, and inject the finite integer-cell labels into natural labels.
E. The actual finite weighted good-return measure decomposes over countably many branch pairs. Truncate to finitely many maps with small discarded mass; prove Borel pair domains and both marginals <=k times Lebesgue. Connect the integral to the ORIGINAL levelCross definition, including infinite full level sets and constant-branch heights.
F. For210, retain only affine-region visits to build the good-return measure. Each omitted full-level visit touches at most two original consecutive pairs. Reuse Transpose.Tape.Statements.Core's levelSet_encard_majorant on a finite interval cover of compact E_t. Conclude sum_t integral levelCross<=small+2 sum_t |E_t|, then use M* and arbitrarily small class masses to derive sum_t |E_t|>=1/2.

SMALLER AFFINE FOELNER ROUTE TO TEST NEXT
Use the split affine multiplication (a,t)(s,b)=(as,t+ab), not a general amenable-extension theorem. First choose a finite almost-invariant slope set S in the commutative group R^units for the finite generator slopes. Next choose a finite almost-invariant translation set T in additive R for all finitely many shifts ab (a in S, b an offset of a return map). Then F=S x T consists of affine maps. For right multiplication by (s,b), slopes leaving S cost at most |T| times their count; remaining translation losses are bounded by sum_a |(T+ab) minus T|. Equal cardinalities convert one-sided losses into the symmetric-difference bound. All maps are invertible, including negative slopes. F need not lie in the subgroup generated by return maps.
For either commutative group, use images of exponent boxes C_n={product_i g_i^e_i:0<=e_i<=n}. They are nonempty, nested, have |C_n|<=(n+1)^m and contain g_i C_(n-1). Some consecutive growth ratio is arbitrarily close to1, since a permanent larger ratio would force exponential growth. Image cardinality avoids assuming independent generators. Reuse mathlib isLittleO_pow_const_const_pow_of_one_lt (or its tendsto corollary), not a fresh analysis proof. This yields finite simultaneous almost-invariance without general invariant means or CFW. This step is a candidate proof and remains to be formalized.

R1858 — VERIFIED FINITE AFFINE ALMOST-INVARIANT SETS
R1858 formalizes finite simultaneous almost-invariant sets for arbitrary finite families of invertible real affine maps, including negative slopes. The proof constructs slope and translation sets using commutative exponent boxes and mathlib polynomial-versus-exponential growth. No amenability or hyperfiniteness premise remains in this algebraic step. Actual admissible labels, weighted returns and the full motion200/210 theorem remain. Four of six original families formalized; final referees pending.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
VERIFIED FINITE ALGEBRAIC ENDPOINT
Let j range over any finite type, with s_j a nonzero real number and b_j real. Let delta>0. There exists a nonempty finite family F of invertible real affine maps such that, simultaneously for every j, writing H_j={f composed with (x -> s_j x+b_j):f in F},

  |F triangle H_j| <= delta |F union H_j|.

Lean represents a map by (a,t) in R^units x R. Its explicit right composition is (a,t) -> (a s_j,t+a b_j). affineRight_apply verifies the action formula; affineRight_injective proves this composition preserves distinct maps. The endpoint is exists_affine_small_symmetric_difference. It permits negative slopes, dependent/duplicate generators and an empty generator family. The family F and its size depend on the requested maps and tolerance; no uniform size or computational bound is claimed.

PROOF COMPONENTS
1. exists_small_growth_step: A real sequence with a(0)>=1 and a(n)<=(n+1)^m has some a(n+1)<=r a(n), for each r>1. Otherwise a(n)>=r^n contradicts mathlib isLittleO_pow_const_const_pow_of_one_lt. No fresh proof of the analytic asymptotic theorem.
2. exponentBox g n is the image of exponent vectors with coordinates in{0,...,n}, under e -> product_i g_i^e_i, for any finite family in a commutative group. Its size is at most(n+1)^m even with arbitrary relations among the generators. It is nonempty, nested and contains each generator translate of the previous box.
3. exists_small_mul_boundary: For every epsilon>0, there is one nonempty finite F with |F g_j minus F|<=epsilon|F| for all j. exists_small_add_boundary reuses the SAME proof through Multiplicative, rather than copying it for additive groups.
4. affine_rectangle_escape_card: For finite slopes S and translations T, the number of maps leaving S x T under right composition is at most |{a in S:a s notin S}| |T| + sum_(a in S) |{t in T:t+a b notin T}|. The proof uses injective image/filter counting, product cardinality and mathlib's finite-union bound.
5. Choose S with slope boundary at most epsilon/2. Then choose T with additive boundary at most epsilon/2 simultaneously for all shifts a b_j indexed by S x J. R1860 — VERIFIED COLLISION CONTROL AND ACTUAL SAMPLE BOUNDARIES

VERIFIED UNIFORM COLLISION THEOREM
For a finite indexed family of distinct affine coefficient pairs(a_i,b_i), and every eta>0, there is rho>0 such that EVERY mesh0<h<=rho satisfies
 volume{x:there exist i!=j with floor((a_i x+b_i)/h)=floor((a_j x+b_j)/h)}<=eta.
The collision set is measurable. Off this set the grid-evaluation map on the family is injective, and conversely injectivity implies no collision. No invertibility or sign assumption is needed for this general coefficient-pair theorem; the later actual affine-family corollary uses units for the slopes.
Proof: each unequal-slope pair has the previously proved2h/|a-c| bound; an equal-slope pair has different offsets, and its collision set is empty for h<=|b-d|. Allocate eta/(N+1) to each of N ordered index pairs, choose their positive thresholds, and take a finite minimum after adjoining a dummy value1. The dummy handles empty families. The finite-union inequality gives the simultaneous bound. No unproved convergence or limit interchange is used.
exists_small_affine_family_collisions specializes this to an actual finite set K of invertible affine maps. Injectivity of the real coefficient pairs is derived from subtype and unit extensionality, not assumed about a potentially duplicate enumeration.

VERIFIED EXACT CARDINALITY TRANSFER
If f is injective on A union B, then
 |f(A) union f(B)|=|A union B|,
 |(f(A) union f(B)) minus(f(A) intersection f(B))|=|(A union B) minus(A intersection B)|.
These are short compositions of mathlib image_union,image_inter_of_injOn,image_sdiff_of_injOn and card_image_of_injOn. Consequently the ENNReal relative-boundary inequality transfers exactly, without a multiplicity factor.
For the ACTUAL gridSample C q from R1859, its integer-value image is exactly the finite image of q whenever all q_i lie in C. Subtype-value injectivity then transfers the boundary inequality BACK into the finite priority universe C. Different finite index types for the two samples are allowed; neither nonemptiness nor a free-generator assumption is hidden in these counting identities.

VERIFIED AFFINE-TO-SAMPLE ENDPOINT
Let F be a finite set of invertible affine maps, g(x)=sx+b with s!=0, and let H=F composed on the right with g. Suppose |F triangle H|<=delta|F union H|, expressed in ENNReal. R1861 proves the complete abstract small-class/small-cut labeling theorem for a finite measure supported on COUNTABLY many invertible affine return graphs, with only a bounded source marginal. EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
EXACT CHECKED COUNTABLE LABELING THEOREM
Let I=[0,c0], with time represented as the subtype of real points in I. Let mu be ANY finite Borel measure on I x I. Let(g_j)_(j in N) be any sequence of invertible real affine maps g_j(x)=s_j x+b_j, allowing negative slopes and duplicates. Assume:
 (a) mu-almost every pair(u,v) lies on at least one graph v=g_j(u);
 (b) for every measurable real set E, mu{(u,v):u in E}<=kappa volume(E),
     where0<=kappa<infinity.
Then for every theta>0 and epsilon>0, there exists ONE actual beta:R->N with:
 (i) beta is measurable;
 (ii) Transpose.Tape.PiecewiseConstOn beta empty c0, the ORIGINAL definition;
 (iii) volume{x in I:beta(x)=n}<=theta for EVERY natural label n;
 (iv) mu{(u,v):beta(u)!=beta(v)}<epsilon.
This is exists_countable_affine_small_cut in CountableAffineLabels.lean. No assumption about finite equivalence classes, hyperfiniteness, invariant Lebesgue measure, ergodicity, freeness or the second marginal appears. There is no uniform bound on the number of cells or breakpoints, as in the original planned path theorem.
The measure/domain assumptions are explicit and still must be derived for the actual original paths. The theorem does not identify an arbitrary measure with the path's original levelCross integral.

FINITE FAMILY AND EXACT GLOBAL ORDER
WeightedAffinePriority.lean introduces IntervalTime and IntervalTimePair, uses the actual finite affine graph union and ONE common family K containing F and all Fg_j, and applies the previous weighted minimum theorem to the actual priority samples. Samples are nonempty at every point because their domain is I x I, rather than merely almost everywhere in an ambient space. Graph-support exceptions and source grid collisions form a measurable bad pair set. Its mass is at most kappa times collision volume, with the graph complement charged by its explicit zero measure. The exact intermediate bound is cut<=delta mu(I x I)+kappa volume(collision(K,h)).
FiniteAffineLabels.lean chooses delta=epsilon/(4(M+1)), eta=epsilon/(4(kappa+1)), where M=mu(I x I) as a real number. It obtains the finite affine set, a common collision threshold, and one mesh small enough also for the class bound. All parameters and the selected permutation are instantiated. The real budgets sum to at most epsilon/2<epsilon; finite-measure toReal/ofReal conversion is justified explicitly.

COUNTABLE REDUCTION REUSES MATHLIB
For G_N, the union of the first N return graphs, the complements form a decreasing measurable sequence whose intersection is the full graph complement. Mathlib tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop and finite mu imply mu(G_N complement)->0. Choose N with tail<epsilon/2. FORMALIZED at R1865: the affine-motion200/210 family, including countable-affine small-label path cuts, quantitative exceptional-time and physical-unit bounds, full native trace-class/nonuniform/robust consequences, and the bounded-piece o(1)-approximation exclusion. NEW R1865 RESULTS
1. affineEvaluation(D) sends (a,b) to x|->a*x+b on an arbitrary real subsetD.
   affine_on_of_tendsto proves pointwise closure of these affine functions
   by importing mathlib Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional for its range.
2. HasAffineIntervalCover(J,f,H) means J actual closed intervals with endpoints
   in[0,H] cover[0,H], and f agrees with an affine formula on each. Intervals
   may overlap, be empty or collapse; every ordinary J-piece polygonal path
   on[0,H] has such a cover. There is no Lipschitz assumption in this definition.
3. local_affine_ae_of_bounded_covers: if q_n have one fixed J of those covers
   and converge pointwise to f on[0,H], f has an open locally affine region
   whose complement in[0,H] is null. CompactSpace.tendsto_subseq extracts
   actual endpoint limits. Their closed intervals still cover; away from
   finitely many endpoints, an interval lies eventually in one actual piece.
   The affine closure theorem proves the local formula there. The eventual
   version ignores finitely many initial indices through a proved tail shift.
4. AffineTimeRequired.not_pointwise_bounded_covers: a tuple satisfying the
   quantitative affine-time requirement cannot be a pointwise limit of such
   eventual fixed-J covers. Complements are proved null, not assumed.
5. not_bounded_affine_approximation: actual paths converge uniformly to that
   tuple; approximants have eventual fixed-J covers; their actual uniform
   distance is bounded by e_n->0. These hypotheses are contradictory. Error

   bound, coefficient bound, limiting partition or limiting regularity is
   inserted for the approximants.

   rescaledTrajOf representatives of correct high-entropy trace classes,

   obstruction are imported, not postulated.

R1868 — CONTRACTING-TREE CHARGE DECAY AND COMPLETE FINITE-STAGE CLOCK ACCOUNTING
PROGRESS at R1868: regular recursion206/208 now has geometric depth-charge bounds, actual assigned-tick and contiguous-call bounds, exact finite-stage clock accounting, and the shallow-stage uncovered-tick bound. Five of six original families remain formalized; the sixth family is about15% complete, low confidence. Native global-limit exclusion and source206 executors remain open; final referees follow all six.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1868 RESULTS
1. levelCharge(V,w,n) is the sum of V(w++u) over ALL B-ary suffixes of
   length n. Mathlib Fin.consEquiv proves its exact child recurrence.
   If rho>=0 and sum_b V(w++[b])<=rho*V(w), then
     levelCharge(V,w,n)<=V(w)*rho^n.
   V>=0 and rho<1 imply summability over every descendant address, using
   mathlib List.equivSigmaTuple and summable_sigma_of_nonneg.
2. For any node w and depth h, the sum of descendant charges with relative
   depth at least h is <=V(w)*rho^h/(1-rho). The same holds for any finite
   collection of those suffixes. This follows from imported geometric sums,
   summable indicators, sigma-sum rearrangement and finite-sum comparison.
   No prior finite-depth cutoff is needed for these charge bounds.
3. assigned_tick_bound: let S be a finite set of actual execution ticks and
   owner(t) its node address. If each node owns at most a*V(node) ticks,
   and every tick in S is owned at depth>=h, then
     |S|<=a*V(root)*rho^h/(1-rho).
   The proof sums the actual ownership fibres using mathlib cardinality
   identities. deep_assigned_tick_bound derives the same bound for the
   filtered deep ticks from the budget for the ENTIRE execution set.
4. subtree_assigned_tick_bound: ticks whose owner has prefix w total at
   most a*V(w)/(1-rho). The proof identifies each suffix-owner fibre with
   the actual original fibre at w++u; unrelated ticks cannot be charged.
5. card_fin_time_interval counts exactly the integer ticks in[A,E) inside
   Fin T, giving E-A when E<=T. contiguous_call_duration_bound therefore
   bounds an actual contiguous call interval whenever its membership is
   equivalent to belonging to that node's descendant ownership fibres.
6. finite_addresses_lt_depth proves the set of B-ary addresses at depth<h
   finite, independently of execution length, using mathlib finite tuple
   images and finite unions. Together with fixed J, shallow stage keys form
   a fixed finite family for later limit extraction.

R1871 — ACTUAL-OCCURRENCE REGULARITY AND THE GEOMETRIC RECURSION LIMIT
PROGRESS at R1871: the geometric recursion limit theorem is formalized. Every physical head limit with the actual contracting stage-clock budgets and regularity of actual positive-duration occurrences has a locally affine open region of full measure, including its frozen post-halt tail. EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1871 RESULTS
1. HasRegularStageSubsequences states the actual-occurrence hypothesis:
   on every strictly increasing subsequence consisting entirely of positive
   duration stages and whose node volumes tend to infinity, the raw frozen
   head profiles admit a further strictly increasing subsequence converging
   uniformly to a finite affine-interval cover on [0,a]. It is preserved by
   passage to a subsequence. Missing padded stages are not included.
2. positive_stage_affine_of_regular_occurrences derives v>0 and a finite
   affine cover of s |-> f(l+v*s) on [0,(r-l)/v] whenever l<r is a limiting
   actual stage. The hypotheses use P->infinity, exact raw head samples,
   unit-Lipschitz extensions, uniform physical convergence, convergent
   A/P,E/P,V/P, A<=E, the actual stage budget E-A<=aV, and its horizon bound.
   It proves eventual positive stage duration and positive volume, discards
   a proved finite prefix, derives (E-A)/V ->(r-l)/v, and then reuses
   native_positive_stage_affine. No early-index positivity is assumed.
3. local_affine_ae_on_stage transports this finite local cover to an open
   locally affine set of full measure in (l,l+v*ell). It reuses the existing

4. physical_limit_constant_after_halt proves f(x)=f(H) for H<=x<=M from
   actual integer paths frozen after their halting ticks, T/P->H, the horizon
   bound, uniform physical convergence, and P->infinity. Arbitrary chosen
   unit-Lipschitz interpolating extensions need NOT be constant between ticks;
   the verified O(1/P) sampling error proves constancy in the limit.
   native_physical_limit_constant_after_halt obtains the raw frozen premise
   by importing the original workTraj_frozen from HaltsAt.
5. regular_physical_limit_locally_affine assembles the entire geometric core.
   Given fixed B,J,rho,a,C with 0<=rho<1 and a>=0, nonnegative charged volumes,
   child charge sum<=rho*parent, root<=C*P, exact integer stages partitioning
   every tick with A<=E<=T and total node own duration<=aV, P>0 tending to

   raw post-halt freezing and the actual-occurrence hypothesis at each fixed
   address/stage: there is an open R subset [0,M], with null complement,
   on which the limiting head path is locally affine.
   No limiting affine-cover assumption occurs in its premises. The proof
   invokes actual local regularity only after proving positive duration.

SCOPE REFINEMENTS OF THE GEOMETRIC CORE
The core does not use whole-subtree call contiguity once own stages are
actual contiguous global-time intervals, fixed in number per node, and all
ticks satisfy the contraction budget. Whole-call contiguity remains useful
for R1870's separate zero-volume subtree statement, but is unnecessary for
this affine-cover conclusion. No new branching/order assumption is inserted.
The theorem applies one head at a time to the same already existing uniform
limit. Thus per-head local subsequence regularity suffices; the source's
joint all-head regularity implies this. Every physical head must still meet
it for the eventual impossibility result. These are verified relaxations of
the geometric hypotheses, not yet a fully integrated native exclusion.
