R1875 — PAID PUBLIC CLOCK AND MASKED-STRIDE GROUP SLAB
PROGRESS at R1875: the exact206 executor work has begun with a verified native public-clock compiler, a three-transition masked binary cell update and a 4*S-transition group slab including partial-group padding and paid scratch rewind. Both head positions are proved at every intermediate tick. The group uses one scratch buffer, and both prefix/difference modes are supported. Five of six original families formalized; regular recursion206/208 best estimate57% complete (low confidence). Full stride recurrence, raw IO/cleanup, asymptotic limit and complete palette composition remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1875 RESULTS
1. ScheduledNativeIO compiles a public schedule sigma_i of native IO
   microinstructions with a fixed finite local mode M. The compiled labels
   are Fin(N+1) x M. All scheduled steps must be active; this is proved for
   the concrete routines, not assumed of arbitrary programs without checking.
   The clock advances exactly once per scheduled instruction and halts at N.
   NativeIOEmbedding reuses existing instruction wiring, and NativeIO's
   trace_stepN gives exact original-machine execution. No new tape simulator.
   native_prefix covers every n<=N, with the full configuration and every
   absolute head position. native_run_and_halt proves N actual transitions
   and the native halt; native_state_count proves q+1=(N+1)*|M|.
   trajectory_add/congr compose prescribed schedule segments without free
   semantic operations. Public schedule selection is compile-time nonuniform
   information; local data is confined to the stated finite mode and tapes.
2. MaskedStrideCell reads bank tape0, then buffer tape1, then writes/moves
   both heads. Exactly THREE native transitions implement
       y = x XOR (a AND previous).
   Prefix mode stores y back into the same buffer cell; difference mode
   stores the ORIGINAL x. Both old values are read before either overwrite.
   Two Boolean values suffice as local mode (four values). The standalone
   three-step instance uses two work tapes, the existing five-symbol alphabet
   and16 states. No zero-cost read, write or movement is supplied.
   result_cells proves exact absolute tape contents, including preservation
   of every other cell, and result_positions proves both heads advance one.
   Blank/nondata buffer symbols decode as zero; data symbols decode exactly.
3. MaskedStrideGroup gives each group S slots of three ticks, followed by
   S physical left moves of the scratch head. The first g<=S slots execute
   the masked cell. The remaining slots make two stationary steps and move
   only the scratch head right once, without reading/writing the bank.
   This is a single-buffer implementation: reading the previous-group bit
   before replacing it avoids a second alternating buffer.
   process_exact proves the exact iteration of the local update/padding.
   group_exact/native_group prove precisely4*S actual native transitions
   and halt in the explicit result configuration. All public masks vary
   arbitrarily by slot. Raw IO and final buffer clearing are not included.
4. group_positions proves BOTH physical head positions at every scheduled
   tick n (and native_prefix transfers it to native prefixes n<=4*S).
   With initial bank/scratch positions b0,b1, during0<=n<=3*S:
       bank=b0+min(floor(n/3),g), scratch=b1+floor(n/3).
   During3*S<=n<=4*S:
       bank=b0+g, scratch=b1+S-(n-3*S), provided g<=S.
   Thus the bank advances exactlyg, scratch restores exactly, and partial
   groups cost the same4*S slab as full groups. Data values never enter
   these head-position formulas. These are the concrete paths needed for
   both zero and positive normalized-stride cases.

R1876 — EXACT MASKED-STRIDE BANK SEMANTICS AND PAID EXECUTION
PROGRESS at R1876: the arbitrary masked binary stride processing phase now has exact cell semantics, a cross-group invariant, the full raw-index zero-filled recurrence, and a single paid native execution of every full/partial group. Its exact time is 4*S*(floor(P/S)+1), at most8*P for1<=S<=P, with4*(N+1) states. Five of six original families formalized; regular recursion206/208 best estimate59% complete (low confidence). Raw IO/final clearing, stride limits, other exact206 palettes and bounded composition remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1876 RESULTS
1. MaskedStrideGroupSemantics proves the cellwise meaning of the existing
   paid4*S slab. At every active slot, both operands are still the original
   bank and scratch values for that group. For j<g the bank receives
      x_j XOR (a_j AND prev_j).
   The scratch receives that output in prefix mode, and the ORIGINAL x_j
   in difference mode. Outside each tape's g-cell update interval, all
   absolute cells are unchanged. Padding and physical rewind write nothing.
2. MaskedStrideScan.AtGroup tracks actual bank/scratch head positions,
   outputs of all earlier groups, the untouched future bank and the exact
   preceding-group buffer value. groups_invariant proves this for every
   full group, starting with zero-decoding scratch cells. partial_correct
   handles any last g<=S, preserves all earlier outputs and the future bank,
   and restores the scratch head. Data and masks never affect these lengths.
3. MaskedStrideBank.value_recurrence proves the standard raw-index equation
      y_n = x_n XOR (a_n AND previous_n),
   where previous_n=0 for n<S; otherwise it is y_(n-S) in prefix mode
   and x_(n-S) in difference mode. This is proved from the recursively
   defined group semantics, not supplied as an assumed executor invariant.
   result_correct proves that every j<P in the actual final bank equals
   this y_j, the bank head advances P, the scratch head restores, and all
   bank cells at/after the end of the processed bank remain unchanged.
   Here x_j is decoded from the actual initial absolute bank cell.
4. MaskedStrideExecution composes scheduled instructions BEFORE compiling
   them. full_exact/full_prefix connect full groups and their intermediate
   states to the existing slab. schedule_exact and native_run execute all
   floor(P/S) full groups plus one last P%S group in a SINGLE native program,
   then halt, with no unpaid call transitions. If P%S=0, the empty final
   slab still executes and is charged. For positive S the exact processing
   duration is N=4*S*(floor(P/S)+1). ticks_le gives N<=8*P when S<=P.
   state_count gives q+1=4*(N+1), using the existing public-clock compiler,
   two work tapes, and the existing five-symbol work alphabet. This pays
   the arbitrary public masks through nonuniform transition tables; it
   does not read them from a free data oracle.

Next finish those interfaces, then the two arbitrary-stride limit cases,
backward variants, all row/integer/F3 palettes and bounded-word composition.

R1877 — COMPLETE RAW MASKED-STRIDE NATIVE EXECUTOR

It loads the input, performs the proved prefix/difference recurrence, erases all scratch cells, emits the correct raw bits and halts. Exact total time is8*P+4*S*(floor(P/S)+1)+2*S, at most18*P for1<=S<=P. It uses two work tapes, five work symbols and4*(T+1) states. EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1877 RESULTS
1. ScheduledTapeAction wraps the existing Microcode.single/native action
   refinement. Exact selected-tape rewind and erasure passes prove all
   absolute-cell updates/preservation, all head positions and preserved
   input/output fields. No new tape semantics or compiler is introduced.
2. ScheduledRawInput loads P bits in exactly3*P scheduled native steps:
   read the actual external input, write/advance bank, advance input.
   All written cells, untouched cells, both head positions, input position
   and preserved output are proved. inputBit_get directly reuses the
   ORIGINAL paper's readInput_natCast and nth_eq_getElem? theorems.
3. ScheduledRawOutput reads a bank cell, emits its decoded bit, then moves
   the bank head. Exactly3*P steps emit P bits in the correct order, with
   all bank/scratch cells and the external input position preserved.
   The statement explicitly uses the native reversed output list.
4. ScheduledSegments concatenates public instruction schedules before
   compilation, reusing trajectory_add/congr. Linking introduces no free
   semantic call: the one global clock selects every actual instruction.
5. MaskedStrideInterfaces proves preserved input/output fields through all
   groups; scratch writes remain inside the original S-cell interval; and
   the stride output at n depends only on input indices at most n.
   The last fact connects loaded bank values to the actual raw input.
6. RawMaskedStrideExecution builds a SINGLE native machine that starts at
   Transpose.init, loads raw input, rewinds the bank, executes every scan
   group, erases S scratch cells, rewinds scratch, rewinds bank, emits P
   raw output bits and halts. native_complete uses NativeIO.blank_denote,
   so no prepared bank or initialized scratch is an assumed resource.
   Every scheduled instruction is proved active before the final halt.
   Its exact time is
       T = 8*P + 4*S*(floor(P/S)+1) + 2*S,
   with T<=18*P for1<=S<=P. fixed_resources gives two work tapes, five work
   symbols and q+1=4*(T+1). All masks/strides remain public size-dependent
   parameters of a nonuniform finite transition table, not data oracles.
7. RawMaskedStrideCorrectness discharges every prepared-bank hypothesis
   and connects the final native output to
       y_j = x_j XOR (a_j AND previous_j),
   previous_j=0 for j<S; otherwise previous_j is y_(j-S) in prefix mode
   and x_(j-S) in difference mode. For inputs of length P, x is exactly
   the actual input bit sequence, as checked by inputBit_get. The theorem
   also supports arbitrary input lengths by zero-extending missing bits.
   result_output proves the final output list, result_scratch proves every
   absolute scratch cell blank, and native_correct packages actual execution,
   halt, <=18*P time, correct raw output and native scratch symbol0 at every
   coordinate. Scratch heads restore through the paid pass position lemmas.

PROGRESS at R1878: exact processing-head positions and the vanishing-stride limit are now connected to the actual raw-input native machine. NEW R1881 RESULTS
1. PhysicalAffineApproximationObstruction combines existing results:
   AffineTimeRequired.not_physical_pointwise_bounded_covers rules out

   development is needed.

   Let n_i->infinity, P_i=inputLength(n_i)=n_i^2*entryBits(n_i),
   1<=S_i<=P_i, with arbitrary size-dependent public mode and masks.
   There cannot be sets W_i and deficits m_i with m_i/P_i->0 and
      2^P_i <= 2^m_i * |W_i|
   eventually, such that every w in W_i encodes a matrix A and the exact
   outputWord of that forward masked prefix/difference operation equals
   the raw encoding of transpose(A). There are no regularity, stride-ratio,
   state-bit, time or machine-correctness assumptions left to discharge.
   Its proof derives native fast correctness from native_correct and
   native_halts, applies R1880 whole-run geometry on the subsequence
   supplied by the original theorem, and permutes encoded ports by the
   inverse encoding. This includes actual initialization and frozen halt.
   It is the one-primitive instance, not the full bounded-word theorem.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1882 RESULTS
1. MaskedStrideWord defines Operation(isPrefix,mask,stride), validity
   1<=stride<=P, the exact mathematical transform, and the actual schedule
   and internal result for an arbitrary finite list. The schedule is the
   existing paid append operation. transform_congr_upto reuses the scan's
   prefix-dependence theorem. result_spec proves that the actual bank bits
   equal the composed transform, both heads return to their original
   coordinates, the entire scratch tape is blank, and external IO fields
   are preserved. It permits arbitrary starting bank/mode/coordinates.
   Every stage's clearing and reset are included. The internal cost is
   <=11*P*length. No external output is recycled as intermediate input.
2. RawMaskedStrideWord wraps this word with one input load/rewind and one
   final output sweep. native_correct proves its exact raw output, actual
   halting and fully blank scratch at time T<= (7+11*length)*P. Fixed
   resources are2 work tapes,5 symbols, and q+1=4*(T+1). This includes the
   empty word and arbitrary public modes/masks/strides at every stage.
3. LinearStateCount.state_bits_of_linear_count is factored from R1881's
   original-library application, not a new asymptotic chain. It directly
   uses ORIGINAL stateBits_div_tendsto with zero auxiliary bits and k=0,
   then Nat.clog_mono_right and squeeze_zero. The existing single-primitive
   state_bits_vanish now calls this shared result with its unchanged
   statement. RawStrideWordResources proves G=3 and, for length<=K,
      q+1 <=4*(8+11K)*P,
   eventually, and hence clog2(q+1)/P->0 as n->infinity. Validity and the
   word-length bound may hold eventually; P>=1 follows from input growth.
4. MaskedStrideWordMotion proves exact data-independent stage paths from
   arbitrary work configurations. Let N=Scan.ticks(P,S). The bank stage
   displacement at integer time n is
      bankPosition(P,S,min(n,N)) - min(n-N-S-S,P);
   the scratch displacement is
      scratchPosition(P,S,min(n,N))
         +min(n-N,S)-min(n-N-S,S).
   Both paths are0 initially and after the paid stage horizon N+2S+P.
   For a list op::ops, each head's path is the first stage path at n plus
   the remaining word path at n-first_stage_ticks. Exact schedule_position
   and the restored endpoints are proved using append_position. There is
   no unproved rule for composing physical paths.
5. RawStrideWordMotion connects these formulas to ORIGINAL native
   workTraj from blank init at every time, including frozen halt. Its
   complete path for head t is
      Word.path(P,ops,t,n-4P)
      + if t=0 then min(floor((n+1)/3),P)-min(n-3P,P)
          +min(floor((n-(4P+Word.ticks))/3),P) else0.
   This includes all raw IO and all stage cleanup/reset costs. The proof
   uses the original run/stepN identity and workTraj_frozen unchanged.
6. StrideStageApproximation gives both heads finite affine covers with
   explicit error at an ARBITRARY public integer start A>=0. The bounded
   group comparison uses the old processing curves at(t-A), with paid
   clearing/reset ramps added. If Q=floor(P/S)<=B, both covers have at
   most9^(B+1)*9 intervals and the unnormalized error is <=2*(Q+2).
   The small-stride bank comparison is just
      clippedRamp(P,A,4,t)-clippedRamp(P,A+4P,1,t),
   with scratch comparison0. Both have9-interval covers and unnormalized
   error <=7*S+2. The actual comparison is to
      Stage.path(P,S,head,floor(t)-A),
   for every real t, including before the stage and after its reset.
   These estimates hold uniformly in A. Division by P gives the needed
   vanishing errors in the two usual regimes, without separately choosing
   convergent start-time subsequences. That final finite-word assembly
   is not claimed to be proved at this checkpoint.

R1883 — PAID BANK REVERSAL AND SHIFTED AFFINE GEOMETRY
PROGRESS at R1883: a paid raw-bit bank reversal now has proved actual scheduled semantics, exact6P+2 time, both heads restored, scratch fully blank, external IO preserved and outside-bank cells unchanged. Every intermediate head position is proved. At arbitrary public start A, each head has an81-interval affine cover with unnormalized error at most4, uniformly in P,A and real time. A generic two-step directional transfer with optional clearing supports the implementation. Five of six original families formalized; regular recursion206/208 best estimate77% complete (low confidence). Mixed palettes and their final bounded-word geometric exclusion remain.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1883 RESULTS
1. ScheduledTransferCell and ScheduledTransfer implement an actual paid
   transfer between the two distinct work tapes. Each cell costs two
   instructions: read the source into finite local mode, then write the
   target, optionally clear the source, and move both heads. The source
   moves left or right; the target moves right. Symbol read/write codecs
   and local mode are parameters. After n cells, source displacement is
   +/-n, target displacement n, and IO is unchanged. At every microscopic
   time m the displacements are +/-floor(m/2) and floor(m/2). The target
   cell j<n holds write(read(original source at source_origin +/- j)).
   Future reads are proved unaffected by earlier writes/clears; source
   and target are distinct tapes. Visited source cells are blank when
   clearing is enabled; all source cells are preserved when disabled;
   unvisited source and outside target cells retain their original values.
   Exact schedule/copy refinement and activity are proved.
2. BankReversal uses the existing binary local mode, two tapes and fixed
   alphabet. It copies P bits forwards to scratch in2P steps, rewinds the
   bank P steps, turns scratch left once, copies scratch backwards to bank
   while clearing in2P steps, rewinds bank P, and turns scratch right once.
   The actual schedule has exactly6P+2 steps, also for P=0. Starting from
   arbitrary work-head coordinates, bank contents, finite mode and IO,
   with the whole scratch tape blank, its result satisfies
      bank[origin+j] = data(bit(original bank[origin+P-1-j])), j<P.
   Both heads return to their original coordinates, the whole scratch
   tape is blank, external input/output fields are unchanged, and every
   bank cell outside [origin,origin+P) is preserved. The last preservation
   fact supports later local row operations. All copies and resets are
   actual NativeIO work actions, not bulk-operation assumptions.
3. BankReversalMotion proves both exact head paths at every time through
   the6P+2-step stage, from arbitrary starting configurations. The bank
   path consists of the forward transfer, first rewind, return transfer
   and final rewind. The scratch path consists of the forward transfer,
   one left turn, backwards return transfer and one right turn. The
   public formulas use clipped integer ramps and half-speed transfer
   ramps. They are zero initially and after the paid stage horizon and
   satisfy path(min(n,ticks))=path(n).
4. BankReversalApproximation defines four real clipped ramps for each
   head, shifted by any public start time A. The bank comparison is
      R(P,A,2) - R(P,A+2P,1) + R(P,A+3P+1,2) - R(P,A+5P+1,1),
   and scratch is
      R(P,A,2) - R(1,A+3P,1) - R(P,A+3P+1,2) + R(1,A+6P+1,1),
   where R(L,a,d)(t)=min(max((t-a)/d,0),L). For every real t and head h,
      |path(P,h,floor(t)-A)-approximation(P,A,h,t)| <=4.
   On every [0,H], H>=0, each comparison has an81-interval affine cover.
   Both bounds are uniform in P and A. After normalization the error is
   <=4/P. These are precisely the shifted stage interfaces needed by the
   existing finite-word/native high-entropy obstruction framework.

1. BackwardMaskedStride defines reflected(P,x)(j)=x(P-1-j) and

NEW R1886 RESULTS
1. ScheduledWord is a shared finite-schedule compiler, polymorphic in the

   tape/mode/decoded-value types, bank port, symbol decoder and a reusable

3. BinaryBankOperation defines the four actual operation types:

   when P>0, including all cleanup/reset/seeks. P=0 is not incorrectly

4. MixedBinaryWord composes arbitrary finite lists of these operations
   on the same actual work bank. Its result_spec proves every output bit
   equals the ordered mathematical composition, all work heads are at

1. ModularRowWord.operation_value: for equal-width little-endian Boolean
   lists a,x of length W, the checked carry machine returns a W-bit word
   whose value is (value(a)+value(x)) mod2^W for addition, or
   (value(a)+2^W-value(x)) mod2^W for subtraction. Addition imports the
   previous RepeatedAdd.addWord_value; subtraction is a short consequence
   of BinaryCarry.subtraction_identity and value_lt using Nat modular laws.
   rawOperation_value reverses the lists to state the exact MSB-first
   semantics of017. These semantic reversals do NOT claim unpaid physical
   bit-order conversion. Width0 is included in the arithmetic statements.

2. PaddedWorkSchedule: a generic work routine may be run for a fixed public
   budget N. Its halt/reject instructions become actual stationary
   self-jumps, and its trajectory equals the existing frozen work run.
   A checked active trace of length t<=N to a stopped state therefore
   reaches the same work state after exactly N paid scheduled steps.
   The schedule is active at every tick; the existing scheduled compiler
   then halts at its external public clock N. No input-dependent stopping
   duration or uncharged wait is introduced. At every prefix n, each head
   is at distance<=n from its initial coordinate.

3. RepeatedAddCalls/RepeatedAddBody now contain the shared caller proofs:
   arithmetic_call_to handles both addition and subtraction; copy_call_to,
   recycle_call_to and jump_trace_to accept an actual target program with

   linking jumps, giving a real trace of length<=18W+30. Existing public
   addition_call/copy_call/recycle_call/jump_trace/body_trace statements
   retain their previous bounds and specialize these shared proofs.
   The old body still includes its paid entry jump, hence18W+31.

4. RowArithmeticUpdate specializes that shared body to a controller that
   stops at the return label, then applies PaddedWorkSchedule. For every

NEXT: DIRECT RAW-ROW CARRY SCAN FOR INTEGER PREFIX/DIFFERENCE.
The prepared add/subtract/recycle block is DONE at RowArithmeticUpdate.
For the raw interface, a simpler direct scan appears to avoid the loader,
marker and reversal composition. Implement ONE such row first, using the

ModularRowWord.rawOperation_value. Do not reprove carry arithmetic.

PREFER THE MOVE-BEFORE-READ VARIANT (7W), to simplify the zipper proof.
The6W sanity-check variant is not worth optimizing or formalizing as well.
Concrete schedule for W>=1, bank at row MSB and accumulator at its MSB:
- One actual jump initializes carry=sub.
- Move both heads rightW ticks, just beyond their respective rows.
- Repeat W times, FOUR paid ticks each:
  1.move both heads left;
  2.read bank a into finite mode, keeping carryc;
  3.read accumulator x, set u=x XOR sub, y=a XOR u XOR c,
    c'=majority(a,u,c), saved=(a if sub else y);
  4.write banky and accumulatorsaved, stay in place, retain c'.
- Move only bank rightW to the next row; accumulator is already at0.
- Pad W-1 stationary ticks. Total1+W+4W+W+(W-1)=7W exactly.
Starting just beyond a field gives the inner scan a simple zipper invariant:
its left lists begin with the LSB-first operands. Each cycle pops one cell
from each left list, then writes its result at the new head; induction
concatenates the reversed outputs on the right. Reuse existing zipper
write/move denotation lemmas rather than reprove tape semantics.

Use only a small finite-update interface if it immediately helps reuse:
Mode := Bool x Sym Bool x Sym Bool (50 modes, with existing Fintype Sym).
A public fixed truth table maps (carry,bank symbol,buffer symbol) to
(new carry,bank output,buffer output). This four-step cell can serve binary
carry and later pointwise F3 arithmetic. Instantiate binary carry with
MaskedStrideCell.bit and BinaryCarry.digit/carry/operandBit. Do not build
an elaborate general transducer framework before proving the first row.
ScheduledNativeIO already supplies the native refinement; a separate
standalone native-machine theorem for every tiny cell is unnecessary.

For addition the buffer holds the current prefix result; for difference
it holds the ORIGINAL current row. Its next-row initial carry is reset
explicitly. Initially blank accumulator cells decode as0; after the first
row the accumulator has W data bits. This uses the existing five-symbol
native alphabet with no row markers. Finish by physically clearing and
rewinding this W-cell buffer and resetting the whole bank head; charge

R1892 — ALL-PREFIX ROW BANK AFFINE APPROXIMATION
PROGRESS at R1892: all-prefix affine approximation of the actual clean integer-row bank is checked, including row interiors, paid cleanup and frozen stopped tail. Native prefixes have error<=8W; real-time sampling error<=8W+4. Rescaling gives error(8W+4)/P and a9-interval affine cover, vanishing when W/P->0 and P->infinity. EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
NEW R1892 CHECKED RESULTS
1. ScheduledNativeIO.repeat_block_error / repeat_linear_error: if each
   length-N scheduled block has endpoint displacement D on a chosen head,
   for every starting state, then r repetitions at every n<=rN lie within
   N of floor(n/N)*D, and within N+|D| of nD/N. N>0 is explicit. The proof
   uses the existing unit-step displacement bound and scheduled append.
   It permits data-dependent motion inside a block. This is a geometry
   lemma; physical active execution is supplied separately by the actual
   bank's proved activity and native-prefix compilation, not assumed free.
   repeat_endpoint gives the exact displacementrD at the block boundary.

2. CoupledRowMotion proves actual seek/cell/row endpoint positions for
   arbitrary work states, independent of payload validity. RawRowArithmetic
   rows_endpoint and rows_linear_error then give bank drift at speed1/7,
   stationary-buffer approximation, and uniform error<=8W for every row
   loop prefix, using the SAME checked executor. W>0 is explicit.

3. ScheduledBankCleanup.schedule_position states the exact path of the
   paid erase/rewind passes. Buffer position is its two clipped W-step
   excursions and lies in[0,W]; bank rewind starts after2W local steps.
   It reuses erase_position, rewind_position and append_position.

4. RowBankCurve.curve(P,W,head,time) is zero for the local buffer and,
   for the bank, the outward clipped ramp of speed1/7 minus its final
   speed1 rewind starting at7P+2W. cover imports the existing clipped-ramp
   covers and their subtraction rule, giving9 affine-cover intervals,
   independent of row count/width. before/cleanup/after verify exact
   phase values. sample_stability bounds floor-time error by4, using
   the EXISTING clippedRamp_sample_error, itself based on mathlib's
   floor estimate and Lipschitz clipping. Constants are not optimized.

5. bank_curve_error covers EVERY n for the actual clean schedule run
   up to min(n,bankTicks): error<=8W relative to the starting position.
   It includes row interiors, both buffer cleanup passes, bank rewind
   and the frozen tail after the native stopping time. bank_endpoint
   proves head restoration even for arbitrary starting tape contents.
   bank_native_prefix_error transfers the bound to an actual original-TM
   stepN configuration for every n<=bankTicks, using native_prefix and
   bank_active. No halted state is counted as further paid execution.
   bank_real_curve_error has bound8W+4 for every real sampled time.

6. bank_scaled_cover / bank_scaled_error give a9-interval cover after
   scaling time and positions byP=rW, with error(8W+4)/P. PositiveP is
   explicit. bank_error_vanishes imports standard limit algebra to prove
   this error tends to0 wheneverP->infinity andW/P->0. The arithmetic
   bank's eventual row geometry can therefore use the existing physical
   affine obstruction once raw IO and bounded operation words are wired.

EXACT STATEMENTS AND DEPENDENCY MAP
BufferedSymbolMap.mapRule supplies an actual finite coupled-cell table for any f : Sym Bool -> Sym Bool. It preserves the finite carry, maps the bank cell, and clears the scratch cell. map_evaluate and map_rows identify its evaluator/list semantics; map_bankValue proves the exact value f(x j) in every valid window. All native execution, cleanup and frame facts come from BufferedRowUpdate and the existing shared buffered executor.
RawSymbolMap runs one such paid update per symbol with arbitrary public f(k). Its indexed_value theorem is the literal pointwise value f(j)(x j); represents holds from any clean bank state. Each padded update costs10, its advance1; the final rewind makes12P internal steps.
